At least quarterly, hospital leaders provide the governing entity with written reports on quality and patient safety that, at a minimum, include the following: • All system or process failures (See also QPS.02.00, ME 3) • The number and type of sentinel events • Whether the patients and the families were informed of the event • All actions taken to improve safety, both proactively and in response to actual occurrences • Follow-up of actions taken, when necessary
Hospital leaders regularly communicate information on quality improvement and the patient safety program to staff.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
group: Leadership for Quality and Patient Safety
statement: Hospital leaders collaborate to prioritize which hospitalwide processes will be measured, which hospitalwide improvement and patient safety activities will be implemented, and how success of these hospitalwide efforts will be measured.
elements: Hospital leaders use available data to set collective priorities for hospitalwide measurement and improvement activities and consider potential system improvements. (See also QPS.04.00, ME 1)
Hospital leaders set priorities for compliance with JCI’s International Patient Safety Goals.

Hospital leaders conduct a data-driven, risk-focused assessment of data annually for diagnostic errors that focuses on at least one of the following areas: • Radiology • Pathology • Laboratory/microbiology • Care coordination

Hospital leaders implement evidence-based interventions based on the diagnostic error risk assessment and data analysis with the intent to improve the diagnostic area(s) of focus and evaluate the effectiveness of the interventions on an ongoing basis, reevaluating when indicated.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Hospital leaders are accountable for reviewing, selecting, and monitoring clinical and nonclinical contracts and inspecting compliance with contracted services as needed.
elements: Hospital leaders identify an individua(s) with oversight responsibility for contracts to meet patient and management needs. (See also AOP.03.00, ME 3)
The hospital has a written description of the nature and scope of those services to be provided through contractual agreements.
Department/service leaders participate in the review, selection, and monitoring of clinical and nonclinical contracts. (See also ASC.01.00, ME 6)

Hospital leaders monitor compliance with contracted services and take actions to maintain continuity of services when contracts are renegotiated or terminated. (See also AOP.03.09, MEs 3 and 4; AOP.05.06, MEs 3 and 4)

All contracts stipulate the quality and performance data that are to be reported to the hospital, the reporting frequency and mechanism, and how the hospital will respond when quality requirements or expectations are not met. (See also AOP.03.09, MEs 3 and 4; AOP.05.06, MEs 3 and 4)
Quality data reported under contracts are integrated into the hospital’s quality monitoring program.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Hospital leaders ensure that health care practitioners and clinical staff not employed by the hospital have the right credentials and are competent and/or privileged for the services provided to the hospital’s patients.
elements: All diagnostic, consultative, and treatment services provided by independent health care practitioners outside the hospital are credentialed and privileged by the hospital to provide such services.

Independent health care practitioners who provide patient care services on the premises of the hospital but are not employees or members of the clinical staff are credentialed, privileged, and evaluated as required in SQE.05.00 through SQE.07.01.
Any support staff accompanying independent health care practitioners and providing care and services in the hospital are compliant with requirements for primary source verification.
The quality of services by independent practitioners outside the hospital is monitored as a component of the hospital’s quality improvement program.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Hospital leaders use data and information in resource decision-making to understand their implications on patient safety and quality.
elements: Hospital leaders use data and information when making decisions on purchasing, replacing, or retiring medical equipment. (See also FMS.07.00, ME 1)
Hospital leaders use data and information when making decisions on staffing needs to continuously support patient safety and quality.
Hospital leaders use the recommendations of professional organizations and other authoritative sources in making resource decisions. (See also GHI.04.00, MEs 1 and 2)
Hospital leaders monitor the results of their decisions and use the data to evaluate and improve the quality of their resource purchasing and allocation decisions.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Hospital leaders establish a supply chain strategy that protects patients and staff from unstable, contaminated, defective, and counterfeit supplies.
elements: Hospital leaders establish a written supply chain strategy that does the following: • Defines the steps in the supply chain • Identifies risk within the steps of the supply chain • Defines supplies at most risk • Outlines recommendations on mitigating risks that will ensure continuity of safe and high-

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
group: Direction of Hospital Departments and Services
statement: The hospital identifies the scope of services and structure of each department or service.
elements: Each department or service in the hospital is directed by an individual with the qualification, training, education, and experience comparable to the services provided. (See also AOP.03.01, ME 1; AOP.04.00, ME 1; AOP.05.01, ME 1; MMU.01.00, MEs 1 and 5; FMS.01.01, ME 1; HCT.01.00, ME 2; PCI.01.00, ME 1; QPS.01.00, ME 1; GHI.01.00, ME 3) The department head does the following: • Ensures that workflow and patient safety are not compromised during their absence • Ensures that the department functions are well managed through regular scheduled visits • Provides guidance as well as continuous assessment of the individual in charge of the department

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
group: Direction of Hospital Departments and Services
statement: Department/service leaders participate in hospitalwide improvement priorities and in monitoring and improving patient care specific to the department/service.
elements: Department/service leaders implement hospitalwide quality measures that relate to the services provided by their department or service, including any contracted services for which they are responsible. (See also FMS.02.00, ME 2)
Department/service leaders implement quality measures to reduce variation and improve processes in the department or service. (See also FMS.02.00, ME 3)
Department/service leaders select measures based on the need for improvement, and when improvement has been sustained, select a new measure. (See also QPS.04.00, ME 2)
When applicable, assessment of participation in quality activities and the results of measurement activities are included in the evaluation of the department’s staff.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
group: Direction of Hospital Departments and Services
statement: Department/service leaders select and implement clinical practice guidelines, clinical pathways, and clinical protocols when designing or improving processes.
elements: Annually, department/service leaders collectively determine at least five priority areas on which to focus the use of clinical practice guidelines.

Clinical practice guidelines, clinical pathways, and clinical protocols relevant to the hospital’s patient population and mission meet the following criteria: • Are selected from among those applicable to the hospital’s services and patients (mandatory

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Hospital leaders establish a framework for ethical management that promotes a culture of ethical practices and decision-making to ensure that patient care is provided within business, financial, ethical, and legal norms and protects patients and their rights.
elements: Hospital leaders establish a framework for the hospital’s ethical management that promotes the following: • A culture of ethical practices and decision-making to ensure the protection of patients and their

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Hospital leaders create and maintain a culture of safety and quality throughout the hospital.
elements: Hospital leaders establish and support an organizational culture that encourages reporting and discussion of opportunities for improving culture of safety in the organization.

Hospital leaders should establish a process to measure the culture of safety of the organization once per year. The feedback rate and results are analyzed, actions developed, and reported to the cluster quality committee.
Hospital leaders develop a code of conduct that identifies and corrects unacceptable behaviors as well as a process to resolve conflicts among staff and between staff and external customers.

Hospital leaders establish regularly scheduled education and provide resources (such as literature and advisories) relevant to the hospital’s culture of safety to all individuals who work in the hospital. (See also SQE.01.07, ME 3; SQE.07.00, ME 2)
Hospital leaders provide an accessible and confidential system for reporting issues relevant to a culture of safety in the hospital.

Hospital leaders implement a process to prevent retribution against individuals who report culture of safety issues and ensure that all reports are investigated within a defined time frame. (See also GLD.07.00, ME 1)
Hospital leaders identify and act on systems issues that lead health care practitioners to engage in unsafe behaviors.
Hospital leaders lead the daily safety huddles.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital implements a workplace violence prevention program to provide a safe and secure workplace.
elements: The workplace violence prevention program is led by a designated individual and developed by an interdisciplinary team.
The hospital develops and implements written policies and procedures to prevent and respond to workplace violence. (See also FMS.03.00, ME 1; FMS.04.00, ME 7; SQE.02.02, MEs 1 and 3)
The hospital implements a process to report incidents to analyze incidents and trends. (See also FMS.03.00, MEs 3 and 5; FMS.04.00, ME 9)
The hospital implements a process for follow-up and support to victims and witnesses affected by workplace violence, including trauma and psychological counseling, if necessary.
The hospital implements a process for the reporting of workplace violence incidents to the governing body. (See also SQE.02.02, ME 3)
Hospital leaders conduct periodic leadership walkarounds.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Health professional education, when provided within the hospital, is guided by the educational parameters defined by the sponsoring academic program and the hospital’s leaders.
elements: The hospital provides a mechanism(s) for oversight of the training program(s), including the following: • Obtains and accepts the parameters of the sponsoring academic program • Obtains the complete record of all students and trainees within the hospital • Understands and provides the level of supervision for all trainees • Integrates students and trainees into the hospital’s orientation, quality and patient safety,

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Human subjects research, when provided within the hospital, is guided by laws, regulations, and hospital leaders.
elements: Hospital leaders identify the official(s) responsible for developing and complying with human subjects research policies aligned with regulatory and professional requirements.

To help the patient determine whether to participate in research, investigation, or clinical trials, the hospital provides the patient with all the following information: • An explanation of the purpose and scope of the research • The expected duration of the patient’s participation • A clear description of the procedures to be followed • A statement of the potential benefits, risks, discomforts, and side effects • Alternative care, treatment, and services available to the patient that might prove advantageous

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Hospital leaders identify a qualified individual to oversee the hospital’s health information technology and processes.
elements: Hospital leaders provide support and resources for technology services in the hospital.
Hospital leaders identify a qualified individual to oversee technological systems and processes. (See also GLD.06.00, ME 1)
Hospital leaders and a qualified individual(s) participate in processes such as selection, testing, implementation, and evaluation of new and evolving health information technology systems.

New and evolving health information technology systems are monitored and evaluated for usability, effectiveness, intended use by staff, and patient safety, and improvements are identified and implemented based on results.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: When patient data and information are sent electronically, via mobile devices or other forms of electronic communication, the hospital implements processes to ensure quality of patient care, compliance with local laws and regulations, and maintenance of security and confidentiality of patient information.
elements: When patient data and information are transmitted through mobile text messaging or electronic communication tools, the hospital ensures that the process is through a secure platform and complies with the following: • Secure, encrypted sign-on processes for authentication of users (password protected and unique

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: For hospitals providing telehealth services, the hospital implements guidelines for the protection of patient data and information.
elements: The hospital implements written guidelines and processes to secure patient information when telehealth services are used.
The hospital establishes processes to ensure that patient information remains confidential when telehealth services are used.
The hospital establishes processes to ensure the integration of information when multiple touchpoints and platforms within the system are used.

All staff involved in providing telehealth services receive cybersecurity training and continuing education, and the training and ongoing education are documented. Training for staff accessing health information technology systems includes the following: • Device security • Access privileges • Password protection • Social engineering and phishing • Cybersecurity threats

All providers who render services via telehealth have privileges to do so and to use specified medical, surgical, and diagnostic equipment to provide telehealth services as applicable to their role and responsibilities.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: For hospitals using artificial intelligence clinical decision support tools, there are processes for selection, implementation, oversight, and improvement.
elements: The hospital identifies qualified individuals to select the relevant AI tools for their respective areas of expertise (for example, pharmacy, wound care, surgery).

The hospital establishes written guidelines and processes for oversight of the effectiveness of AI tools used by the hospital. These include the following: • Approval and implementation processes • Human practitioner involvement in final decision-making of patient care • Security and privacy of patient data (See also PCC.01.02, ME 1) • Identification of system discrepancies • Analysis from providers and relevant third-party sources • Updates to software/technology as deemed appropriate • Ethical considerations
The hospital tracks usage and trends on an ongoing basis and reports outcomes to the relevant parties (for example, key stakeholders, leadership team, third-party sources).

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital develops, maintains, and tests a program for response to planned and unplanned downtime of data systems.
elements: The hospital maintains, and tests for effectiveness at least annually, a written program for response to planned and unplanned downtime of data systems. The program is supported by procedures and forms to be used during planned and unplanned downtime. (See also FMS.08.00, ME 1; HCT.01.05, ME 1)
The hospital identifies the probable impact that planned and unplanned downtime of data systems will have on all aspects of care and services.

The program includes continuity strategies for the provision of ongoing safe, high-quality patient care and services, including services provided by outside vendors, during planned and unplanned downtime of data systems. The program supports documentation and reporting of patient information (for example, reporting of laboratory results) during the downtime.
The program identifies internal and, when applicable, external communication strategies for planned and unplanned downtime.

The hospital implements downtime recovery tactics and ongoing data backup processes to recover and maintain data and ensure data integrity and maintain confidentiality and security of patient information.
Staff are trained in the strategies, tactics, and procedures used for planned and unplanned downtime of data systems.
Downtime assessment report is generated and reviewed.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital develops and maintains processes and procedures for cybersecurity and cyber risk management.
elements: The hospital maintains, and tests at least annually, a written incident response program that includes the following: • Identifying the probable impact a cyberattack on data systems will have on all aspects of care and

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital establishes and implements a program for the safe use of lasers, electrosurgical, and other optical radiation devices used for performing procedures and treatments.
elements: The hospital’s written program for the safe use of lasers, electrosurgical, and other optical radiation devices meets the following criteria: • Is based on industry standards and professional guidelines and complies with applicable laws and

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital plans for managing information and selects processes to meet the needs of those who require data and information.
elements: The hospital selects processes to meet the information needs of the following: • Those who provide clinical services • The hospital’s leaders and department/service leaders (See also GLD.03.02, MEs 1 and 2) • Individuals, services, and agencies outside the hospital (See also GLD.03.01, ME 2) • Patients accessing personal data
The processes implemented are appropriate to the hospital’s size, complexity of services, availability of trained staff, technical resources, and other resources.

The needs assessment, planning, and designing of information management processes of the hospital involve both clinical and managerial staff. The process identifies the needs/requirements of external organizations (for example, Ministry of Health, accrediting bodies, national research and databases) and includes at least the following: • The hospital’s mission • The hospital’s scope of services provided • Complexity of care • Resources • Access to affordable technology • Usability and interoperability assessments • Support for effective communication among caregivers

Relevant clinical and managerial staff participate in selecting, integrating, and using information management technology, which is identified and integrated with existing information management processes. Adequate resources are provided for an effective information management system. (See also HCT.01.00)

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital maintains the confidentiality, security, privacy, and integrity of data and information through processes to manage and control access.
elements: The hospital implements processes, documented in policy, consistent with laws and regulations to ensure the confidentiality, security, and integrity of data and information, including medical records. (See also PCC.01.02, ME 1)

The hospital identifies, in writing, those authorized to access data and information, including those authorized to make entries in the patient medical record, and determines their level of access based on each individual’s role and responsibilities.

The hospital defines appropriate levels of security and confidentiality for data and information and has a process in place to grant authorized individuals access privileges to data and information in accordance with their level of access appropriate to confidentiality measures.

The hospital implements processes to ensure that different categories of data and information (that are restricted on a need-to-know basis) are accessed only by authorized individuals and in accordance with their level of access. (See also ACC.03.00, ME 2)

The hospital implements processes to ensure that only authorized individuals make entries in the patient medical record and in accordance with their level of access. Appropriate mechanisms for response to requests for access to information are established.
The hospital monitors compliance with the processes and release of information and acts when violations occur. Incidents related to confidentiality and security are reported and acted upon.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital maintains the confidentiality, security, privacy, and integrity of data and information through processes that protect against loss, theft, damage, destruction, ransomware, and other cyberattacks.
elements: The hospital conducts and documents an annual information security risk assessment throughout the organization, and data security risks are identified and prioritized from the risk assessment.

Data and information are stored in a manner that protects against loss, theft, damage, destruction, ransomware, and other cyberattacks through processes that include but are not limited to the following: • Process for regularly backing up and retrieving information system data • Process for protecting medical record from loss, theft, and deliberate alterations or destruction • Process for ensuring confidentiality, integrity, and security of medical records during storage

The hospital implements data security best practices to protect and secure data and information through processes that include but are not limited to the following: • Safeguarding data and information against loss, destruction, tampering, damage, and

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital determines the retention time of patient medical records, data, and other information.
elements: The hospital determines the retention time of patient medical records and other data and information and complies with laws and regulations.

The retention process of medical records takes into account at least the following: • The medical records are retained for a minimum of five years after the patient was last seen unless otherwise specified by laws and regulations. For minors, records shall be kept until they are 18 years of age, and then for a minimum additional five years. • The process addresses the retention period of different types of the medical records as well as the permanent types (for example, records of medical-legal cases). • The process addresses the retention period of different parts of the medical record as well as the permanent parts (master patient index, admission and discharge dates, name of the most responsible physician, diseases treated, operations performed, and a discharge summary for each admission).
The retention process provides expected confidentiality and security.
Patient medical records, data, and other information are destroyed or deleted in a manner that does not compromise confidentiality and security and renders the information unreadable.
When the hospital discontinues operation, it stores the medical records in a facility offering retrieval services for the specified retention periods. Patients or their representatives are informed.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Clinical staff, decision-makers, and other staff members are educated and trained on information systems, information security, and the principles of data and information use and management.
elements: Clinical staff, decision-makers, and others are provided education and training on information systems, information security, and the principles of data and information use and management, as appropriate to their role and responsibilities. The education and training include, but are not limited to, the following: • Selection and use of indicators (measures) in assessing and improving work processes • Data collection and analysis • Use of data and information for decision-making • Data and information confidentiality and security

Staff who use an electronic health record system receive education, ongoing training, and assessment to ensure that they can effectively and efficiently use the system to carry out their job responsibilities.
Staff receive education and ongoing, annual training related to cybersecurity based on their roles and responsibilities.
Clinical and managerial data and information are integrated as needed to support decision-making.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital maintains an effective information management system to serve its internal and external users and stakeholders.
elements: The hospital categorizes the needed information into either manual or computerized.
Data elements are defined, and forms are developed for designated staff to enter the necessary data.
Data are collected within predetermined time frames and frequency.
The hospital has a process for securely storing data and information with easy retrieval.
Data and information are accurately and timely disseminated to the targeted internal and external users.
When data are shared between health care providers, it is shared using the National Platform for Health Insurance Exchange Services (NPHIES) platform.
Data and information are disseminated in a format useful for decision-making.
The hospital has a process for documenting, approving, and validating any modification or update related to the information management system.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: There is a process for clinical and administrative staff to obtain information that supports safe patient care.
elements: Information resources are available to address clinical and administrative staff needs and support them to maintain and improve their competencies.

Information resources support patient care, patient safety, patient education, performance improvement, educational functions for hospital and medical staff, research, and other appropriate functions.
Information resources (for example, books, journals) are accessible when needed.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Documents, including policies, procedures, and programs, are managed in a consistent and uniform manner.
elements: The hospital has a written guidance document that defines the requirements for reviewing policies and procedures, including the following: • Review and approval of all documents by an authorized person before issue • Frequency of review and continued approval of documents (every two to three years or when

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Leaders review, approve, and manage implementation of policies and procedures that guide and support patient care and services.
elements: Required policies, procedures, and plans are available, and staff understand how to access those documents relevant to their responsibilities.
Staff are trained and understand those documents relevant to their responsibilities.
The requirements of the policies, procedures, and plans are fully implemented and evident in the actions of individual staff members.
The implementation of policies, procedures, and plans is monitored, and the information supports full implementation.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital uses standardized diagnosis and procedure codes and ensures the uniform use of approved symbols and abbreviations across the hospital.
elements: The hospital uses standardized diagnosis codes and procedure codes. For diagnosis coding, the hospital uses the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th Revision, Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM), and for procedure coding, Australian Classification of Health Interventions (ACHI).
The hospital implements the uniform use of approved symbols and identifies those not to be used.
The hospital implements the uniform use of approved definitions.

If the hospital allows abbreviations, it meets the following criteria: • The hospital implements a uniform use of approved abbreviations with only one meaning. • The hospital implements a do-not-use list of abbreviations. • The hospital does not use abbreviations on informed consents, patient rights documents,

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital retrieves, disseminates, and transmits health information on a timely basis in a format that meets user expectations, and with the desired frequency.
elements: Data and information dissemination meets the needs of individuals and programs within and outside the hospital that provide patient care, treatment, and services.
The hospital disseminates data and information in useful formats within time frames that are defined by the hospital and consistent with laws and regulations.
Staff providing patient care have access to the data and information needed to carry out their job responsibilities and provide patient care safely and effectively.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital initiates and maintains a standardized, accurate medical record for every patient assessed or treated and determines the record’s content, format, and location of entries.
elements: The hospital initiates a medical record for each patient on their first contact with the hospital, whether it is for an admission, emergency department, or outpatient clinic visit.
The patient medical record contains the following: • At least two unique identifiers for each page or item (See also IPSG.01.00, ME 1) • Author of each entry • Date of each entry • Time of each entry
The hospital ensures that there is only one medical record for each patient.

The hospital has a process to ensure complete and accurate medical records by adopting measures including but not limited to the following: • A policy identifies all staff members authorized to make entries in medical records. • All entries in the medical records must be legible, indelibly verified, dated, and authenticated. • Clinical staff authorized to make entries in the medical record receive formal training in clinical documentation improvement per the national/international guidelines. • The author of each entry must be identified and authenticated by official stamp, signature, written initials, or computer entry. • The medical record must be completed within 30 days of patient discharge and before any elective vacation or period of absence of the staff member entering the notes in the medical record. • The hospital has a policy to deal with delinquent medical records. • The most responsible physician must complete their medical records.

The hospital determines and standardizes the specific content, format, and location of entries for patient medical records according to the needs of health care professionals, including those related to telehealth. The hospital controls the process through a structure (for example, a forms committee, the medical records review committee).

The hospital implements a process on the proper use of copy-and-paste, autofill, autocorrect, and templates and provides education and training on the process to all staff who document in the electronic medical record.

The hospital implements processes to facilitate accurate and complete documentation in patient medical records, including ensuring that the medical record contains sufficient information to identify the patient and their care provider, support the diagnosis, justify the treatment, and document the results of care provided. (See also HCT.01.01, ME 3)
The hospital has processes for how entries are corrected, overwritten, reviewed, and authenticated.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: As part of its monitoring and performance improvement activities, the hospital regularly assesses patient medical record content.
elements: A representative sample of medical records that includes active and discharged medical records in all service areas is reviewed at least quarterly or more frequently as determined by law and regulation.
The review is conducted by physicians, nurses, and others authorized to manage or make entries in patient medical records.
The review focuses on the timeliness, accuracy, completeness, and legibility of the medical record.
Medical record content required by law or regulation is included in the review process.
The results of the review process are incorporated into the hospital’s quality oversight mechanism by analyzing data and taking corrective actions.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The health information management (medical records) department has adequate qualified staff.
elements: The health information management (medical records) department is directed by an individual qualified by education (bachelor’s degree in health information management) and experience.
The department director is credentialed in health information management through formal training per the national/international guidelines.
The department has adequate staff to carry out its functions.
Staff working in the department are credentialed in health information management through formal training per the national/international guidelines.
Clinical coding staff working in the department are credentialed/certified in clinical coding through formal training per the national/international guidelines.
The department has one or more staff members who are credentialed in clinical documentation improvement (CDI) through formal training per the national/international guidelines.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital maintains a master patient index (either manual or computerized) of all patients who have ever been admitted to or treated by the hospital.
elements: The master patient index is used to identify a patient’s medical record number.

The master patient index provides basic patient demographic information (identification information collected during registration) as well as patient activity (visit) information: • The patient demographic information (identification information) includes medical record number, patient’s full name, date of birth, sex, marital status, address, national identification number, next of kin (and their contacts) and/or a person that the patient wishes to be contacted in an emergency, or authorized representative/designee. • The patient activity (visit) information includes admission and discharge/transfer dates for inpatient hospitalizations, date of death when a death occurs, encounter date or date of service for outpatient visits, most responsible physician, and mother’s name for newborns.
The patient demographic information (identification information) of the master patient index is recorded on the front sheet of the medical record.
The master patient index is updated for each new episode of care for any change in information.
The master patient index is retained permanently to provide historical access to basic patient information and dates of stay in the hospital.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital maintains the medical records in one central place.
elements: The hospital has a medical records department that accommodates all medical records.

The hospital has processes to manage the different parts of the medical records. • The different parts of multiple records are cross-referenced to the patient’s unique identifier to enable records linkage. • The different parts can be easily located when not stored together. • The hospital ensures that all information is available and accessible when needed.

The processes include, but are not limited to, the following: • Records that are partly paper-based and partly electronic • Records that include items requiring incompatible storage systems such as videos and audio

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital has a process to ensure availability of the medical records in a timely manner.
elements: The hospital determines in a policy all disciplines that may have access to the medical records.
Care providers have access to current and past medical records.
Medical records are readily retrievable for each patient encounter.
Medical records are available within 30 minutes of being requested.
Medical records can be retrieved any time of the day.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Medical records are consistently organized.
elements: Individual medical records are securely compiled.
Medical records are organized into sections (for example, a section for test results, operative reports, consultations, discharge summary).

The different sections of the medical record are organized chronologically (for example, the physician orders start with the initial set written when the patient was admitted to the hospital and end with the discharge order).

During each hospitalization episode, both inpatient and outpatient medical records are separated into different sections in the patient’s medical record (for example, for doctors’ orders, nursing notes, progress notes).

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital has a system to manage voluminous medical records.
elements: The hospital has a system that enables medical record linkage.
When the medical record is divided into volumes, the number of each volume should be clearly visible on the folder and on the sign-out slip (for example, Volume 1 of 2, Volume 2 of 2).

When the hospital practices thinning of voluminous medical records: • The hospital develops thinning guidelines that remain consistent for the type of documentation contained. • The hospital retains documentation in the medical record that reflects the current plan of care and services provided. • The hospital removes parts of the medical record older than a certain date and moves them into a secondary record (the overflow record).

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital develops and implements a policy for releasing medical records from the medical records department.
elements: The hospital has a policy that describes the process for releasing medical records for patient care encounters (inpatient, outpatient, and emergency department).

The hospital determines when to release medical records for reasons not related to direct patient care (for example, research, utilization management, quality improvement, morbidity and mortality, government requests).
The hospital has an approval mechanism for releasing medical records for reasons not related to patient care. The approval mechanism is implemented.
The hospital defines a time frame for responding to requests related to the release of medical records and monitors compliance.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital has a system for tracking medical records.
elements: The hospital has a medical records tracking system to identify the location of any record not in the medical records department and its date and time of movement as well as subsequent movements, when applicable.
The medical records tracking system includes all components of the medical records.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: A qualified individual(s) guides the implementation of the hospital’s infection prevention and control program and oversees the activities needed to carry out the program throughout the hospital.
elements: One or more individuals qualified by education, training and experience oversee the infection prevention and control program and ensure that the program complies with local and national laws and regulations and applicable infection control guidelines, including the following: • Demonstrated understanding of infection prevention and control principles and patient safety

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital coordinates infection prevention and control activities across all departments and services.
elements: There is a formal interdisciplinary coordination mechanism, such as a committee for the infection prevention and control program that involves infection prevention and control professionals. The committee is chaired by the hospital director or the medical director.

All departments and services of the hospital are included in the infection prevention and control program, including representatives from the medical staff, nursing staff, microbiology, operating room, central sterilization service, pharmaceutical care, dietary services, housekeeping, infection prevention and control staff, and other departments as needed. (See also FMS.03.00, ME 1)

The function and activities of the coordination mechanism are documented and include but are not limited to the following: • Review of the hospital infection prevention and control policies and procedures • Review of the reports of health care–associated infections surveillance submitted regularly by the

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Hospital leaders provide resources to support the infection prevention and control program.
elements: Hospital leaders approve staffing levels and provide staff for the infection prevention and control program according to the hospital’s size, complexity of activities, level of risks, and the program’s scope.

Hospital leaders ensure that the infection prevention and control program receives the resources, such as equipment and supplies, required to meet its goals and responsibilities. When some infection prevention and control functions are outsourced (for example, sterilization, laundry), the hospital provides oversight and management of the contract. (See also GLD.05.00)
Information management systems support the infection prevention and control program. Goals of the Infection Prevention and Control Program

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital uses a risk-based, data-driven method to establish priorities, implement interventions, and monitor the effectiveness of the health care–associated infection prevention and control program.
elements: The hospital completes and documents an infection prevention and control risk assessment to establish the priorities of the health care–associated infection program through data collection and analysis at least annually, and when necessary for specific events, and it includes, at a minimum, the following: • Respiratory tract infections • Urinary tract infections • Intravascular invasive devices • Surgical sites • Multidrug-resistant organisms • Epidemiologically significant infections • Emerging or reemerging infections within the community

The hospital identifies and implements evidence-based interventions to address infection risks identified in the risk assessment, and it includes, at a minimum, adoption and implementation of the following: • Care bundle for prevention of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) consistent with recognized

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The laboratory implements a process to reduce the risks of infection resulting from exposure to infectious diseases and biohazardous materials and waste.
elements: The laboratory implements written policies and procedures to reduce the risks of infection. The laboratory has a system for monitoring the laboratory safety and infection control program through documented safety and infection control audits (conducted at least twice yearly), reporting of the findings of the to the laboratory director, the facility safety officer, the infection control department, and other concerned parties, and taking and documenting corrective actions, whenever needed.
The hospital reports infections acquired in the laboratory as defined in the policy and compliance with laws and regulations.

The laboratory follows biosafety and infection control rules for relevant practices: • Exposures to aerosols and droplets are controlled. • Laboratory coats, gowns, or uniforms are worn. • Biosafety cabinets are used when required by laws and regulations, or manufacturer’s guidelines. • Procedures explain how to handle accidents and injuries, including decontamination procedures, emergency treatment procedures, and the location and use of safety equipment, including provision of safety equipment (eye wash, emergency shower, fire extinguisher, fire blanket,

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital reduces the risk of infections associated with medical/surgical equipment, devices, and supplies by proper cleaning, disinfection, sterilization, and storage.
elements: The hospital provides central sterilization services and implements proper infection prevention and control practices when cleaning and performing low-level and intermediate-level disinfection of noncritical medical equipment, devices, and supplies that address the following: • Practices of transportation, cleansing, decontamination, disinfection, sterilization, storage, and recall of sterile items guided by policies and procedures consistent with scientific guidelines and

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital implements a process for managing the reuse of single-use devices in accordance with the manufacturer’s requirements and any applicable laws and regulations.
elements: The hospital identifies, in writing, single-use devices and materials that may be reused in accordance with local and national laws and regulations. Justification of reprocessing is provided by the head(s) of the concerned department(s). The reuse of single-use devices is managed through a policy, approved by the infection prevention and control committee and hospital director, that defines the following: (See also GHI.04.00, ME 4) • The items that can be reused • Patients and conditions for reuse of single-use items • Measures taken to ensure safety and integrity, including testing and maintenance by biomedical

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital implements a process for managing expired and damaged devices and supplies.
elements: The hospital implements a process to manage expired supplies.
The hospital implements a process to manage damaged supplies.
The hospital stores supplies in a manner that prevents contamination or damage and under environmental conditions recommended by the manufacturer when applicable.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The infection prevention and control program provides oversight for the cleaning and disinfection of the environment.
elements: The infection prevention and control program implements evidence-based cleaning and disinfection guidelines and procedures (for example, housekeeping policies) throughout the hospital that describe the areas to be cleaned, the schedule for cleaning, and the procedures for cleaning different environmental surfaces. Policies and procedures, schedules, and agents utilized are reviewed by infection prevention and control staff. (See also MMU.05.00, ME 2)

Evidence-based guidelines direct cleaning and disinfection procedures in high-risk areas as indicated by evidence-based cleaning and disinfection standards. The guidelines include but are not limited to the following: • All units have a cleaning/disinfection schedule which lists all environmental surfaces to be cleaned. • The hospital environment, lockers, and cabinets are clean. • Food is stored under sanitary conditions and consumed in designated places. • Food refrigerators are clean and used only for food storage. • There are separate clean and dirty utility areas in each patient care area. • There are policies and procedures on pest control that address the regular schedule for pest control, chemical list, and time and place of exposure. • Routine environmental microbiological cultures are not performed unless recommended by the

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The infection prevention and control program follows evidence-based guidelines related to cleaning and disinfection of laundry, linens, and scrub attire provided by the hospital.
elements: Laundering methods comply with local and national laws and regulations and follow guidelines from recognized infection control agencies. The methods are guided by policies and procedures on linen management that cover all steps starting from collecting linen from patients’ rooms until completion of the cleaning process.

Standard precautions are used when handling laundry, linens, and hospital-issued scrub attire, and appropriate transmission-based precautions are used as indicated by infection risk. Measures adopted by the hospital include but are not limited to the following: • Hand-washing facilities are in all areas where un-bagged linen is handled. • Soiled linen (contaminated with patient’s blood, excreta, or other body fluids) and linen from patients under isolation precautions are contained and transported in accordance with current professional standards. • Soiled linen must be handled as little as possible and with minimal agitation. • Appropriate barriers (gloves, gowns, and masks) should be used when handling soiled linen. • Linen is bagged at the location where it is used and not stored or pre-rinsed in patient care areas. • Linen is put into special color-coded and waterproof laundry bags.

Laundry, linens, and hospital-issued scrub attire are transported, processed, and stored in a manner that prevents cross-contamination of soiled and clean items. Measures adopted by the hospital include but are not limited to the following: • Clean linen is transported, handled, and stored in a way that protects it from contamination and dust. • Clean and used linen are separated during storage and transport. • Linen carts for clean and used linen are clearly identified. • Loose (un-bagged) linen is not put down a laundry chute.

Staff wear clean, hospital-issued scrub attire in critical areas identified by the hospital, in accordance with applicable infection control, national health care industry standards, and hospital policy.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital implements processes for proper disposal of waste, proper management of human tissues, and safe handling and disposal of sharps and needles.
elements: The hospital implements practices to reduce the risk of infection from handling and disposal of infectious waste, blood and blood components, body fluids, and body tissues. The measures include but are not limited to the following: • There is a policy and procedure for safe disposal of medical waste. • Medical waste is disposed of by a specialized company and includes all types of medical waste. • Medical waste segregation, collection, and storing are done per applicable laws and regulations. • Yellow bags are used for all non-sharp disposable materials contaminated with patient blood and/ or body fluids. • Yellow bags are distributed in the hospital in sufficient number and locations. • Red bags are used for tissues, body parts, and amputated parts to be saved and then collected by the municipality to be buried. • Medical waste containers are cleaned and maintained regularly. • Hazard signs are fixed on all medical waste containers. • Medical waste collection points are cleaned and maintained regularly. • Medical waste collection points are cleaned and maintained regularly. • Staff working in medical disposal are well trained and vaccinated against blood-borne pathogens.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital reduces the risk of infections associated with exposure to blood, body fluids, and other potentially infectious materials.
elements: The hospital identifies processes that could result in patient or staff exposure to blood and body fluids.

The hospital implements structures (for example, staff health clinic) and practices to reduce the risk of exposure to blood and body fluids. The structure and practices include pre-employment counseling and medical services related to screening, immunization, and post exposure management, addressed through policies and procedures consistent with laws and regulations and recommendations of professional organizations.
The hospital uses an expeditious, timely process for reporting patient, staff, and visitor exposures to blood and body fluids and needle pricks and sharps injuries.
The hospital uses a process for acting on patient, staff, and visitor exposures to blood and body fluids.

Staff are educated in how to report an exposure incident, including exposure to open pulmonary tuberculosis and vaccine-preventable viruses (chickenpox, measles, mumps, and rubella). Follow-up and management of exposure processes are implemented.
The hospital, through its infection prevention and control team, tracks and monitors patient and staff exposures to blood and body fluids and takes corrective actions to prevent recurrence.

Reports of exposure incidents are reviewed, and actions are taken to minimize the risk of future exposures to blood and body fluids. The screening, immunization, and post exposure management data are kept in staff medical records.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital reduces the risk of infections associated with the operations of food and dietetics services.
elements: The hospital stores food and nutrition products in a manner that reduces the risk of infection, including those stored outside of the kitchen and food preparation areas. Measures adopted include but are not limited to the following: • Kitchen design supports its function. • Refrigerator temperatures are checked daily and documented on log sheets. • The kitchen environment and functions are addressed in policies and procedures that are reviewed by the infection prevention and control team. • Kitchen environment is clean.

The hospital adopts and implements kitchen sanitation measures and guidelines for preparation areas to prevent cross-contamination and infection. Measures include but are not limited to the following: • Kitchen areas are separated based on assigned function (separate areas for vegetables, meat, dessert preparation, and so on). • Adequate number of hand-washing facilities are present in each area. • Food containers are properly labeled and expiry dates noted. • Food is protected from environment during storage, preparation, display, and transportation. • Garbage containers or receptacles are adequate in number, insect and rodent proof, and covered. • Boards used to cut meat, poultry, chicken, or vegetables are identifiably separated and immediately washed after use. • Fruits and vegetables are washed and disinfected thoroughly. • Food containers are washed immediately after being emptied from food. • There are policies and procedures that address staff hygiene and health in the kitchen and are reviewed by the infection prevention and control team. • While handling food, staff wash their hands, cover their hair, and wear gloves. • Personnel with respiratory infections or gastroenteritis are restricted from handling food. • Stool tests and cultures are performed routinely upon hiring, every six months, and after returning from vacation. • Results of stool analysis and cultures are reviewed by the infection prevention and control practitioner.
The hospital prepares food and nutrition products using proper sanitation and temperature. Food delivery to the receiving area must be checked for quality and temperature.
The hospital uses a process to ensure that proper food temperature is maintained during preparation, transportation, and distribution.
Professional guidelines are adopted for nutritional products with special storage and preparation requirements, such as human milk, baby formula, and other enteral products.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital protects patients, visitors, and staff from transmission of infections and communicable diseases.
elements: The hospital uses a process, guided by policies and procedures, to isolate patients with infectious diseases, and staff use transmission-based precautions in accordance with recommended guidelines. The policies and procedures address separating patients with communicable diseases and those who are colonized or infected with epidemiologically important organisms from other patients, staff, and visitors. (See also FMS.09.01, ME 1)

The policies and procedures also address the transfer of patients outbound or inbound to secure the prevention of spread of methicillin-resistant staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) or other epidemiologically significant organisms. All patients for transfer outbound known to have MRSA or other epidemiologically significant organisms must be reported upon requesting the transfer with the supporting document. All patients transferred to the hospital must be kept under contact transmission-based precaution unless proving otherwise.
The hospital protects immunocompromised or otherwise vulnerable patients through isolation or reverse/protective isolation in accordance with recommended guidelines. (See also PCC.01.04, ME 4)

The hospital routinely monitors and makes available negative pressure rooms for infectious patients who require isolation for airborne infections. Measures for negative pressure rooms include but are not limited to the following: • There is at least one negative pressure airborne isolation room in the emergency department and one in patient care areas (one negative pressure room for every 25 to 30 beds in general hospitals). • The infection prevention and control team decides the need for more airborne isolation rooms, depending on the volume of patients in need for airborne isolation admitted to the hospital. • The ventilation system serving airborne isolation facilities provides pressure patterns that prevent airborne pathogens from being distributed to other areas of the hospital. Rooms designed for airborne isolation patients are under negative pressure, air is exhausted to the outside and not recirculated unless filtered through a high-efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filter, and the negative pressure for the isolation room is validated daily when a patient is isolated (admitted in the room). Weekly validation is done when the room has no patients. A minimum of 12 air changes per hour should be maintained by testing and documentation per manufacturer’s recommendation/hospital policy. • The entry of the isolation room is through a work area or ante-room that serves as a site for hand washing, gowning, and storage of protective clothing (gloves, aprons, masks). • Toilet, shower or tub, and hand-washing facilities are provided for each isolation room. • Transmission-based precaution cards (isolation signs) are consistent with the patient’s diagnosis, are posted in Arabic and English, and indicate the type of precautions required. • Transmission-based precaution cards (isolation signs) are color coded for isolation of different categories (for example, contact is green, airborne is blue, droplet is pink or red). • Transmission-based precaution cards (isolation signs) have short statements supported with the required figures. • Isolation instructions highlight the transmission-based precaution cards (isolation signs) needed while transporting patients under transmission-based precautions to another department (for example, radiology). • Staff wear respirator (high-filtration) masks (N-95, N-99) during direct care of patients on airborne precautions; these masks are available on all units likely to admit patients on airborne precautions. • Respirator (high-filtration) masks (N95, N-99) can be reused by the same patient caregiver per the period specified by the manufacturer.
The hospital implements a process to manage patients with airborne infections when negative air pressure rooms are not available, including adding temporary negative pressure rooms.
Staff are educated in managing infectious patients when there is a sudden influx or when negative pressure rooms are not available.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital provides resources and equipment to protect staff, health care practitioners, patients, and visitors from biological, physical, and chemical hazards, and these are readily available for use.
elements: The hospital identifies situations in which personal protective equipment is required.

The hospital ensures that appropriate personal protective equipment (gown, gloves, masks, and protective eyewear) and hand hygiene agents are readily available when needed. Policies and procedures are available on the appropriate use of gloves, gowns, facemasks, protective eyewear, and high-filtration respirator masks (N-95, N-99). (See also IPSG.05.00, MEs 1 and 2; FMS.09.01, ME 1)
Staff are trained and correctly use personal protective equipment in each identified situation.
The hospital implements environmental disinfecting procedures for areas and situations in the hospital identified as at risk for infection transmission.

Liquid soap and running water, hand disinfectants, and single-use towels are provided where handwashing and hand-disinfecting procedures are required, and hand air dryers are not used in patient care areas. (See also IPSG.05.00, MEs 1 and 2)

Patients and visitors are educated on when to disinfect their hands, when transmission-based precautions such as isolation precautions must be followed, and how to use personal protective equipment when applicable. (See also IPSG.05.00, MEs 1 and 2)

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital implements processes to support preparedness for epidemiologically significant infectious diseases or special pathogens.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The infection prevention and control process is integrated with the hospital’s overall program for quality and patient safety, using data and measures that are epidemiologically important to the hospital.
elements: The hospital integrates infection prevention and control activities into the quality and patient safety program. (See also GLD.04.00, ME 1; QPS.01.00, ME 1)

The hospital collects and analyzes data for infection prevention and control activities, including epidemiologically important infections. Data collection process takes into account at least the following: • The hospital selects indicators based on the projected use of data (internal and external benchmarking). • The hospital defines the data collection methods and sources (for example, hospital information system, verbal and written communication, medical record review, direct observation, and review of clinical indicators). • There are policies and procedures that define the types of surveillance for health care–associated infections. • There are written standardized definitions for identifying health care–associated infections. • The policies and procedures define how data will be collected, analyzed, and used. • The monitoring process includes using indicators related to infection issues that are epidemiologically important to the hospital.
The hospital uses monitoring data to evaluate and support improvements to the infection prevention and control program at least annually. (See also GLD.04.00, ME 4)
Monitoring data include internal and external benchmarking infection rates as applicable.
The infection prevention and control program documents monitoring data and provides reports of data analysis to leaders on a quarterly basis.

The hospital uses risk, rate, and trend information to design or modify processes to reduce health care–associated infections to the lowest possible level and makes the necessary improvements for the identified epidemiologically important infections, processes, and devices associated with the risk of health care–associated infections.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital provides education on infection prevention and control practices to staff, health care practitioners, patients, families, and others when indicated by their role in the hospital.
elements: The hospital provides initial education about infection prevention and control to all staff and health care practitioners at orientation when they begin work in the hospital. Education and training records are maintained in staff files. (See also SQE.02.00, ME 2; SQE.02.01, ME 5)

The hospital provides ongoing education and training to all staff related to the hospital’s infection prevention and control program and emerging trends in infection prevention and control; hospitalwide policies, procedures, and practices of the infection prevention and control program; and departmental policies, procedures, and practices of the infection prevention and control program based on the service provided at least annually. (See also SQE.02.01, ME 1)
The hospital provides education about infection prevention and control to patients, families, and other caregivers as appropriate.
The hospital regularly communicates findings and trends from the infection prevention and control program activities to all staff, physicians, and management.
The hospital communicates information and data from the infection prevention and control program to leaders and the governing body.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
group: Management of Quality and Patient Safety Activities
statement: A qualified individual(s) guides the implementation of the hospital’s program for quality and patient safety, and manages the activities needed to carry out an effective program of continuous quality improvement and patient safety within the hospital.
elements: Hospital leaders select a qualified individual(s) who is experienced in the methods and processes of improvement to lead the implementation of the hospital’s quality and patient safety program. (See also GLD.06.00, ME 1; GLD.04.00, ME 3; PCI.08.00, ME 1) This includes the following: • A quality management director, qualified by education, training, and experience in quality, is responsible for directing all aspects of the quality management program, and reports to the hospital leadership. • A multidisciplinary quality improvement committee has members from the leadership group (the hospital director, medical director, nursing director, quality management director) and other members/invitees as appropriate. • The quality improvement committee coordinating and overseeing the quality improvement program throughout the hospital is responsible for developing, implementing, and evaluating the quality improvement program; approving all quality improvement initiatives; and receiving quality reports and providing feedback to relevant stakeholders. • The quality improvement committee meets regularly and maintains appropriate documentation of its activities.
The individual(s) leading the quality and patient safety program selects and supervises qualified staff for the program.

The quality and patient safety program provides support and coordination to department/ service leaders for like measures (for example, on developing and using indicators to evaluate and improve performance) across the hospital and for the hospital’s priorities for improvement. (See also GLD.04.00, ME 1; QPS.03.03, ME 1)

The quality and patient safety program implements a training program (formally or through orientation and mentoring) by qualified professionals for all staff on continuous quality improvement that is consistent with staff members’ roles in the quality and patient safety program. Training on quality improvement includes the use of quality improvement methodologies and tools (for example, Plan-Do-Check-Act [PDCA], Lean Six Sigma, cause-and-effect analysis, process map, Pareto chart, brainstorming). Training also includes learning fundamental data competencies such as accurate data collection, interpretation of key performance indicators, basic data analysis, and use of data to monitor trends, evaluate outcomes, and support improvement initiatives.
The quality and patient safety program is responsible for regularly communicating ongoing performance, results of data analysis, and results of quality improvement efforts to all staff.
The hospital defines the qualifications for its quality and patient safety program leaders and its staff.
Quality improvement teams are selected by the service leaders, and these teams use quality tools to improve processes.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
group: Management of Quality and Patient Safety Activities
statement: Hospital leaders support a hospitalwide continuous quality improvement program.
elements: Hospital leaders provide resources required for the continuous quality improvement program, including human, financial, and time resources.
Hospital leaders actively participate in quality improvement activities, including improvement teams.
Hospital leaders support staff to make and participate in quality improvement initiatives and to attend quality improvement educational activities.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The quality and patient safety program staff support the quality indicator and measure selection process and provide coordination and integration of measurement activities throughout the hospital.
elements: The quality and patient safety program integrates and supports the selection of clinical and managerial performance measures and indicators throughout the hospital, at the hospitalwide level and at the department or service level. Clinical indicators are referenced to current evidence-based practice whenever applicable. Indicator selection is such that they represent key care and service structures, processes, and outcomes based on the mission and scope of services. Measures and indicators that the hospital uses may include, but are not limited to, the following: Structure • Availability of essential supplies and equipment • Availability of medical records • Availability of blood and blood products • Availability of emergency medications • Vacancy rates in all departments • Surgical volumes • Staffing ratios Process • The timing and use of antibiotics prior to surgery • Blood and blood products administration • Documentation in medical records • Delay of physicians answering nurses’ phone calls and pages • Waiting times for treatment • Venous thrombo-embolism prophylaxis for surgical patients • Neuropathy testing in diabetic patients Outcome • Mortality rates • Health care–associated infections • Staff satisfaction • Patient satisfaction • Unplanned return to the operating room • Return to the emergency department within 24 hours • Unplanned transfer to the critical care unit • Resuscitation of patients (cardiac/respiratory arrest) • Readmission to the hospital within 30 days of discharge • Various adverse events (for example, falls, injuries, pressure ulcers) • Medication errors • Sentinel events • Patient complaints • Length of stay • Patient-reported outcome measure (PROM)
For each indicator, there is a clear definition, sample size, data collection method, frequency, analysis, and expression (for example, a ratio, with defined numerator and denominator).

The quality and patient safety program coordinates and integrates all department and service- specific measurement activities throughout the hospital, including information developed from risk management activities integrated and coordinated with the quality improvement and patient safety activities. (See also GLD.04.00, ME 2)

The quality and patient safety program integrates patient safety activities and event reporting systems, risk management, safety culture measures, quality indicators, and other measures to facilitate integrated solutions and improvements. (See also GLD.04.01, ME 2)
The quality and patient safety program tracks the progress on the planned collection of measure data and quality indicators for the selected priorities.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital develops a quality improvement program that provides a structured framework for monitoring and improving performance as well as supporting innovation.
elements: The quality improvement program covers processes of care involving high-risk, high-volume, problem-prone, and high-cost areas.
The quality improvement program is in line with the hospital strategic plan.
The quality improvement program is based on a documented quality improvement plan that is revised at least annually, with defined scope, goals, and objectives.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital develops and maintains a patient safety program.
elements: Hospital leaders adopt a just culture that promotes both professional accountability and reporting of adverse events/near misses.
Hospital leaders establish a multidisciplinary patient safety committee (can be integrated with quality improvement committee) to provide direction and oversight of the patient safety program.
Hospital leaders conduct patient safety culture assessment at least once annually. Data are analyzed and improvements are made accordingly.
Hospital leaders conduct regular leadership patient safety rounds in patient care services to encourage reporting of incidents/near misses and to identify potential risks and hazards.

The hospital adopts safe practices that have been proven to improve patient safety and reduce harm to patients such as those from the World Health Organization (WHO) and other national and international organizations concerned with patient safety.
The hospital provides equipment/devices with technological features proven to reduce errors and improve safety.
Patient safety activities and their results are communicated to the staff and other relevant groups and used as the basis for improving the hospital’s processes.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
group: Analysis and Validation of Measurement Data
statement: The quality and patient safety program includes the collection, aggregation, and analysis of data to support patient care, treatment, and services; hospital management; the continuous quality improvement program; and participation in external databases.
elements: The quality and patient safety program has a process to aggregate data from multiple qualitative and quantitative sources on a regular basis.

Aggregate data (structure, process, and outcome indicators) and information support patient care, treatment, and services; hospital management; professional practice review; other performance monitoring activities (for example, patient safety, risk management); and the overall quality and patient safety program. (See also PCC.02.02, ME 2; QPS.03.02, ME 1)
The hospital provides aggregate data and information to agencies outside the hospital when required by laws and regulations.
The hospital implements a process to contribute to and learn from external databases for comparison purposes.
The hospital maintains security and confidentiality when contributing to or using external databases.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
group: Analysis and Validation of Measurement Data
statement: The hospital uses an established, statistically sound process to validate data as a component of its quality and patient safety program.
elements: The hospital validates data, to ensure performance monitoring reflects the actual performance, when any of the following conditions are noted, at a minimum: • A new measure is implemented (in particular, those clinical measures that are intended to help a hospital evaluate and improve an important clinical process or outcome). • Data will be made public on the hospital’s website or in other ways. • A change has been made to an existing measure, such as the data collection methods have changed, or the data abstraction process or abstractor has changed. • The data resulting from an existing measure have changed in an unexplainable way. • The data source has changed, such as when part of the patient health care record has been turned into an electronic format and thus the data source is now both electronic and paper. • The subject of the data collection has changed, such as changes in average age of patients, comorbidities, research protocol alterations, new practice guidelines implemented, or new technologies and treatment methodologies introduced. • When the data collection method is manual, and data collection staff have changed mid-cycle.
The hospital uses an evidence-based methodology for data validation.
Hospital leaders assume accountability for the validity of the quality and outcome data made public.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
group: Analysis and Validation of Measurement Data
statement: Individuals with specialized experience, knowledge, and skills systematically aggregate, validate, and analyze data in the hospital.
elements: The hospital regularly aggregates, analyzes, and transforms data into useful information to identify useful trends, variances, and opportunities for improvement. Aggregate data and information include information requirements for key functions as specified in this manual (for example, facility management and safety, infection control, clinical data and information, identified hospitalwide indicators, department-specific indicators, physician-specific information). (See also QPS.03.00, ME 2)
The hospital defines and approves appropriate data management qualifications for individuals who participate in data collection, aggregation, validation, and analysis.
The hospital uses established statistical tools and techniques in the analysis process (for example, brainstorming, fishbone diagrams).
