Hospital leaders determine the frequency of reporting the results of analysis to those accountable for action, in accordance with laws and regulations and national health care industry standards, and in a manner they can understand and use.

Data analysis supports comparisons internally and externally over time, including comparisons with databases of like hospitals, with best practices, and with objective scientific professional sources to identify deficiencies and opportunities for improvement.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
group: Analysis and Validation of Measurement Data
statement: The data analysis process includes at least one evaluation of the clinical, financial, and operational impact of hospitalwide improvement priorities per year.
elements: The hospital collects data on the amount and type of resources used on at least one hospitalwide priority improvement project per year before and following the improvement. (See also GLD.04.00, ME 1; QPS.01.00, ME 3)
The quality and patient safety program staff work with other units such as human resources, information technology, and finance in deciding which data are to be collected.
The hospital uses the results of the analysis to refine the process and report it through the quality and patient safety program mechanism to leaders.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
group: Analysis and Validation of Measurement Data
statement: The hospital identifies undesirable trends and variation and always conducts an intensive analysis, or a comprehensive systematic analysis, when these are evident from its data collection.
elements: The hospital defines and implements, through a policy and form, data collection processes (for example, reportable incidents, occurrence variances) to ensure that risks to patient safety are identified and reported in a timely manner.
The hospital, in a timely manner, conducts an intensive analysis or a comprehensive systematic analysis of data when adverse events, patterns, or undesirable trends occur.

The hospital performs data collection and analysis for all the following, at a minimum, when applicable: • All confirmed transfusion reactions • All serious drug reactions or drug-related patient safety events as defined by the hospital or laws

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital achieves and sustains improvement in quality and safety.
elements: The hospital plans, tests, and implements improvements in quality and patient safety, prioritizing quality improvement projects as well as strategic and operational planning based on the information resulting from data analysis. When appropriate, the hospital tests improvement interventions prior to full implementation. (See also GLD.04.02, ME 1)
Data are available to demonstrate that improvements are effective and sustained. (See also GLD.06.01, ME 3)
The hospital changes policies, procedures, protocols, and guidelines when necessary to plan, to carry out, and to sustain quality and patient safety improvement.
Successful improvements are documented and reviewed by the quality and patient safety program and hospital leaders to understand why efforts were or were not successful. (See also GLD.04.00, ME 2)

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital uses an ongoing program of risk management, overseen by qualified individuals with the appropriate experience, knowledge, and skills, to identify and proactively reduce unanticipated adverse events and other safety risks to patients and staff.
elements: The hospital’s risk management program framework for all hospital departments and services (clinical and managerial) includes the following: • Scope and objectives of the program as well as the individual responsible for the program • A risk management policy that identifies and prioritizes risk urgency and has a plan to minimize

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Leaders of hospital departments and services define the desired qualifications of all staff.
elements: Department and/or service leaders consider the following elements to project department staffing needs: • Hospital’s mission • Mix of patient populations served by the hospital and the complexity of patient care needs • Scope of services provided by the hospital • Volume of patients • Medical equipment and technology used in patient care (See also GLD.06.00, ME 2)

The hospital, through the department head, defines staff qualifications specific to their job responsibilities and requests the resources required by the department for a safe and quality service (for example, space, equipment, supplies, staffing, and other resources).
The hospital director ensures the recruitment and selection of competent and skilled hospital staff and that the recruitment and retention of all staff comply with applicable laws and regulations.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital defines the responsibilities of every staff member in a current job description.
elements: Each staff member not permitted to practice independently has a job description which is used when selecting employees for hire, performance evaluation, internal promotion, and transfer. The job description specifies the reporting relationships.
Each job description includes defined responsibilities for the staff member with this job and the required knowledge, skills, and attitude to perform the job responsibilities.

Job descriptions and/or specified privileges are required for medical staff when present in the hospital for the following circumstances: • Serves in primarily a managerial role or in dual clinical and managerial roles, with the managerial

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Leaders of hospital departments and services implement processes for the recruitment and retention of staff.
elements: The hospital implements a coordinated process to recruit staff.
The hospital implements a coordinated process to evaluate the qualifications of new staff.
The hospital implements a coordinated process to appoint individuals to the staff, which considers evaluation of verified credentials. (See also SQE.03.00)
The hospital implements a process that is uniform across the hospital for similar types of staff.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital evaluates staff performance.
elements: The hospital uses a defined process to ensure that staff qualifications are consistent with the care, treatment, and services it provides. (See also ASC.02.01, MEs 1 and 2)

The hospital, through policy and procedure, regularly evaluates staff based on objective criteria and performance expectations that reflect their job responsibilities. The outcome of the performance evaluation is used to set objectives for performance improvement and professional development. (See also HRP.02.01, ME 2)

New staff are evaluated through a process described in a policy or other document before or at the time they begin their work responsibilities. All new employees go through a probationary period, during which clinical staff can work only under direct supervision for competency evaluation. Competency evaluation during the probationary period is a structured process that aims to assess and review the employee’s knowledge, performance, capability, conduct, and suitability for the role.
The department or service to which the individual is assigned conducts the evaluation.

An individual with the educational background, experience, or knowledge related to the skills being reviewed conducts or co-leads the evaluation. The performance evaluation is signed by both the employee and the supervisor and is documented in the personnel file.
Clinical staff evaluations are designed to be a two-way process and are completed and documented annually or more frequently as defined by hospital policy or consistent with laws and regulations.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: There is documented personnel information for each staff member.
elements: Personnel records for each staff member are standardized, complete, current, and maintained.
The hospital has a policy guiding the initiation, management, content update, and retention time and disposal of personnel files.
Personnel records are kept confidential and secure, consistent with hospital policy, and only those who are authorized can access them.
Personnel records contain documented evidence of the following: • Current job description that includes job qualifications and responsibilities, as indicated (See also

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital has the necessary staff to support the care, treatment, and services it provides.
elements: Hospital leaders implement a hospital staffing process that results in a written staffing plan for each department developed in collaboration with the human resources department that supports the care, treatment, and services it provides to fulfill its part of the hospital’s mission. (See also GLD.03.01, ME 1)

The hospital staffing process indicates the number, types, and desired qualifications of staff per departmental needs and job responsibilities, using a recognized staffing method. The staffing plan identifies an evidence-based estimation of the number of staff needed per shift, considering all relevant factors (for example, patient acuity, patient care hours, size of the hospital, scope of services provided).
The hospital staffing process describes the assignment and reassignment of staff.
The hospital staffing process complies with local laws and regulations.
The effectiveness of the hospital staffing process is monitored on an ongoing basis to identify any deficiencies and take improvement actions accordingly.
The hospital staffing process is reviewed and revised at least annually, consistent with hospital policy and when indicated.
The hospital staffing process involves coordination with various hospital department/service leaders.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital provides orientation for all staff.
elements: The hospital completes general orientation before staff provide care, treatment, and services independently. The hospital provides all new employees with an employee manual or equivalent that contains a summary of the general orientation program as well as other relevant important information. (See also GHI.02.00, ME 4)

The hospital orients staff on the following according to their job description as general orientation: • High-risk quality and general and facility management and safety issues (for example, reporting of medical errors, infection prevention and control practices, the hospital’s policies on telephone medication orders, fire safety, disasters, hazardous materials, utilities, equipment failures) • The hospital’s mission, vision, values and organization chart; the department and/or unit to

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Staff participate in education and training.
elements: Staff participate in ongoing education and training to maintain or increase their competency, and as needed. Staff participation is guided by a policy that describes the structure and process used in the continuing education of all categories of staff. (See also AOP.05.02, ME 2)
Hospital staff are provided ongoing education and training.

The hospital uses various sources of data and information, including the results of quality and safety measurement activities, to identify staff education needs. The training and educational needs are identified based on objective criteria that include, but are not limited to, the following: • The hospital mission, vision, and scope of services • Individual staff member’s education and training history • Information from quality assessment and improvement activities • Needs generated by advancements made in the medical and health care management fields • Findings from department performance appraisals of individuals • Findings from peer review activities • Findings from the hospital’s technology and safety management programs • Findings from infection control activities (See also GLD.07.01, ME 3)
Staff education programs are developed and provided based on these data and information.

The education is provided under an educational program with an ongoing schedule of educational activities and is relevant to the hospital needs, each staff member’s ability to meet patient needs, and/ or continuing education requirements.
The hospital provides adequate time and resources (for example, financial support) for all staff to participate in relevant education and training opportunities.
Completion of training and education is documented for all staff in their personnel record.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Staff are competent in resuscitative techniques appropriate to their role in the hospital.
elements: Clinical staff who provide patient care, treatment, and services, including medical staff, are trained in and maintain valid certification of at least basic life support (BLS).

The hospital identifies the level of training related to advanced cardiac life support (ACLS), neonatal resuscitation program (NRP), pediatric advanced life support (PALS), and advanced trauma life support (ATLS) appropriate to their roles in the hospital for all clinical staff who provide patient care. Examples include, but are not limited to, the following: • Physicians and nurses working in critical care areas must maintain additional certification in ACLS, PALS, and NRP as appropriate to the patients’ age groups. • Internal medicine physicians must maintain additional certification in ACLS. • Emergency department physicians must maintain additional certification in ACLS, PALS, and ATLS. • Pediatricians must maintain additional certification in PALS and NRP. (See also ASC.02.00,

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital provides a staff health and safety program that addresses staff physical and mental health and safe working conditions.
elements: The hospital implements a staff health and safety program that is responsive to urgent and nonurgent staff needs through direct treatment and referral. The program covers all staff members and is coordinated with the hospital’s quality, safety, risk management, and infection control program and is consistent with laws and regulations. The program is based on assessment and, where necessary, reduction of occupational health and safety risks.

The staff health and safety program, at a minimum, includes the following: • Initial employment health screening • Measures to control or reduce harmful occupational exposures, such as exposure to toxic drugs or harmful noise levels, including the use of protective equipment and clothing, stress management,

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital identifies staff who are at risk for exposure to and possible transmission of vaccine-preventable diseases and implements a staff vaccination and immunization program.
elements: The hospital identifies epidemiologically significant infections, which includes hepatitis B and C, HIV, and tuberculosis, as well as staff who are at high risk for exposure to and transmission of infections. All employees have baseline screening for hepatitis B and C, HIV, and tuberculosis. (See also PCI.08.01, ME 2)

The hospital develops and implements a staff vaccination and immunization program, which includes the following: • Determination of the immune status of newly hired staff against hepatitis B, measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella by serological testing, and vaccinating those susceptible. Response to hepatitis B vaccination is monitored in vaccinated employees four weeks after completing vaccine series. Non-responders to hepatitis B vaccine are offered at least a second series of the vaccine. • Screening for tuberculosis of newly hired staff with PPD test. The test is repeated annually for those who are non-reactive. PPD conversion rates are calculated and monitored. (See also

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Leaders and staff are trained and demonstrate competence in workplace violence prevention.
elements: The hospital develops and implements a workplace violence program consistent with the international and national norms, laws, and regulations of the country.

The hospital provides training, education, and resources (at the time of hire, annually, and whenever changes occur regarding the workplace violence prevention program) to leaders and staff on workplace violence. (See also GLD.07.02, ME 2)
The hospital determines what aspects of training are appropriate for individuals based on their roles, workplace, and responsibilities.

The training, education, and resources address prevention, recognition, response, mitigation, and reporting of workplace violence as follows: • What constitutes workplace violence (See also GLD.07.02, ME 2) • Education on the roles and responsibilities of leaders, clinical staff, security personnel, and

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital has a uniform process to collect, verify, and evaluate credentials of the nursing staff.
elements: The hospital has a standardized procedure, defined in a policy, to collect, verify, and document the license, education, training, certifications, and experience of each nursing staff member, whether full time or part time.
License, education, training, certifications, and experience are verified from the original source and documented.

Licensure is verified from the original source consistent with the following parameters and is documented: • The hospital must verify that the third party implements the verification process as described in hospital policy or regulations and that the process meets the expectations described in these standards. • The affiliated hospital that has already conducted primary source verification of the nursing staff applicant is acceptable if the affiliated hospital has current Joint Commission International (JCI) accreditation with “full compliance” on its verification process found in SQE.03.00, MEs 1 and 2. • The hospital that bases its decisions in part on information from a designated official governmental or nongovernmental agency must evaluate the agency providing the information initially and then periodically thereafter to ensure that JCI standards continue to be met. • The hospital receives confirmatory documentation.
A record is maintained with the credentials, including current professional license, certificate, or registration, for every nursing staff member.
The hospital has a process to ensure that the credentials of contracted nurses are valid and complete prior to assignment.
The hospital has a process to ensure that nurses who are not employees of the hospital but accompany private physicians and provide services to the hospital’s patients have valid credentials.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital has a standardized process to identify job responsibilities and to plan clinical work assignments based on the nursing staff member’s credentials and any regulatory requirements.
elements: Nursing staff have education, experience, training, and/or certification consistent with the hospital’s scope of services, as indicated in their job description and as applicable to their role.
Core criteria for evaluating nursing staff in the program include, at a minimum, current licensure and current competence.

In addition to patient volume and acuity, licensure, education, training, skill level, and experience of a nursing staff member are used to plan clinical work assignments in accordance with laws and regulations and nursing licensing boards.

The process considers applicable laws and regulations and ensures registration of all nursing staff with the Saudi Commission for Health Specialties and maintenance of a valid license to practice only within their profession.
The process supports nurse staffing plans developed by the nursing director that maintains an adequate staffing level in all nursing units.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital has a standardized process for nursing staff participation in the hospital’s continuous quality improvement activities, including evaluating individual performance when indicated.
elements: Nursing staff participate in the hospital’s continuous quality improvement activities.
The performance of individual nursing staff members is reviewed when indicated by variances noted on trend or as negative deviations to continuous quality improvement activities.
Information from the review process is documented in the nurse’s personnel record or in a separate credential record, consistent with hospital policy.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital has a uniform process to collect, verify, and evaluate the credentials of other clinical staff.
elements: The hospital has a standardized process, defined in a policy, for collecting, documenting, and verifying each clinical staff member’s license, education, certifications, training, and experience, whether full time or part time.
License, education, training, certifications, and experience are verified from the original source and documented.

Licensure is verified from the original source consistent with the following parameters and is documented: • The hospital must verify that the third party implements the verification process as described in hospital policy or regulations and that the process meets the expectations described in these standards. • The affiliated hospital that has already conducted primary source verification of the other clinical staff applicant is acceptable if the affiliated hospital has current Joint Commission International (JCI) accreditation with “full compliance” on its verification process found in SQE.04.00, MEs 1 and 2. • The hospital that bases its decisions in part on information from a designated, official, governmental, or nongovernmental agency must evaluate the agency providing the information initially and then periodically thereafter to ensure that JCI standards continue to be met. • The hospital receives confirmatory documentation.
A record is maintained with copies of any required license, certification, or registration for other clinical staff.

The hospital has a process to ensure that staff who are not employees of the hospital but accompany private physicians and provide services to the hospital’s patients have valid credentials that are comparable to the hospital’s requirement for credentials.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital has a uniform process to identify job responsibilities and to make clinical work assignments based on other clinical staff’s credentials and any regulatory requirements.
elements: Verified licensure, education, training, and experience of other clinical staff are used to make clinical work assignments and develop job responsibilities.

The process considers relevant laws and regulations and ensures registration of all other clinical staff with the Saudi Commission for Health Specialties and maintenance of a valid license to practice only within their profession.
The process supports the staffing process for other clinical staff.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital has a uniform process for other clinical staff participation in the hospital’s continuous quality improvement activities.
elements: Other clinical staff participate in the hospital’s continuous quality improvement activities.
The performance of other clinical staff is reviewed when indicated by the findings of the continuous quality improvement activities.
Appropriate information from the review process is documented in the other clinical staff member’s record.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital has a uniform process for collecting the credentials of medical staff members permitted to provide patient care without supervision.
elements: The hospital has an ongoing, uniform process to manage the credentials of medical staff members.

Medical staff members permitted by laws and regulations and the hospital to provide patient care without supervision are identified. All members of the medical staff must be registered with the Saudi Commission for Health Specialties before allowed to work independently. The process of appointment, reappointment, and granting of privileges is in accordance with relevant laws and regulations.

Education, licensure/registration, and other credentials required by law or regulation are copied by the hospital and maintained for each medical staff member in their personnel record or in a separate credential record.
All credentials required by hospital policy are copied by the hospital and maintained for each medical staff member in their personnel record or in a separate credential record.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Medical staff members’ education, licensure/registration, and other credentials required by laws and regulations and the hospital are verified and kept current.
elements: Education, licensure/registration, training, experience, and other credentials required by laws and regulations or issued by recognized education or professional entities as the basis for clinical privileges are verified from the original source that issued the credential. The process is defined in a policy and applies to full-time, part-time, visiting, and locum tenens medical staff members.
Additional credentials required by hospital policy are verified from the source that issued the credential when required by hospital policy.

When third-party verification is used, the hospital verifies that the third party (for example, a government agency) implements the verification process as described in hospital policy and/or laws and regulations and that the process meets the following expectations: • The hospital verifies that the third party implements the verification process as described in hospital policy or regulations and that the process meets the expectations described in these standards. • The affiliated hospital that has already conducted primary source verification of the medical staff applicant is acceptable if the affiliated hospital has current Joint Commission International (JCI) accreditation with “full compliance” on its verification process found in SQE.03.00, MEs 1 and 2. • The hospital that bases its decisions in part on information from a designated official governmental or nongovernmental agency must evaluate the agency providing the information initially and then periodically thereafter to ensure that JCI standards continue to be met. • The hospital receives confirmatory documentation.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: There is a uniform decision process for the initial appointment of medical staff members, and others permitted to practice independently.
elements: Medical staff appointments and granting of clinical privileges are made consistent with hospital policy and are consistent with the hospital’s patient population, mission, and the care, treatment, and services provided. The appointment, reappointment, and granting of privileges are based on the following: • Evaluation of verified credentials (license, education, training, and experience) • Evaluation of mental and physical health and capabilities • Competency, actual performance, and outcomes of care • Category of the medical staff as stated in the professional registration with the Saudi

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital has a standardized, objective, evidence-based process to grant or deny privileges for medical staff members and others permitted to practice independently.
elements: The privilege delineation process used by the hospital meets the following criteria: • Standardized, objective, and evidence-based • Documented in hospital policies • Active and ongoing as the credentials of medical staff members change • Followed for all classes of medical staff membership • Effectiveness of the process can be demonstrated

The hospital establishes criteria that determine a medical staff member’s ability to provide patient care, treatment, and services within the scope of the privilege(s) requested, including evaluation of the following: • Current licensure and/or certification, as indicated, verified with the primary source • The applicant’s specific relevant training and credentials, verified with the primary source • Evidence of physical ability to perform the requested privilege • Data from professional practice review by an organization(s) that currently privileges the

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Hospital leaders grant temporary clinical privileges to medical staff for a limited period of time and for circumstances as defined by hospital policy.
elements: Temporary or emergency privileges are granted to meet a specific patient care need for the time period defined in hospital policy.
When temporary privileges are granted to meet a specific need, the organized medical staff verifies current licensure and current competence.

Temporary privileges of applicants for new privileges may be granted while awaiting review and approval by the organized medical staff upon verification of the following: • Current licensure • Relevant training or experience • Current competence • Ability to perform the privileges requested • Other criteria required by applicable laws and regulations • A query and evaluation of any relevant medical staff data bank or platform information, if

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: At a minimum every two years, the hospital decides to grant, deny, and/or modify requested medical staff membership and clinical privileges.
elements: The hospital has a documented process for reappointment of all categories of medical staff.

The hospital determines if medical staff membership and clinical privileges are to continue with or without modification based on the ongoing professional practice evaluation of the medical staff member at least every two years.
Each medical staff member’s personnel file contains evidence that all credentials are current.

Medical staff member personnel files contain any credentials obtained after initial appointment and include evidence of primary source verification prior to use in modifying or adding to clinical privileges.
Medical staff members and other clinical staff requesting privileges are notified regarding the granting decision. In the case of privilege denial, the applicant is informed of the reason for denial.

The hospital has implemented a process to disseminate all granting, modification, or restriction decisions to all appropriate internal and external persons or entities, as defined by hospital policy and applicable laws and regulations.
The renewal decision is documented in the medical staff member’s credential record and includes the identification of the reviewer and any special conditions identified during the review.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital uses an ongoing standardized process to evaluate the quality and safety of the patient care provided by each medical staff member.
elements: All medical staff members are included in an ongoing professional practice evaluation process and standardized evaluation at the department/service level as defined by hospital policy.

The ongoing professional practice evaluation process identifies areas of achievement and potential improvement related to the behaviors, professional growth, and clinical results of the medical staff member, and the results are reviewed with objective and evidence-based information as available. These results are compared to other department/service medical staff members. (See also GLD.07.01, ME 3)

The data and information from the monitoring are reviewed at least every 12 months and when indicated by the findings of performance improvement activities by the individual’s department or service head, senior medical manager, or medical staff body, and the medical director; and the results, conclusions, and any actions taken are documented in the medical staff member’s credential record and other relevant records. The data and information resulting from the medical staff performance review are used to do the following: • Provide feedback and counseling to the medical staff regarding their performance • Recommend plans for improvement • Amend clinical privileges as necessary, by expansion or limitation, a period of counseling and

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Hospital leaders define the circumstances requiring monitoring and evaluation of a medical staff member’s professional performance.
elements: A period of focused professional practice evaluation is implemented for all initially requested privileges.

Criteria are developed for unplanned evaluation of the performance of the medical staff member or other medical staff when issues affecting the provision of safe, high-quality patient care are identified.

The performance monitoring process is clearly defined and includes each of the following elements: • Criteria for conducting performance monitoring • Method for establishing a monitoring plan specific to the requested privilege • Method for determining the duration of performance monitoring • Circumstances under which monitoring by an external source is required
Focused professional practice evaluation is consistently implemented in accordance with the criteria and process defined by hospital policy.
The measures employed to resolve performance issues are defined in writing and implemented. Section III:

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Hospital leaders are accountable for the protection of human research subjects.
elements: Hospital leaders establish and promote a code of ethical professional behavior.
Hospital leaders, verbally and in writing, communicate within the hospital its commitment to protect human subjects research participants and support the code of ethical professional behavior.
Hospital leaders assume responsibility for patient protection irrespective of the sponsor of the research.
Hospital leaders have a process for budgeting to provide adequate resources for effective operation of the research program.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Hospital leaders establish the scope of the research program.
elements: Hospital leaders determine the scope of the research program.
Hospital leaders identify the facilities and resources that support the research program.
Hospital leaders identify the qualifications of staff permitted to participate in the research program as principal investigators or other members of the research team.
There is documentation of the qualifications of staff permitted to participate in the research program.
Hospital leaders identify those circumstances in which hospital employees and staff can serve as research subjects.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Hospital leaders establish a policy for sponsors of research to ensure their commitment to the conduct of ethical research.
elements: Hospital leaders establish a written policy for sponsors of research with requirements of accountability for the research, including the following: • Compliance with the hospital’s policies and processes for monitoring and evaluating the quality,

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: When one or more of the research-related duties and functions of the sponsor are provided through an outside commercial or academic contract research organization, the accountabilities of the outside contract research organization are clearly defined.
elements: The hospital establishes and implements a written process to determine the activities and responsibilities of a contract research organization.
The duties and functions transferred by the sponsor to the contract research organization are contained in a written contract.
The contract specifies that the contract research organization or sponsor is responsible for monitoring and evaluating the quality, safety, and ethics of the research. (See also GLD.07.00, ME 1)
The sponsor is responsible for monitoring the contract.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Hospital leaders implement a process to provide the initial and ongoing review of all human subjects research.
elements: Hospital leaders identify and support the structure and operational requirements of the research review process.
The research review process complies with applicable laws and regulations.
Hospital leaders specify the requirements of entities outside of the hospital that provide all or a portion of the research review process, such as a contract research organization.
Hospital leaders ensure that research that is exempt from the research review process is identified.
Hospital leaders specify the requirements for documentation of the activities of the research review process.
Hospital leaders provide for a review of all research review processes at least annually.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital manages conflicts of interest with research conducted at the hospital.
elements: The hospital has a written policy to identity and manage conflicts of interest with research conducted at the hospital.
The hospital’s conflict of interest policy includes a process for managing conflicts of interest, both financial and nonfinancial.
The hospital specifies the individuals, committees, and others for whom the requirements apply.
The hospital has an ongoing education and monitoring process to ensure compliance with the requirements.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital integrates the human subjects research program into the quality and patient safety program of the hospital.
elements: The research program is a component of the hospital’s processes to report and act on sentinel events and other adverse events, as well as the processes to learn from near misses (or close calls).

The research program is included in the hospital’s programs for hazardous materials management, medical equipment management, and medication management. (See also FMS.05.00, ME 1; FMS.07.00, ME 1; MMU.01.00, ME 1)
The evaluation of staff participating in the research program is incorporated into the ongoing monitoring processes of professional performance. (See also SQE.01.03, ME 2)

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital informs patients and families about how to gain access to clinical research, clinical investigations, or clinical trials and includes protections for vulnerable populations to minimize potential coercion or undue influence.
elements: The hospital establishes and implements an informed consent process that enables patients to make informed and voluntary decisions about participating in clinical research, clinical investigations, or clinical trials, including the following: • How consent for participation will be obtained and documented • Under what circumstances consent will be obtained again during the research Note: This is accomplished through the research review process.
Patients and families are identified and informed about how to gain access to clinical research, clinical investigations, or clinical trials relevant to their treatment needs.

Through the research review process, the hospital implements safeguards to protect the safety, rights, and well-being of vulnerable patients, as identified by the hospital, who may be at risk for coercion or undue influence. (See also PCC.01.04, ME 4)
Through the research review process, the hospital implements safeguards to protect the safety, rights, and well-being of hospital staff who may be at risk for coercion or undue influence.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital’s governing body and leaders approve and monitor the hospital’s participation in providing medical education.
elements: The decision to provide medical education is made by the governing entity and leaders of the hospital, is consistent with the hospital’s mission, and is documented.
The hospital’s governing entity and leaders obtain, review, and accept the parameters of the participating medical school, and this action is documented.

The hospital’s governing entity and leaders endorse a set of metrics to monitor and evaluate the ongoing operation of medical education programs, and there is documented review of the monitoring data.
The hospital’s governing entity and leaders review the medical education programs within the hospital at least annually, and the review is documented.
The review includes the satisfaction of patients and staff with the clinical care provided under the program.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital’s teaching staff, patient population, technology, and facility are consistent with the goals and objectives of the education program.
elements: There is documented evidence that the teaching staff of the hospital are adequate in number and have the education, training, and competence to support and advance the education of medical students and trainees.
There is documented evidence that the hospital’s patient population is adequate in number and clinical needs to support the education of medical students and trainees.
There is documented evidence that the hospital’s facilities, technology, and other resources support the education of medical students and trainees.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Teaching staff are identified, and each staff member’s role and relationship to the academic institution is defined.
elements: Teaching staff are identified to hospital staff, and there is a complete list of teaching staff, including both professional and academic titles, as applicable.
Staff are educated about these individuals, their roles, accountabilities, and authority.
The hospital implements a process to monitor and maintain current records of applicable academic titles and requirements for renewal or redesignation.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The hospital has a process for supervision of each type and level of medical student and trainee by a qualified physician.
elements: The hospital has a process for supervision of each medical student and trainee by a medical staff member with appropriate privileges to provide uniform medical student and trainee experiences.

The hospital establishes written descriptions of the roles, responsibilities, and patient care activities of the participants of professional education programs. The descriptions are as follows: • Include the process by which the supervisor(s) and professional education program director make decisions about each participant’s progressive involvement and independence in specific patient

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Medical education provided in the hospital is coordinated and managed through a defined operational mechanism and management structure.
elements: The operational structure for medical education in the hospital has been established and is fully operational.
The management structure for medical education in the hospital has been determined and implemented.
There is a complete and current list of all medical students and trainees in the hospital.

For each medical student and trainee, there is documentation of at least the following: • Enrollment status • Academic classification • Any required licensure or certification • Reports of medical student and trainee achievements • Identification of medical student and trainee competencies • Any known factors that will require accommodation • Any known factors that may influence the level of supervision required

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Medical students and trainees comply with all hospital policies and procedures, and all care is provided within the quality and patient safety parameters of the hospital.
elements: All medical students and trainees are provided an orientation that includes at least the following: • Hospital quality and patient safety program • Infection prevention and control program • Medication safety program • International Patient Safety Goals • Other required hospital orientation, including at the department and unit level • Ongoing required education
Medical students and trainees are included in the data collection for the hospital’s quality monitoring programs.
Those supervising medical students and trainees ensure that the medical students and trainees are knowledgeable of the programs and participate in the programs.
Medical students and trainees can demonstrate knowledge of these programs.
Those supervising medical students and trainees consider compliance with these programs in their evaluation of medical student and trainee performance.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: Medical trainees who provide care or services within the hospital—outside of the parameters of their academic program—are granted permission to provide those services.
elements: The hospital determines what types of trainees and under which circumstances trainees can be hired or otherwise engaged by the hospital to provide patient care or other services.
Trainees providing such services are granted permission through credentialing and privileging, a job description, or other relevant processes for the services being provided.
Trainees providing such services are evaluated for the services being provided.

manual: Hospitals and Academic Medical Centers Standards
statement: The ambulatory care organization informs the community about its services and how to obtain care and screens patients to identify whether their health care needs match the ambulatory care organization’s mission and resources.
elements: The ambulatory care organization’s services, hours of operation, and process to obtain care are communicated to the community.
Screening results are used to determine if the patient’s needs match the ambulatory care organization’s mission and resources.
Patients are accepted only if the ambulatory care organization can provide the necessary services and appropriate care.

If the patient’s needs do not match the organization’s mission and resources, there is a process to transfer, refer, or assist the patient in identifying and/or obtaining appropriate sources of care. Patients who present with emergencies beyond the organization’s capacity are stabilized before transfer to another organization.
Specific screening tests or evaluations are identified when the ambulatory care organization requires them prior to initiating treatment and services.

statement: Patient flow in the ambulatory care organization is designed to provide efficient care and uniform access based on patient needs.
elements: The ambulatory care organization uses decision criteria to prioritize patients with immediate needs.
The ambulatory care organization has an appointment system to book patients in advance. Appointment staff are aware of the organization’s services and direct patients to the appropriate services.

The ambulatory care organization uses a standardized process for registering patients for services based on their full name and identification number or passport number for visitors, and the patient registration and treatment processes are designed to prioritize those who are sick and those with urgent needs.
Patients with appointments and patients who walk into the organization without an appointment are managed in a consistent manner.
When care and/or treatment are delayed, the patient is informed of the reasons for the delay or wait as well as available alternatives consistent with their clinical needs.

statement: The ambulatory care organization designs and carries out processes to provide continuity of patient care services in the organization and coordination among health care practitioners.
elements: The leaders of departments and services design and implement processes that support continuity and coordination of patient care, such as care plans, guidelines, and other such methods.
Health care practitioners record observations, test results, treatments, results of team meetings, and other pertinent information in the patient’s medical record.
The patient’s medical record(s) is up to date and available to those practitioners who are authorized to have access and need it for the patient’s care.

When consultations to other available specialties are requested, the following occur: • The consultation clearly states the reason for and urgency of the request. • Consultation requests provide appropriate answers to the issues that the referring physician raised. • Arrangements are made to ensure that consultations are immediately available for emergency cases. Urgent consultations are referred to the emergency department.
The ambulatory care organization supports effective, team-delivered care consistent with its mission and patient needs.

statement: There is a qualified individual identified as responsible for the patient’s care.
elements: The individual responsible for the patient’s care is identified.
The individual is qualified to assume responsibility for the patient’s care.
The individual is identified to the organization’s staff.

statement: The ambulatory care organization has a program to provide ongoing care and support to patients with chronic diseases.
elements: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a chronic disease management program appropriate to its scope of services and patient population, including patient and family education and promotion of self-management.

The ambulatory care organization partners with other providers, such as primary care centers, hospitals, and health care practitioners, to facilitate coordination of services to improve the management of patients with chronic conditions.
The ambulatory care organization evaluates the efficacy of its chronic disease management program.

statement: The medical records of patients seen over time who require complex care or have complex diagnoses contain profiles of the medical care and are made available to the health care practitioners providing care to those patients.
elements: The ambulatory care organization identifies the types of patients receiving ongoing complex care and/ or with complex diagnoses who require a profile.
The health care practitioners who treat those patients identify the medical information to be included in the profile.
The ambulatory care organization uses a process to ensure that the profile contains accurate and complete medical information.
The ambulatory care organization uses a process to ensure that the profile is updated as needed and available in an easy-to-retrieve and easy-to-review format.
The process is evaluated to see if it meets the health care practitioners’ needs and improves the quality and safety of clinical services.

statement: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process to refer patients to other health care practitioners, other levels of care, other health care settings, or other organizations to meet their continuing care needs.
elements: There is an established process to guide referrals for care outside the ambulatory care organization.
A referral is based on the patient’s needs for care that cannot be provided by the ambulatory care organization.
Appropriate patient care information is shared with health care practitioners and organizations outside the ambulatory care organization.
There is a process to follow up on care that the ambulatory care organization’s patients receive from outside sources.

statement: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process to transfer patients to another organization to meet their continuing care needs.
elements: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process, based on its capabilities, to transfer patients, including criteria to address patients’ needs for continuing care.

The process addresses how responsibility for continuing care is moved to another practitioner or setting, ensuring that the receiving organization explicitly accepts responsibility for the patient’s care and is provided with all necessary information to deliver appropriate care.

The process addresses who is responsible for the patient during transfer, ensuring the patient is monitored, with monitoring data and transfer time documented in the medical record. The receiving organization acknowledges the patient’s arrival, time, and condition, with this information also documented in patient’s medical record.
The process addresses what is done in situations in which transfer is not possible.

There is a process to evaluate the quality and safety of the transfer process, including a follow-up mechanism that provides information about the patient’s condition upon arrival at the receiving organization.

statement: Information about the care and services that the patient will need when referred by the ambulatory care organization is communicated to the patient, family, and continuing care practitioner and/or setting.
elements: The ambulatory care organization has a process through which it communicates to patients and their families about their ongoing health needs and needed care and services.
A written summary conveys information to a continuing care setting and contains, as appropriate, a medication list, significant diagnoses and treatments, follow-up instructions, and test results.
When an individual health care practitioner refers a patient to the ambulatory care organization, the organization provides a summary of its care to the referring health care practitioner.

statement: Patient education and follow-up instructions are given in a form and language the patient can understand.
elements: Patient education and follow-up instructions are provided in a language that the patient can understand.
Patient education and follow-up instructions are provided in writing, verbally, and/or in another form the patient understands.
The instructions include any return for follow-up care.
The instructions include when to obtain urgent care.

statement: The process for referring or transferring the patient evaluates the need for transportation.
elements: The process for referring patients evaluates the need for transportation.
The process for transferring patients evaluates the need for transportation.
Transportation needs are evaluated when patient’s care is complete, and they are not being referred or transferred.

When a patient is identified with emergent clinical care needs beyond the ambulatory care organization’s scope and mission, the organization ensures safe and timely transportation to a health care organization that can provide the appropriate level of care.
Transportation is appropriate to patients’ needs.

statement: The ambulatory care organization’s transportation services comply with relevant laws and regulations and meet requirements for quality and safe transport.
elements: Ambulatory care organizations that own medical transport vehicles ensure that they meet relevant laws and regulations related to their operation, condition, and maintenance.

Ambulatory care organizations that provide transportation services, including contracted services, ensure that transportation services meet the ambulatory care organization’s requirements for quality and safe transport.

Staff responsible for monitoring the patient or providing other patient care during transport have the qualifications, including appropriate life support certification, required for the type of patient being transferred.

All vehicles used for transportation, contracted or owned by the ambulatory care organization, comply with the infection prevention and control program and have appropriate medical equipment, supplies, and medications to meet the needs of the patient being transported. Specifically, ambulances, whether owned or contracted, meet the following requirements: • The ambulances are fully equipped to transfer sick patients of all age groups to higher organizations when needed. • The emergency services nurse or technician checks the ambulances’ required equipment daily and after each dispatch for proper functionality and documents their findings. • The emergency services nurse or technician do daily and post-dispatch checks of ambulance medications for availability and expiry and documents their findings. • The ambulances are tested daily for proper operation and periodically maintained, with findings documented.
There is a process in place to monitor the quality and safety of transportation provided or arranged by the ambulatory care organization, including a complaint process.

statement: An initial assessment process is used to identify the health care needs of all patients.
elements: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements an initial assessment process to identify the health care needs of all patients.
The ambulatory care organization identifies who performs which assessments.

The ambulatory care organization identifies the assessment process for those patients whose needs do not match the organization’s mission and resources and who may require a referral or transfer to another organization.

statement: The scope and content of initial assessments conducted by different clinical disciplines are defined in writing and based on applicable laws and regulations.
elements: The scope and content of initial assessments by each clinical discipline are defined in writing and documented in the patient medical record.

The assessments include at least, as appropriate to the patient’s needs, the following: • A medical history and physical examination as well as chief complaint and chronic illnesses • A list of current medications and known allergies (See also MMU.4, ME 1.) • An initial psychological assessment, as indicated by the patient’s needs • An initial social assessment, as indicated by the patient’s needs
Only qualified individuals permitted by licensure, applicable laws and regulations, or certification perform the assessments.
The ambulatory care organization identifies, in writing, those special patient groups and populations it serves that require modifications to its assessment.
The assessment process for special patient groups by different specialties and in different locations reflects their needs.

statement: Patients are screened for nutritional status, functional needs, and other special needs as indicated by their condition, and referred for further assessment and treatment when necessary.
elements: The ambulatory care organization develops screening criteria for identifying patients who require further nutritional or functional assessments or social needs assessments, and the criteria are implemented consistently throughout the ambulatory care organization where needed.

Patients are screened for nutritional status when indicated by their condition, and if needed, further assessed and treated in the ambulatory care organization, or referred or provided with a referral to appropriate follow-up.

Patients are screened for functional status when indicated by their condition, including the risk of fall, and if needed, further assessed and treated in the ambulatory care organization, or referred or provided with a referral to appropriate follow-up.
When the need for additional specialized assessments is identified, patients are referred within the ambulatory care organization or to outside services in the community.
Screening and specialized assessments that label the patient “at risk” and are conducted within the ambulatory care organization are completed and documented in the patient’s medical record.

statement: All patients are screened for pain and assessed when pain is present.
elements: Patients are screened for pain, and the screening is documented.

When pain is identified from the initial screening exam, the patient is further assessed and treated as needed in the ambulatory care organization or provided with a referral for further assessment and treatment.
The assessment or referral is documented in the patient medical record.

statement: The ambulatory care organization has a process for obtaining findings from relevant outside assessments and incorporating them into the organization’s patient assessment process.
elements: Relevant findings from assessments performed outside the ambulatory care organization are included in the patient assessment process.
The ambulatory care organization has a process for obtaining and using outside assessment findings.
The ambulatory care organization has a process for when relevant outside assessments are not a­ vailable to the ambulatory care organization.
The ambulatory care organization identifies a time frame sufficient for obtaining relevant outside findings to incorporate into the patient assessment process.

statement: There is an established reassessment process for patients requiring additional services or ongoing care.
elements: The scope and content of reassessments conducted by each clinical discipline are defined in writing and documented in the patient medical record.
Only qualified individuals permitted by licensure, applicable laws and regulations, and/or certification perform reassessments.
The reassessment process for special patient groups and populations is modified to reflect their needs.

statement: The time frames for initial assessments and, as appropriate, reassessments are consistent with each patient’s needs, organizational policy, and accepted professional guidelines.
elements: Time frames for performing assessments are established for all clinical disciplines and services.
Time frames for performing reassessments are established for all clinical disciplines and services.
Patients are assessed within a time frame consistent with their needs and as established by organization policy and accepted professional guidelines.
Patients are reassessed within a time frame consistent with their needs and as established by organization policy and accepted professional guidelines.
Patients are assessed for follow-up when required by their needs.

statement: Laboratory services are available to meet patient needs, and all such services meet applicable local and national standards, laws, and regulations.
elements: Laboratory services meet applicable local and national standards, laws, and regulations.
Laboratory services are available on site or through outside sources to meet the needs related to the ambulatory care organization’s mission and patient population.
Experts in specialized diagnostic areas are contacted when needed.
Outside sources are selected based on an acceptable record and compliance with laws and regulations.

statement: A qualified individual(s) is responsible for managing the laboratory services in the ambulatory care organization, and all laboratory staff have the required credentials to administer, perform, and interpret tests.
elements: The laboratory and other laboratory services throughout the ambulatory care organization are under the direction and oversight of a qualified individual(s).

Responsibilities of the laboratory leader include at least the following: • Developing, implementing, and maintaining policies and procedures • Overseeing the organization’s laboratory services from an administrative perspective • Maintaining any necessary quality control programs • Recommending outside sources of laboratory services • Monitoring and reviewing all laboratory services in the organization, both within and outside the

statement: A qualified individual oversees and supervises point-of-care testing (POCT) in the ambulatory care organization, and trained and competent staff perform the testing.
elements: The person who manages the laboratory services or a designee (or when there are no on-site laboratory services, a qualified individual with the appropriate technical knowledge and experience) oversees and supervises the POCT program.
The ambulatory care organization develops guidelines for acquiring POCT devices/methods.
The ambulatory care organization identifies those staff who perform POCT, and these staff have the required qualifications, training, and competency to perform POCT.
The ambulatory care organization identifies, in writing, the POCT performed in the organization. The organization also identifies all POCT devices and their locations in the facility.
The POCT program includes a defined process for reporting abnormal test results, including critical results.
The POCT program includes maintenance, quality-controlled performance, documentation, and evaluation.
The POCT program is monitored, evaluated, and included in quality improvement activities.

statement: A laboratory safety program is in place, followed, and documented, and compliance with the facility management and infection prevention and control programs is maintained.
elements: A laboratory safety program addresses potential safety risks in the laboratory and other areas outside the laboratory where laboratory services are provided. The program complies with national and international laboratory safety standards and is readily available to all laboratory personnel.

The laboratory safety program is part of the organization’s facility management and quality improvement and patient safety programs and is monitored through regular safety inspections and analysis of the findings to improve the program. The program provides reports to the facility management program at least annually and when any safety events occur.

The laboratory safety and infection prevention and control program is part of the organization’s infection prevention and control program, complies with national and international laboratory infection prevention and control standards, and is readily available to all laboratory personnel. The laboratory safety and infection prevention and control program provides reports to the infection prevention and control program at least annually and when any infection control events occur; it is monitored through regular infection prevention and control inspections and analysis of the findings, which are used to improve the program.
Identified safety risks are addressed by specific processes and/or devices to reduce the safety risks.

Laboratory staff are oriented to safety and infection prevention and control procedures and practices and receive ongoing education, including mandated annual safety training and competency assessment and training for new practices and procedures.

statement: The laboratory uses a coordinated process to reduce the risks of infection because of exposure to infectious diseases and biohazardous materials and waste.
elements: The laboratory has a defined process for reducing the risks of infection.
Infections acquired in the laboratory are reported, as defined in the policy and in compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

The laboratory follows biosafety and infection prevention and control rules for relevant practices, including the following: • Exposures to aerosols and droplets are controlled (for example, when mixing, sonicating, centrifuging, and flaming inoculating loops). • Laboratory coats, gowns, or uniforms are worn to protect street clothes and prevent contamination. Personal protective equipment is provided and used. (See also PCI.5, ME 1.) • Fume hoods and biosafety cabinets are used when required. • Rules govern how to handle laboratory exposure to infectious agents, accidental cuts, needlestick injuries, accidental ingestion, and contact of potentially infectious agents with mucus membranes. These rules include decontamination procedures, whom to contact for emergency treatment, and the location and use of safety equipment. The rules guide biological safety procedures, the use of standard precautions, and the use of eyewash stations and emergency

statement: Laboratory services provided in the organization meet patient and staff needs, are adequately supplied, and properly manage specimens.
elements: The laboratory develops a services and specimens manual that is distributed to all patient care areas.
The ambulatory care organization establishes the expected report time for results, whether performed in house or sent out, and results are reported within a time frame to meet patient needs.
The laboratory establishes reference ranges for each test performed.
Essential reagents and supplies are available, and all reagents are evaluated to ensure accuracy and precision of results.
The laboratory establishes and implements procedures for ordering tests, including required clinical data. The procedures also address the required checks for request completion.

The laboratory establishes and implements procedures for collecting and identifying specimens, including the following: • Patient preparation for specimen collection • Positive patient identification • Quality and quantity of sample • Phlebotomy, sample collection, and labeling procedures • Required checks for adequacy of specimen labeling • Required checks for label/request discrepancies

The laboratory establishes and implements procedures for transporting, storing, and preserving specimens, including the following: • Specimen packing, handling, and transportation • Specimen rejection reasons • Required checks for proper packaging • Required checks for quality and quantity of specimen(s)
The laboratory establishes and implements procedures for requesting the introduction of a new test.

statement: All equipment used for laboratory testing is regularly inspected, maintained, and calibrated, and appropriate records are maintained for these activities.
elements: The laboratory has a defined process for selecting, receiving, installing, and identifying equipment. The process also outlines validating laboratory equipment for its intended use.
The laboratory develops, implements, and documents a program for managing laboratory equipment, including how to select and acquire laboratory equipment.
The program includes an inventory of all laboratory equipment.
Laboratory equipment is inspected and tested when new and according to age, use, and manufacturers’ recommendations thereafter, and the inspections and testing are documented.
Laboratory equipment is calibrated and maintained according to manufacturers’ recommendations, and the calibration and maintenance are documented.

The ambulatory care organization has a system in place for monitoring and acting on laboratory equipment hazard notices, recalls, reportable incidents, problems, and failures. The process also includes the required investigation and follow-up of equipment malfunction or failure.

statement: Quality control procedures for laboratory services are in place, followed, and documented.
elements: The ambulatory care organization establishes and implements a quality control program for the clinical laboratory as per the manufacturers’ instructions. The program identifies the performance and review responsibility. Control specimens are handled and tested in the same manner and by the same laboratory personnel who are testing patient samples.
The program includes validating test methods.
The program includes daily surveillance and documentation of test results. The program specifies the number and frequency of running controls and establishes tolerance limits for results.
The program includes testing reagents, including acquiring the correct reference range when the reagents/methodology change.
The program includes rapidly correcting and documenting deficiencies/unacceptable results.

statement: There is a process for proficiency testing of laboratory services.
elements: The laboratory participates in a proficiency-testing (PT) program or an alternative for all specialty laboratory services and tests. The proficiency program participation ensures the following: • All analytes are covered with PT. • Alternative PT is performed when appropriate. • There are clear instructions for receiving, processing, and reporting PT results. • PT samples are tested by the same personnel handling the patient samples. • PT samples are tested using the same method for testing the patient samples. • PT samples are not referred to another external laboratory for testing. • PT results are not shared with another external laboratory.

For each specialty, subspecialty, analyte, or test, the laboratory’s PT results meet satisfactory performance criteria in accordance with laws and regulations. Unacceptable performance is investigated, and appropriate corrective actions are taken. Corrective actions are implemented and monitored.
The laboratory maintains records of its participation in a PT program. Laboratory management reviews and approves PT records.

statement: Reference/contract laboratories used by the ambulatory care organization are licensed and accredited or certified by a recognized authority.
elements: The ambulatory care organization outlines an inclusive list of send-out tests. The organization describes specimen collection, labeling, handling, transportation, and results reporting of send-out tests.

The ambulatory care organization maintains a copy of the license from a recognized licensing authority for all reference/contract laboratories used by the ambulatory care organization, selected through selection criteria.

The ambulatory care organization maintains a copy of the certificate or letter of accreditation or certification, from a recognized laboratory accreditation or certification program, for all reference/ contract laboratories used by the ambulatory care organization.
The ambulatory care organization maintains documentation that any reference/contract laboratory it uses participates in an outside PT program.

statement: The ambulatory care organization identifies measures for monitoring the quality of the services provided by reference/contract laboratories.
elements: The frequency and type of performance expectation data from reference/contract laboratories are determined by the ambulatory care organization and specified in the contract’s conditions.
The qualified individual responsible for the laboratory or a qualified designee reviews the performance expectation data from reference/contract laboratories.
The responsible individual or qualified designee takes action based on the results.
An annual report of the data from reference/contract laboratories is provided to ambulatory care organization leaders to facilitate management of contracts and contract renewals.

statement: The laboratory has the right space and facilities relevant to the services provided.
elements: The laboratory’s design and location meet applicable local and international regulations.

The laboratory has adequate spaces for patient waiting areas; lavatories; each laboratory activity/ section; storage for reagents, supplies, consumables, samples, waste holding, and records; and administrative and clerical staff.
The laboratory has adequate water taps and sinks for handwashing and washing contaminated equipment.
The laboratory is equipped with adequate electrical outlets and emergency power.
The laboratory has adequate lighting, ventilation, and temperature and humidity controls.
The laboratory corridors are unobstructed and maintain access control and adequate emergency exits.
The laboratory has safety signs that are adequately displayed and distributed.
The laboratory workplace is free of hazards, clutter, and distractions, with clean and well-maintained floors, walls, ceilings, bench tops, and sinks.
The laboratory has conveniently located telephones and other means of communication.

statement: The laboratory defines the format and contents of laboratory reports.
elements: The report identifies the testing laboratory.
The report includes full patient identification.
The report identifies the ordering physician.
The report clearly documents the date and time of specimen collection and the source of the specimen.
The report identifies the reporting date and time.
The report highlights the test result(s) and reference intervals/ranges.
The report documents the condition of the specimen that may limit the test’s adequacy.
The report identifies and highlights the authorized person releasing the report.

statement: The laboratory has a process for correcting or amending reported results.
elements: The process defines report corrections and amendments.
The process describes the format of the corrected report.
The process requires inclusion of the previous result in the corrected report.
The process requires notification of the ordering physician.

statement: Radiology and diagnostic imaging services are available to meet patient needs, and all such services meet applicable local and national standards, laws, and regulations.
elements: Radiology and diagnostic imaging services meet applicable local and national standards, laws, and regulations.
Radiology and diagnostic imaging services meet the needs related to the ambulatory care organization’s mission and patient population.
The ambulatory care organization maintains a roster of experts in specialized diagnostic areas and ensures that the roster is accessible to staff who need it.

Outside sources are selected based on recommendations of the individual responsible for radiology and diagnostic imaging services and have an acceptable record of timely performance and compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

statement: A qualified individual(s) is responsible for managing the radiology and diagnostic imaging services.
elements: One or more qualified radiology specialists direct and supervise radiology and diagnostic imaging services; they read, review, and authorize all radiology reports. A licensed radiology technician carries out radiology services.
Responsibilities for developing, implementing, and maintaining policies and procedures are defined and carried out.
Responsibilities for administrative oversight are defined and carried out.
Responsibilities for maintaining quality control programs are defined and carried out.
Responsibilities for recommending outside sources of radiology and diagnostic imaging services are defined and carried out.
Responsibilities for monitoring and reviewing all radiology and diagnostic imaging services are defined and carried out.

statement: Individuals with proper qualifications and experience perform diagnostic imaging studies, interpret the results, and report the results.
elements: Those individuals who perform diagnostic and imaging studies or direct or supervise the studies are identified.
Properly qualified and experienced staff perform diagnostic and imaging studies.
Properly qualified and experienced staff interpret study results.
Properly qualified and experienced staff verify and report the results of studies.
There is an adequate number of staff to meet patient needs.
Supervisory staff have proper qualifications and experience.
