statement: A radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program for patients, staff, and visitors is in place, is followed, and complies with applicable professional standards, laws, and regulations.
elements: A comprehensive radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program for patients, staff, and visitors is in place, is followed, and complies with applicable professional standards, laws, and regulations. The program covers all areas that use ionizing radiation. Safety measures include the following: • All rooms where ionizing radiation is administered are tested and certified radiation leak proof by the appropriate certifying local authority. • All women in the childbearing period with missed menstruation are checked for the possibility of pregnancy prior to x-ray tests.
Radiology and diagnostic imaging staff are oriented to safety precautions and procedures and receive ongoing education and training for any new procedures, equipment, and hazardous materials.

Safety protective equipment and devices appropriate to the practices and hazards encountered from radiation and diagnostic imaging are available to staff, patients, and visitors, and in the area in which radiology and diagnostic imaging services are provided. Safety measures include, but are not limited to, the following: • Safety warnings are posted on the doors in clear and appropriate locations. • Personnel are monitored for radiation exposure by thermoluminescence dosimeters (TLD) that are regularly checked. • All types of radiation protection aprons are periodically inspected and tested for integrity and effectiveness with documentation.
Radiation safety includes education about dosing and implementation of protocols that identify the maximum dose of radiation for each type of study.

Hazards from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are addressed using industry standards and evidence-based guidelines (for example, identification of safety zones, access restrictions, signage, availability of non-ferromagnetic equipment, and so on).

The radiation and/or diagnostic imaging safety program is part of the organization’s facility management and infection prevention and control programs and provides reports to those programs at least annually and when any safety events and infection control events occur.

statement: Radiology and diagnostic imaging study results are available in a timely way as defined by the ambulatory care organization.
elements: The ambulatory care organization has established the expected report time for radiology and ­diagnostic imaging study results.
The timeliness of reporting of urgent studies is measured.
Radiology and diagnostic imaging study results are reported within a time frame to meet patient needs.

statement: All equipment used to conduct radiology and diagnostic imaging studies is regularly inspected, maintained, and calibrated, and appropriate records are maintained for these activities.
elements: Radiology and diagnostic imaging services develop, implement, and document a program to manage equipment by qualified personnel.
The program identifies how radiology and diagnostic imaging equipment is selected and acquired.
There is a documented inventory of all radiology and diagnostic imaging equipment and their operation and service manuals.
Radiology and diagnostic imaging equipment is inspected and tested when new and according to age, use, and manufacturers’ recommendations.

Radiology and diagnostic imaging equipment is inspected, calibrated, and maintained for proper functioning according to manufacturers’ recommendations. Maintenance and repair records are properly maintained, including corrective actions.
The ambulatory care organization has a system in place for monitoring and acting on radiology and diagnostic imaging equipment hazard notices, recalls, reportable incidents, problems, and failures.

statement: Quality control procedures for the radiology and diagnostic imaging services are in place, followed, validated, and documented.
elements: The ambulatory care organization establishes and implements quality control procedures for the radiology and diagnostic imaging services.
Quality control includes validating test methods.
Quality control includes daily surveillance and documentation of imaging results.
Quality control includes testing reagents and solutions, when used, and documenting test results.
Quality control includes rapidly correcting and documenting when a deficiency is identified.

statement: The ambulatory care organization regularly reviews quality control results for all outside contracted sources of radiology and diagnostic imaging services.
elements: The ambulatory care organization determines the frequency and type of quality control data from outside contracted sources of radiology and diagnostic imaging services.
The qualified individual responsible for radiology and diagnostic imaging quality control or a qualified designee reviews the quality control results from the outside contracted source.
The responsible individual or a qualified designee takes action based on the quality control results.
An annual report of the quality control data from the outside contracted source is provided to ambulatory care organization leaders to facilitate contract management and renewal.

statement: The laboratory has the right space and facilities relevant to the services it provides.
elements: The laboratory’s design and location meet applicable local and international regulations.

The laboratory has adequate spaces for patient waiting areas; lavatories; each laboratory activity/ section; storage for reagents, supplies, consumables, samples, waste holding, and records; and administrative and clerical staff.
The laboratory has adequate water taps and sinks for handwashing and washing contaminated equipment.
The laboratory is equipped with adequate electrical outlets and emergency power.
The laboratory has adequate lighting, ventilation, and temperature and humidity controls.
The laboratory corridors are unobstructed and maintain access control and adequate emergency exits.
Safety signs are adequately displayed and distributed in the laboratory.
The laboratory workplace is free of hazards, clutter, and distractions, with clean and well-maintained floors, walls, ceilings, bench tops, and sinks.
The laboratory has conveniently located telephones and other means of communication.

statement: Sedation and anesthesia services, if provided by the ambulatory care organization, meet professional standards and applicable local and national standards, laws, and regulations.
elements: Sedation and anesthesia services meet professional standards and applicable local and national standards, laws, and regulations.
Sedation and anesthesia services are available to meet patient needs.
Outside sedation and anesthesia sources are selected based on acceptable records of performance and compliance with applicable laws and regulations.
There is a contract in place when the ambulatory care organization uses outside sources for sedation and anesthesia services.

statement: A qualified individual(s) is responsible for managing sedation and anesthesia services.
elements: Sedation and anesthesia services are uniform throughout the ambulatory care organization.
Sedation and anesthesia services are under the direction of one or more qualified individuals.

The qualified individual(s) assumes responsibilities for at least the following: • Developing, implementing, and maintaining policies and procedures • Providing administrative oversight • Maintaining any necessary quality control program • Recommending outside sources of sedation and anesthesia services • Monitoring and reviewing all sedation and anesthesia services

statement: The administration of procedural sedation is standardized throughout the ambulatory care organization.
elements: The administration of procedural sedation is standardized throughout the ambulatory care organization.

Standardization of procedural sedation includes identifying and addressing at least the following: • Areas in the ambulatory care organization where procedural sedation may occur • Special qualifications or skills of staff involved in the procedural sedation process (See also SQE.2,

statement: Practitioners responsible for procedural sedation and individuals responsible for monitoring patients receiving sedation are qualified.
elements: A Saudi board-certified or equivalent anesthesiologist responsible for providing procedural sedation is competent in at least the following: • Techniques and various modes of sedation • Pharmacology of sedation drugs and the use of reversal agents • Monitoring requirements • Response to complications (See also SQE.2, ME 1; SQE.4; SQE.5; and SQE.8.)

A Saudi board-certified or equivalent anesthesiologist responsible for patient monitoring during procedural sedation is competent in at least the following: • Monitoring requirements • Response to complications • Use of reversal agents • Recovery criteria (See also SQE.2, ME 1; SQE.4; and SQE.5.)
Procedural sedation competencies for all staff involved in sedation are documented in the personnel files.

statement: Procedural sedation is administered and monitored according to professional practice guidelines.
elements: Written policies and procedure describe the presedation assessment process and related documentation, including at least the following to evaluate risk and appropriateness of procedural sedation for the patient: • Identifying any airway problems that may influence the type of sedation used • Evaluating at-risk patients for appropriateness of procedural sedation • Planning the type and level of sedation that the patient will need based on the procedure being

statement: The risks, benefits, and alternatives related to procedural sedation are discussed with the patient, their family, or those who make decisions for the patient.
elements: The patient, family, and/or decision-makers are educated on the risks, benefits, and alternatives of procedural sedation.
The patient, family, and/or decision-makers are educated about postprocedure analgesia.
A qualified individual provides and documents the education.

statement: A qualified individual conducts a preanesthesia assessment and preinduction assessment.
elements: The ambulatory care organization has a policy requiring that each patient receives a preanesthesia assessment to evaluate the anesthesia’s risk and appropriateness for the patient. The assessment includes the following: • Identifying any airway problems • Selecting the anesthesia, and planning anesthesia care • Safely administering the anesthetic based on patient assessment, identified risks, and type of

statement: Each patient’s anesthesia care is planned and documented, and the anesthesia and technique used are documented in the patient’s medical record.
elements: A Saudi board-certified or equivalent anesthesiologist performs anesthesia as required.
The anesthesia care of each patient is planned and documented in the patient’s medical record.
The anesthesia agent, dose (when applicable), and anesthetic technique are documented in the patient’s medical record.
The anesthesiologist and/or nurse anesthetist and anesthesia assistants are identified in the patient’s medical record.

statement: The risks, benefits, and alternatives related to anesthesia are discussed with the patient, their family, or those who make decisions for the patient.
elements: The patient, family, and/or decision-makers are educated on the risks, benefits, and alternatives of anesthesia.
The patient, family, and/or decision-makers are educated before the procedure about options for managing postoperative pain.
The anesthesiologist or another qualified individual provides and documents the education.

statement: Each patient’s physiological status during anesthesia and surgery is monitored according to professional practice guidelines and documented in the patient’s medical record.
elements: There is a policy describing the intraprocedural/operative monitoring of patients with or without anesthesia or sedation.
The frequency and type of monitoring during anesthesia and surgery are based on the patient’s preanesthesia status, the anesthesia, and the surgical procedure.
Monitoring of the patient’s physiological status is consistent with professional practice.
Monitoring results are documented in the patient’s medical record.

statement: Each patient’s postanesthesia status is monitored and documented, and the patient is discharged from the recovery area by a qualified individual or by using established criteria.
elements: There is a policy describing how patients are received and discharged from the recovery room.
A Saudi board-certified or equivalent anesthesiologist monitors patients during postanesthesia recovery.
Monitoring findings are documented in the patient’s medical record.
A Saudi board-certified or equivalent anesthesiologist discharges patients from the postanesthesia unit or discontinues recovery monitoring.
The time recovery is started and the time the recovery phase is complete are documented in the patient’s medical record.

statement: Each patient’s surgical care is planned and documented based on the results of the assessment.
elements: Before the procedure, the responsible physician documents in the patient’s medical record the assessment information used to develop and support the planned invasive procedure.
The responsible physician plans and documents each patient’s surgical care based on the assessment information.
Before the procedure, the responsible physician documents the preoperative diagnosis and planned procedure in the patient’s medical record.

statement: The risks, benefits, and alternatives are discussed with the patient and their family or those who make decisions for the patient.
elements: The patient, family, and decision-makers are educated on the risks, benefits, potential complications, and alternatives related to the planned surgical procedure.
The education includes the need for, risk and benefits of, and alternatives to blood and blood product use.
The patient’s surgeon or other qualified individual provides and documents the education.

statement: Information about the surgical procedure is documented in the patient’s medical record to facilitate continuing care.
elements: Surgical reports, templates, or operative progress notes include at least the following: • Postoperative diagnosis • Names of operating surgeon and assistants • Procedures performed and descriptions of each procedure’s findings • Perioperative complications, if any • Surgical specimens sent for examination, if any • Amount of blood loss and/or transfused blood, if any • Registry numbers of all implantable devices, if any • Date, time, and signature of the responsible physician
The ambulatory care organization identifies information that may routinely be recorded in other areas of the medical record.
The surgical report, template, or operative progress note is available immediately after surgery before the patient is transferred to the next level of care.

statement: Patient care after surgery is planned and documented.
elements: The postsurgical care provided by medical, nursing, and others meets the patient’s immediate postsurgical needs.
The responsible surgeon documents the postsurgical plan of care in the patient’s medical record.
When indicated by a change in the patient’s needs, the postsurgical plan of care is updated or revised based on the patient’s reassessment by the health care practitioners.

statement: Surgical care that includes implanting a medical device is planned with special consideration of how standard processes and procedures must be modified.
elements: The ambulatory care organization identifies the types of implantable medical devices in its scope of services.

Policies and practices include special factors such as the following: • The selection of devices based on current science and research • The presence of implants in the operating theatre and/or other setting(s) where surgical/invasive

statement: The ambulatory care organization provides care and treatment to all patients, using uniform care processes that follow applicable laws and regulations.
elements: The organization’s department/service leaders collaborate to provide uniform care processes.
When similar care is provided in more than one place in the organization or more than one site, care delivery is uniform.
The provision of uniform care reflects local and regional laws and regulations.

The provision of uniform care meets the following requirements: • Access to and appropriateness of care and treatment do not depend on the patient’s ability to pay or the source of payment. • Within the organization’s defined hours of operation, access to appropriate care and treatment by qualified practitioners does not depend on the time of day or day of week. • Acuity of the patient’s condition determines the resources allocated to meet the patient’s needs.

statement: An individualized plan of care is developed, revised when indicated by a change in the patient’s condition, and documented for each patient.
elements: The attending physician develops the plan of care based on patient assessment, including history, physical exam, laboratory results, consult notes, and other pertinent patient information obtained by the nurse and other disciplines participating in the care and investigations, as applicable.
The care plan is designed to achieve desired outcomes specified as measurable goals.
The patient and, when appropriate, their family are involved in the planned care.
The planned care for a continuing care patient is reviewed during every visit based on the outcome measures and revised when indicated by a change in the patient’s condition.
The attending physician provides and documents the planned care for the patient in the patient’s medical record.

statement: Clinical practice guidelines and related clinical pathways and/or clinical protocols as well as other evidence- based recommendations are used to guide patient assessment and treatment and reduce unwanted variation.
elements: The leaders of the ambulatory care organization collaboratively set criteria to select guidelines, clinical pathways, and/or clinical protocols.

The leaders of the ambulatory care organization follow the process described by clinical practice guidelines, clinical pathways, and/or clinical protocols relevant to the ambulatory care organization’s population and mission. The guidelines, pathways, and/or protocols are as follows: • Selected from among those applicable to the ambulatory care organization’s services and patients

statement: Professional practice guidelines, laws, and regulations guide the care of high-risk patients and the provision of high-risk services.
elements: Ambulatory care organization leaders identify high-risk patients and services.

When the ambulatory care organization provides high-risk services, leaders establish and implement guidelines and procedures for those services and for the care of high-risk patients, including at least the following: • Care of emergency patients • Care of patients with a communicable disease (See also PCI.5.) • Care of immunosuppressed patients • Care of patients with emotional or psychiatric disorders • Care of patients receiving dialysis • Care of patients receiving radiation therapy • Care of patients receiving chemotherapy • Care of patients in restraints • Care of vulnerable patient populations, including frail elderly, dependent children, and patients

statement: Clinical guidelines and procedures are established and implemented for the handling, use, and administration of blood and blood products.
elements: An individual with education, knowledge, and expertise oversees the administration of blood and blood products.
Clinical guidelines and procedures are established and implemented for the handling, use, and administration of blood and blood products.

Clinical guidelines and procedures address the processes for the following: • Patient consent for administration (See also PFR.4.1, ME 3.) • Procurement of blood from the blood bank or blood storage area • Patient identification • Blood administration • Patient monitoring • Identification of and response to signs of potential transfusion reactions (See also COP.2.1 and

statement: The ambulatory care organization establishes and implements a program for the safe use of lasers and other optical radiation devices.
elements: The ambulatory care organization’s program for the safe use of lasers and optical radiation devices is based on industry standards and professional guidelines and complies with applicable laws and regulations.
A qualified individual with the appropriate training and experience oversees and supervises the laser and optical radiation safety program.
All staff involved in the use of lasers and optical radiation devices receive safety training and continuing education; the training and ongoing education are documented.

The ambulatory care organization establishes and implements administrative and engineering controls for the laser and optical radiation safety program to promote safety and prevent injury for patients and staff.

Personal protective equipment appropriate to the type of lasers and optical radiation devices and type of procedures is available for staff and patients, and staff use it correctly and ensure that patients are protected during procedures.

The ambulatory care organization has processes for maintenance of the lasers and optical radiation devices and routine calibration and alignment checks of the lasers, which are done by qualified and trained individuals.

statement: The ambulatory care organization reports adverse events and adverse health effects resulting from the use of lasers and other optical radiation devices and implements and monitors action plans to prevent recurrence.
elements: The laser safety and optical radiation program is part of the organization’s facility management program and provides reports to the facility management program at least annually and when any safety events occur.

The laser safety and optical radiation program is part of the organization’s infection prevention and control program and provides reports to the infection prevention and control program at least annually and when any infection control events occur.

When adverse health effects result from the use of lasers and/or optical radiation devices, the ambulatory care organization reports adverse events and identifies and implements action plans to prevent recurrence.

statement: Resuscitation services are available throughout the ambulatory care organization.
elements: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a policy and procedure outlining the resuscitation process.
Basic life support services are available during all hours of operation and throughout all areas of the ambulatory care organization.
The role of staff involved in the cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) process is clearly defined in the policy and monitored for implementation.
The ambulatory care organization has a process to provide or obtain advanced life support when needed.
Medical equipment and medications for resuscitation are standardized and available for use based on the needs of the population served.
Qualified staff check the crash cart on every shift.
All staff who provide patient care, including contracted physicians and health care practitioners, are trained to provide basic life support services.

statement: When patients remain in the ambulatory care organization for extended periods, food is available that is appropriate for the patient’s nutritional status and consistent with their clinical care.
elements: A variety of food choices or nutrition is available when patients are in the organization for extended periods of time.
Orders are based on patients’ nutritional status, clinical care needs, and dietary preferences, as appropriate.
When families provide food, they are educated about the patients’ dietary limitations.

statement: Patients at nutritional risk receive nutrition therapy.
elements: A qualified individual provides further assessment for patients identified as at nutritional risk through screening.
Nutrition therapy is planned for patients at nutritional risk.
When the ambulatory care organization provides the nutritional therapy, the patient’s progress is monitored and recorded in their medical record.
If the patient has been referred to an outside source, the referral is documented in the patient’s medical record.

statement: Patients are supported in managing pain effectively.
elements: Based on the scope of services provided, the ambulatory care organization has processes to identify patients in pain.
When pain is an expected result of planned treatments, procedures, or examinations, patients are informed about the likelihood of pain and options for pain management.
Patients in pain receive care according to pain management guidelines and according to patient goals for pain management, including the use of nonpharmacologic interventions and medication.
Based on the scope of services provided, the ambulatory care organization has processes to communicate with and to educate patients and families about pain.
Based on the scope of services provided, the ambulatory care organization has processes to educate staff about pain and pain management strategies, including nonpharmacologic interventions.

statement: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process to improve accuracy of patient identification.
elements: Patients are identified using two patient identifiers, including full name as in the identification document and unique medical record number, and identification should not use the patient’s examination or procedure room number or location in the ambulatory care organization.
Patients are identified before performing diagnostic procedures, providing treatments, withdrawing blood, administering medications, and performing surgery and other procedures.
The ambulatory care organization ensures correct identification of patients in special circumstances, such as patients without identification or two patients with the same name.
Patients are actively involved in the process of patient identification.

statement: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process to improve the effectiveness of verbal and/or telephone communication among caregivers.
elements: The receiver documents and reads back the complete verbal order, which is confirmed by the individual giving the order.
The receiver documents and reads back the complete telephone order, which is confirmed by the individual giving the order.
The receiver documents and reads back the complete test result, which is confirmed by the individual giving the result.

statement: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process for reporting critical results of diagnostic tests.
elements: The ambulatory care organization has defined critical values for each type of diagnostic test.
The ambulatory care organization has identified by whom and to whom critical results of diagnostic tests are reported.
The process involves the receiver writing down and reading back the result to the result provider.
The read-back process and the physician’s intervention are documented in the patient’s medical record.
The ambulatory care organization develops a process for contacting patients who had already left the center when critical test results were reported.

statement: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process for handover communication.
elements: Standardized critical content is communicated between health care practitioners during handovers of patient care.
Standardized methods, forms, or tools support a consistent and complete handover process.
The ambulatory care organization tracks and uses data from handover communications to improve approaches to safe handover communication. Goal 3: Improve the Safety of High-Alert Medications

statement: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process to improve the safety of high-alert medications.
elements: The ambulatory care organization has a list of all high-alert medications, including look-alike/sound- alike medications, developed from organization-specific data.

The ambulatory care organization implements strategies to improve the safety of high-alert medications, which may include specific storage, prescribing, preparation, administration, or monitoring processes.
The location, labeling, and storage of high-alert medications, including look-alike/sound-alike medications, are uniform throughout the ambulatory care organization.

statement: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process to manage the safe use of concentrated electrolytes.
elements: The ambulatory care organization has a process that prevents inadvertent administration of concentrated electrolytes.
Concentrated electrolytes are present only in patient care areas identified as clinically necessary.
Concentrated electrolytes in patient care areas are clearly labeled and stored in a manner that promotes safe use. Goal 4: Ensure Correct-Site, Correct-Procedure,

statement: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process for the preoperative verification and surgical/invasive procedure site marking.
elements: The ambulatory care organization uses a checklist or other process to document, before the procedure, that the informed consent is appropriate to the procedure; that the correct site, correct procedure, and correct patient are identified; and that all documents and medical technology, instruments, and implants needed are on hand, correct, and functional.

The ambulatory care organization uses an instantly recognizable mark for surgical/invasive procedure site identification that is consistent throughout the organization and surgical site marking is performed for multiple organs, laterality, and different levels.
The person performing the surgical/invasive procedure marks the site and involves the patient in the marking process.

statement: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process for the time-out immediately before the surgical/invasive procedure and for the sign-out after the procedure.
elements: The time-out is done immediately before the start of the procedure with all team members present, including surgeon, anesthesiologist, and circulating nurse.

During the time-out, the team agrees on the following components and clarifies any unanswered questions or confusion: • Correct patient identity (See also IPSG.1.) • Correct procedure to be done • Correct surgical/invasive procedure site

Before the patient leaves the area in which the surgical/invasive procedure was performed, the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist, including a sign-out, is conducted, and a member of the team, typically a nurse, verbally confirms the following components of the sign-out: • Name of the surgical/invasive procedure that was recorded/written • Completion of instrument, sponge, and needle counts (as applicable) • Labeling of specimens (when specimens are present during the sign-out process, labels are read

statement: The ambulatory care organization adopts and implements evidence-based hand-hygiene guidelines to reduce the risk of health care–associated infections.
elements: The ambulatory care organization has adopted currently published, evidence-based hand-hygiene guidelines.
The ambulatory care organization implements an effective hand-hygiene program throughout the organization and monitors compliance with hand hygiene.
Handwashing and hand-disinfection procedures are used in accordance with hand-hygiene guidelines throughout the ambulatory care organization.
The ambulatory care organization provides handwashing and hand-disinfection facilities to meet its needs.

statement: Not applicable to ambulatory care organizations.
The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process to reduce the risk of patient harm resulting from falls for the organization’s patient population.
elements: The ambulatory care organization implements a process for screening patients whose condition, diagnosis, situation, or location may put them at risk for falls and uses screening tools/methods appropriate for the patients served.

When fall risk is identified from the screening process, measures and/or interventions are implemented to reduce fall risk for those patients identified at risk, and the screening and interventions are documented.
The ambulatory care organization identifies locations and situations that present a risk for falls for patients and implements measures and/or interventions to mitigate those risks.

statement: Medication use in the ambulatory care organization is organized to meet patient needs, is appropriate to the organization’s mission and services, and complies with applicable laws and regulations.
elements: Medications available in the organization for prescribing and use are identified in a list and appropriate to the organization’s mission, patient needs, and services.
The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a program to guide medication management and use that meets applicable laws and regulations.

Health care practitioners involved in ordering, dispensing, administering, and patient-monitoring processes are included in the development and ongoing evaluation of the medication management and use program in accordance with local laws and regulations.

The program addresses the following as appropriate to the organization: • Planning • Selection and procurement • Traceability • Storage • Ordering • Preparing and dispensing • Administration • Monitoring • Evaluation (See also IPSG.2 and IPSG.3.)
Qualified staff who have a valid registration with the Saudi Commission for Health Specialties manage medication use processes.
The ambulatory care organization establishes an interdisciplinary mechanism for overseeing and monitoring medication management processes.

statement: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a program for prudent use of antibiotics based on the principles of antibiotic stewardship.
elements: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a program for antibiotic stewardship appropriate to its size and involves a multidisciplinary team, including, as applicable, physicians, nurses, pharmacists, trainees, patients, families, and others.
The program is based on scientific evidence, accepted practice guidelines, and local laws and regulations.

The program follows guidelines for optimal use of antibiotic therapy for treating infections, including guidelines for empiric and therapeutic use of antibiotics and proper use of prophylactic antibiotic therapy.
The program includes educating staff, patients, families, and the community, as appropriate to the organization’s size and services, about use and misuse of antibiotics.

statement: There is a method for overseeing the ambulatory care organization’s medication list, availability of medications, and medication use.
elements: There is an updated list of medications stocked in the ambulatory care organization or, if applicable, readily available from outside sources.

The process to develop the list (unless determined by regulation or an authority outside the ambulatory care organization) includes representation from all those who prescribe and manage medications in the ambulatory care organization.
Criteria guide decisions to add or to remove medications from the list.
The list is reviewed at least annually based on safety and effectiveness of use information.
There is an updated list of the signatures of medical staff who are authorized to prescribe medications, along with their prescribing privileges.

statement: Medications, including emergency medications and medications that require special handling, are properly and safely stored.
elements: Medications are stored under conditions suitable for product stability and based on the manufacturers’ guidelines, including medications stored on ambulances (as applicable).
All medication and vaccine refrigerators are connected to an alternate power source, and a temperature log is always maintained.
The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process for handling medications and vaccines when temperature monitoring indicates out of range.
Controlled substances are accurately accounted for according to applicable laws and regulations.
Additional medications requiring special handling are controlled, labeled, and stored according to manufacturers’ recommendations.
Medications, chemicals used to prepare medications, and open multidose containers are accurately labeled with contents, opening date, time, expiry date, staff initials, and warnings.
There are written guidelines for ensuring the stability of sterile multidose vials, containers, vaccines, and multidose medications.
All medication storage areas are periodically inspected to ensure proper storage.
Medications are protected from loss, personal use, or theft throughout the ambulatory care organization.

The ambulatory care organization has a written policy and procedure managing expired and nearly expired medications, including the following: • Identifying, collecting, and returning the nearly expired medications • Documenting the return of expired medications to the supplier or manufacturer and keeping a

statement: The ambulatory care organization identifies a current list of medications taken by the patient at home and reviews the list against all new medication prescribed or dispensed in the organization.
elements: The patient’s medical record lists current medications taken at home as an outpatient, and this information is made available to the patient’s health care practitioners and the pharmacy, as applicable.
New medications prescribed or dispensed to the patient are compared to the list of medications taken by the patient at home.

New medications prescribed or dispensed are reviewed for the following: • The appropriateness of the drug, dose, frequency, and route of administration • Therapeutic duplication • Existing or potential allergies or sensitivities • Existing or potential interactions between the medication and other medications or food
Computer programs and print reference materials, when used to cross-check drugs for drug-drug interactions and allergies, are current.

statement: Medications prescribed and/or administered in the ambulatory care organization follow standardized processes to ensure patient safety.
elements: Qualified individuals, as identified and permitted by the organization and relevant licensure, laws, and regulations, prescribe and/or administer medications.

The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a written document that defines the complete elements of a medication prescription/order, and in addition to the complete elements, the order should cover accurate patient demographics including the following: • Name and medical record number • Age • Allergy status • For all pediatric orders, patient weight (so dosage is adjusted accordingly)
The prescription of narcotics and controlled medications follows Saudi Ministry of Health laws and regulations.
There is a uniform system for dispensing and distributing medications available in the most ready-to- administer form possible.

The ambulatory care organization evaluates the appropriateness of prescriptions before dispensing, including the following: • Allergies, indications, dosage, frequency, route of administrations, therapeutic duplication, and possible interactions are considered. • There is an updated medication profile for each patient treated in the emergency department and/or day procedure. • The pharmacist or a physician does the review. • The reviewer discusses any concerns in the process with the prescriber before medication dispensing. • The medication, dosage amount, and route of administration are verified with the prescription or order.

Medication preparation areas comply with infection prevention and control measures and safe practices, including the following: • Preparation areas and surfaces are clean and tidy. • Preparation areas are equipped with a wash sink, antiseptic soap, and a sharps container of appropriate size. • Medications are prepared using aseptic technique, and staff qualified to prepare medications have documented evidence of training in aseptic technique. • Medications that are prepared and not immediately used are labeled with the medication name, dose, route of administration, and patient’s identifiers.
Medications prescribed and/or administered in the ambulatory care organization are noted in the patient’s medical record.
The medical records of patients on multiple medications list their current medications, including medication name, dose, frequency, and route of administration, as well as any herbs or supplements.
All prescriptions given to patients should not include any abbreviations (refer to MOI.4).

statement: Medications are monitored for patient adherence, clinical effectiveness, and adverse medication effects.
elements: Patient adherence in taking medications and medication effectiveness are monitored.
Medication adverse effects on patients are monitored and documented.

The ambulatory care organization implements a written process to respond to actual or potential adverse drug events and significant adverse drug reactions (ADRs), including the following: • Defining significant ADRs and time frame for reporting • Intensively analyzing all significant ADRs • Notifying treating physicians of the analysis results • Flagging patient’s medical record for significant ADRs • Giving patient appropriate medical care for ADR • Reporting significant ADRs to the relevant authorities per laws and regulations
Any newly discovered allergies are documented in the patient’s medication profile.

statement: The ambulatory care organization establishes and implements a process for acting on medication errors and near misses.
elements: The ambulatory care organization defines medication error and near miss.
The ambulatory care organization establishes and implements a process for reporting and acting on medication errors and near misses, including the time frame for reporting and the reporting format.
The ambulatory care organization identifies those individuals accountable for acting on medication error and near miss reports.

The ambulatory care organization analyzes medication errors, conducts a root-cause analysis for all significant medication errors and near misses, and transforms the data from the analysis into information to improve medication use processes and prevent similar medication errors.

statement: The ambulatory care organization provides education that supports patient and family participation in care decisions and care processes.
elements: The ambulatory care organization plans education consistent with its mission, services, and patient population.
There is an established structure or mechanism for education throughout the ambulatory care organization.
The education structure and resources are effectively organized.

statement: Each patient’s educational needs related to immediate and ongoing health care needs are assessed and recorded in their medical record.
elements: The educational needs of the patient and family are assessed.
Educational needs assessment findings are recorded in the patient’s medical record.
All staff uniformly record patient education.

statement: The patient’s and family’s ability to learn and willingness to learn are assessed.
elements: The patient’s literacy, including health care literacy, education level, and language, are assessed and documented.
The patient’s emotional barriers and motivations are assessed.
The patient’s physical and cognitive limitations are assessed.
The assessment findings are used to plan the education.

statement: Education methods include the patient’s and family’s values and preferences and allow sufficient interaction among the patient, family, and staff for learning to occur.
elements: The education process considers the patient’s and family’s values and learning preferences.
There is a process to verify that patients and families receive and understand the education provided, and the provided education is evaluated for effectiveness.
Those who provide education encourage patients and their families to ask questions and speak up as active participants.
Verbal information is reinforced with written material that is related to the patient’s needs and consistent with the patient’s and family’s learning preferences.

statement: Health care practitioners caring for the patient collaborate to provide education and have the knowledge, time, and communication skills to do so.
elements: Patient and family education is provided collaboratively when indicated.

Patients’ and families’ education is based on their health care needs, which include, but are not necessarily limited to, the nature of their disease, necessary treatments, infection prevention and control practices, safe use of medications, diet and nutrition, medical equipment use, and preoperative and postoperative care.
Those who provide education have the subject knowledge to do so.
Those who provide education have adequate time to do so.
Those who provide education have the communication skills to do so.

statement: The ambulatory care organization is responsible for developing and implementing processes that support patients’ and families’ rights during care.
elements: The ambulatory care organization works collaboratively to protect and advance patient and family rights.
The leaders develop a statement of patient rights and responsibilities and support its implementation.
The ambulatory care organization understands patient and family rights as identified in laws and regulations.
The ambulatory care organization understands the patient and family rights in relation to the cultural practices of the community or individual patients served.

The ambulatory care organization respects the right of the patient, and in some circumstances the right of the patient’s family, to have the prerogative to determine what information regarding their care would be provided to family or others, and under what circumstances.
All staff are knowledgeable about patient rights and can explain their responsibilities in protecting patient rights.

statement: The ambulatory care organization seeks to reduce physical, language, cultural, and other barriers to access and delivery of services.
elements: The department/service leaders and staff of the ambulatory care organization identify the most common barriers in its patient population.
The department/service leaders develop and implement a process to overcome or limit barriers for patients seeking care.
The department/service leaders develop and implement a process to limit the impact of barriers on the delivery of services.

statement: The ambulatory care organization provides care that respects the patient’s dignity, personal values, and beliefs, and the patient’s rights to privacy and confidentiality of care and information are respected and protected.
elements: Staff provide care that respects the patient’s values and beliefs and preserves the patient’s dignity.
Staff members identify patient expectations and needs for privacy and confidentiality during care and treatment.
A patient’s expressed need for privacy is respected for all clinical interviews, examinations, and procedures/treatments and during transportation.
Confidentiality of patient information is maintained according to laws and regulations.
Patients are requested to grant permission for the release of information not covered by laws and regulations.

statement: Patients are protected from verbal abuse and physical assault, and vulnerable populations are identified and protected from additional risks.
elements: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process to protect all patients from abuse and assault.
The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process to identify vulnerable patient groups at additional risk and protect them from these risks to safety.
Staff members understand their responsibilities in the protection processes.

statement: The ambulatory care organization provides care that respects patients’ and families’ personal values and beliefs and supports their rights to participate in the care process.
elements: Patients’ values and beliefs are identified.

Processes that address the following are developed and implemented to support and promote patient and family participation in care processes: • The right to refuse or discontinue care • The right to withhold resuscitation services and to forgo or withdraw life-sustaining treatments • The right to receive appropriate assessment and management of pain (See also COP.7.) • The right to access and participate in the organization’s process to receive and act on complaints and to resolve conflicts and differences of opinion about care (See also GLD.10.)
Department/service leaders and clinical staff are involved in developing the processes that support patient and family rights to participate in the care process.

Staff are trained on at least the following: • The policies and procedures • How to identify and respectfully support a patient’s values and beliefs • Their role in supporting patients’ and families’ rights to participate in the care process (See also

statement: The ambulatory care organization identifies patient and family responsibilities in the care process.
elements: The organization identifies patient and family responsibilities in the care process.
The process to identify patient and family responsibilities involves patients, their families, health care practitioners, and others, as appropriate.

The responsibilities identified include at least the following: • Patient’s full disclosure of their health information • Patient’s cooperation during examinations and procedures • Patient’s respect for the organization’s staff and other patients • Patient’s respect for the organization’s policies and procedures on smoking, infection prevention

statement: All patients are informed about their rights and responsibilities in a manner and language they can understand.
elements: The leaders ensure that patient rights and responsibilities are available to patients and families and that patients are informed about their rights and responsibilities in a manner they can understand.
Information about patient rights and responsibilities is provided in writing to each patient when registering for the first time.
The statement of patient rights and responsibilities is always posted or otherwise available from staff.
The organization has a process to inform patients of their rights and responsibilities when written communication is not effective or appropriate.

statement: Patient informed consent is obtained through a process defined by the ambulatory care organization and carried out by trained staff in a manner and language that the patient can understand.
elements: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a clearly defined informed consent process.
Designated staff are trained in the informed consent process and obtain consent in a manner and language that the patient understands.
Patients give informed consent consistent with the process.
When the organization uses a general consent for treatment, patients are aware of those tests, procedures, and treatments that require separate informed consent.
Informed consent is uniformly recorded.
Each patient and their family are educated about giving informed consent, participating in the care process, and understanding any financial implications of care choices.

statement: Informed consent is obtained before surgery, anesthesia, procedural sedation, use of blood and blood products, and other high-risk treatments and procedures.
elements: Informed consent is obtained before surgical or invasive procedures.
Informed consent is obtained before anesthesia and procedural sedation.
Informed consent is obtained before the use of blood and blood products.
Informed consent is obtained before photographing the patient’s body parts, even if deemed critical for care.
Informed consent is obtained before involving the patient in a research project.
The ambulatory care organization develops and regularly updates a list of procedures and conditions requiring informed consent.
Informed consent is obtained before additional and/or other high-risk procedures and treatments.
The identity of the individual providing the information to the patient and family is noted in the patient’s medical record.

The physician/dentist performing the procedure conducts the informed consent process, which includes explaining the nature of the procedure, the benefits and risks of the procedure, alternative modalities, and the risks of not undergoing the procedure.
A qualified physician/dentist conducts the informed consent process for surgery/procedure.

statement: Patients and families receive adequate information about the illness, proposed treatment(s), and health care practitioners so that they can make care decisions.
elements: Patients are informed of the following information: • Patient’s condition • Proposed treatment(s) • Name of the person(s) providing the treatment • Potential benefits and drawbacks • Possible alternatives • Likelihood of success • Possible problems related to recovery • Possible results of nontreatment (See also PFR.4.1, ASC.3.3, ASC.5.1, and ASC.7.1.)
Patients know the identities of the physicians and other health care practitioners responsible for their care.
The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process to respond to a patient’s request for additional information on the health care practitioner responsible for their care.
Patients are supported in discussing their plan of care with the physician and having all their questions answered.
Patients are provided with all the information regarding the identity, professional status, and contact information of their treating physician.

statement: The ambulatory care organization establishes a process, within the context of existing law and culture, for when others can grant consent.
elements: The ambulatory care organization develops and implements a process for when others can grant informed consent.
The process respects law, culture, and custom.
Individuals other than the patient granting consent are noted in the patient’s medical record.

statement: The ambulatory care organization leaders develop and implement a policy and procedure on the patient’s right to voice their complaints and concerns.
elements: Patient complaints are resolved in a time frame described in the policy.
The ambulatory care organization assigns a staff member responsible for managing complaints.
Patient satisfaction surveys are conducted at least quarterly.
Data collected from surveys and complaints are analyzed and trended, and the information collected is used for improvement and integrated into the quality and safety program.

statement: The ambulatory care organization assigns an individual(s) to manage the organization’s facility management program and ensures compliance with relevant laws, regulations, building and fire safety codes, and facility inspection requirements.
elements: Ambulatory care organization leaders assign a full-time or part-time individual(s) to manage the organization’s facility management program and coordinate improvements with the quality and patient safety program.

Ambulatory care organization leaders establish an interdisciplinary team to oversee and monitor the facility management and safety program, which includes plans for emergency management, utility systems, hazardous materials, fire safety, medical equipment, building safety and security.
Ambulatory care organization leaders understand national and local laws, regulations, building and fire safety codes, and other requirements that apply to the organization’s facilities.

Ambulatory care organization leaders implement the national and local standards, laws, regulations, building and fire safety codes, environmental protection standards, recommendations of professional centers, and other requirements or approved alternatives.
Ambulatory care organization leaders ensure that the organization meets the conditions of facility reports or citations from inspections by national and local authorities.

All facility-related safety incidents are thoroughly investigated and managed in accordance with organizational procedures. Sentinel events associated with facility safety are reviewed and acted upon following the organization’s sentinel event policy.

statement: When planning for demolition, construction, or renovation, the ambulatory care organization conducts a preconstruction risk assessment.
elements: When planning for demolition, construction, or renovation, the ambulatory care organization conducts a preconstruction risk assessment (PCRA) for at least the following: • Air quality • Infection prevention and control (Infection Control Risk Assessment [ICRA]) • Utilities, such as water and power • Fire hazards, such as smoking • Noise • Vibration • Hazardous materials • Emergency response, such as response to codes • Other hazards that affect care, treatment, and services
The ambulatory care organization acts based on its assessment to minimize risks during demolition, construction, and renovation.
The ambulatory care organization ensures that contractor compliance is monitored, enforced, and documented.

statement: The ambulatory care organization plans and implements a program to provide a safe physical facility through inspection and planning to reduce risks.
elements: The ambulatory care organization has a program to provide a safe physical facility and maintains adequate and complete documentation for the facility management and safety program.

The ambulatory care organization’s building and its surroundings are hazard free. In hazardous areas, required hazard controls are in place (for example, hooded exhaust and safe evacuation of fumes and dust in casting area of dental laboratory).
The ambulatory care organization has a documented, accurate inspection of its physical facilities, which is conducted by an interdisciplinary team at least four times per year and updated annually.
The ambulatory care organization’s safety management program includes the regular inspection, testing, and maintenance of all the program’s operating components.

The ambulatory care organization has an ongoing program to monitor data on incidents, injuries, and other events for corrective actions and to further plan, prevent recurrences, and reduce risks to ensure a safer physical facility.
The ambulatory care organization plans and budgets for upgrading or replacing systems, buildings, or components needed for the continued operation of a safe, secure, and effective facility.

The ambulatory care organization implements measures to ensure a safe, aesthetically appealing environment, including but not limited to the following: adequate parking space, waiting areas, and toilets; cleanliness and tidiness at all times; no broken furniture or scratched or distorted walls; maintenance of an ambient temperature between 20° and 24.4° Celsius; and use of nonirritant air freshener to control unwanted odor.

statement: The ambulatory care organization plans and implements a program to provide a secure environment for patients, families, staff, and visitors.
elements: The ambulatory care organization has a program to provide a secure environment, including monitoring and securing areas identified as security risks. The program ensures that trained security personnel are available in the organization according to its size and design complexity, equipment and data are secured, and patient privacy is respected.
The program ensures that all staff, contract workers, and vendors are identified.

All security risk areas and restricted areas are identified, documented, monitored, and kept secure by security personnel or security systems. Patient and staff files are accessible only to authorized persons.

statement: The ambulatory care organization has a program for the inventory, handling, storage, use, control, and disposal of hazardous materials and waste.
elements: Hazardous materials and wastes are identified in the ambulatory care organization.

Hazardous materials and wastes are safely managed and controlled through the hazardous materials and waste program. The ambulatory care organization makes a continuous effort to reduce hazardous materials.
The hazardous materials and waste program includes the following: • Inventory of hazardous materials and waste that includes the material, quantity, and location,

statement: The ambulatory care organization develops, maintains, and evaluates a program for disaster preparedness to respond to internal and external emergencies and disasters that can occur in the organization and/or community.
elements: The ambulatory care organization has identified major internal and external emergencies and disasters, such as community emergencies and natural or other disasters, that pose significant risks of occurring, considering the ambulatory care organization’s geographic location.

The ambulatory care organization establishes and implements a program for disaster preparedness that identifies its response to internal and external disasters, including the following: • Determining the type, likelihood, and consequences of hazards, threats, and events • Determining communication strategies based on the ambulatory care organization’s role in such

statement: The ambulatory care organization establishes and implements a program for the prevention, early detection, suppression, abatement, and safe exit from the facility in response to fires and non-fire emergencies.
elements: The ambulatory care organization establishes and implements a program to ensure that all occupants of the organization are safe from fire, smoke, or other non-fire emergencies.
The program includes the documented assessment of fire risks, including when construction is present in or adjacent to the facility.
The program includes the early detection of fire and smoke, ensuring fire alarms are in place and functioning. High-risk areas, such as a dental laboratory, have fire detection equipment available.

The program includes fire abatement and smoke containment, including in high-risk areas such as dental laboratories. The program includes testing of fire extinguishers and distribution in the ambulatory care organization according to the type of extinguisher required.
The program includes the safe exit from the facility when fire and non-fire emergencies occur, ensuring that egress routes, corridors, and fire escapes are marked and free from obstacles.

statement: The ambulatory care organization regularly tests its fire and smoke safety program, including any devices related to early detection and suppression, and documents the results.
elements: All staff participate in at least one fire and smoke safety program test per year.
Staff can demonstrate how to bring patients to safety.
Fire detection (including fire alarm systems) and abatement equipment and systems are inspected, tested, and maintained according to manufacturers’ recommendations.
Inspection, testing, and maintenance of equipment and systems are documented.

statement: The fire safety program includes limiting smoking by staff and patients to designated non–patient care areas of the facility.
elements: The fire safety program addresses eliminating smoking in the ambulatory care organization, including posting “No Smoking” signs at all entrances and waiting areas.
The program applies to patients, families, visitors, and staff.
The program identifies who may grant patient exceptions for smoking and when those exceptions apply.

statement: The ambulatory care organization establishes and implements a program for inspecting, testing, and maintaining medical equipment.
elements: The ambulatory care organization establishes and implements a medical equipment program, which includes a written inventory of medical equipment.

Medical equipment with special installation requirements; heating, ventilation, or air conditioning requirements; or room modifications is installed following the manufacturer’s recommendations and safety requirements.

Medical equipment is inspected and tested before initial use, and thereafter inspected, tested, and maintained according to age, use, and manufacturers’ recommendations (according to supplied and available manufacturer’s service manual). These activities are documented. The medical equipment is tagged with a periodic preventive maintenance (PPM) label. All defective medical equipment is labeled accordingly.
Qualified individuals inspect, test, and maintain medical equipment.

Medical equipment is discontinued according to a clear policy including lifespan, beyond economic repair, and vendor or government recalls. Equipment is disposed of as per government rules and regulations.
The ambulatory care organization has a system in place for monitoring and acting on medical equipment hazard notices, recalls, problems, failures, and reportable incidents and events.

statement: The ambulatory care organization establishes and implements a program to ensure that utility systems are inspected, tested, maintained, and improved.
elements: Utility systems and components are inspected and tested based on organization-developed criteria.

Utility systems and components are maintained based on organization-developed criteria, which includes performing and recording periodic preventive maintenance (PPM) and corrective maintenance of all electrical and mechanical systems. Maintenance records are maintained.
Utility systems and components are improved when necessary.
The ambulatory care organization inventories and labels its utility systems and components.

statement: The ambulatory care organization has emergency processes to protect facility occupants in the event of power failure or interruption and water contamination.
elements: Electrical power is available during all hours that the ambulatory care organization is operating.
Potable water is available during all hours that the ambulatory care organization is operating.
The ambulatory care organization has identified the areas and services at greatest risk when power fails or is interrupted, or water is contaminated.
The ambulatory care organization seeks to reduce the risks of such events.
The ambulatory care organization plans alternative sources of power and water in emergencies.

statement: The leaders of the ambulatory care organization develop a policy and procedure for safely using various types of compressed gases.
elements: The policy and procedure highlight safe use of cylinder transporters, including measures such as storing cylinders in well-ventilated areas, safely storing butane and other flammable gases outside the laboratory, safely storing oxygen cylinders, and securing cylinders upright against the wall with a chain or inside special containers.
The policy and procedure ensure timely replacement of empty cylinders and an available backup system.
Ambulatory care organizations with piped gas systems follow the regulatory body’s testing and safety requirements.

statement: Designated individuals or authorities regularly monitor water quality.
elements: Quality of potable water is tested at least quarterly or more frequently based on local laws and regulations, conditions of water sources, and previous experience with water quality problems. The testing results are documented.

Quality of nonpotable water is tested at least every six months or more frequently based on local laws and regulations, conditions of water sources, and previous experience with water quality problems. The testing results are documented.
Measures are implemented to prevent and reduce the risks of contamination and growth of bacteria in water, and the effectiveness of the measures is monitored.
Actions are taken and documented when water quality is found to be unsafe.
Dental unit waterlines are treated and tested according to manufacturers’ guidelines, and treatments and testing are documented.

statement: Quality of water used in hemodialysis is tested for chemical, bacterial, and endotoxin contaminants, and processes and practices of hemodialysis services follow professional standards for infection prevention and control.
elements: The ambulatory care organization’s hemodialysis services in the ambulatory care organization follow industry standards and professional guidelines for maintaining water quality and implementing infection prevention and control measures.
Water used in hemodialysis is tested monthly for bacterial growth and endotoxins and tested annually for chemical contaminants. The testing results are documented.
The ambulatory care organization routinely disinfects its hemodialysis water distribution system.
The ambulatory care organization tests its hemodialysis machines for water quality, and documents testing results.

The ambulatory care organization establishes and implements procedures for reprocessing dialyzers, including, as applicable, frequency for reusing/replacing dialyzers and cleaning and testing of dialyzers.

statement: The ambulatory care organization educates and trains all staff members about their roles in providing a safe and effective patient care facility.
elements: For each component of the ambulatory care organization’s facility management program, there is planned education to ensure that all staff members can effectively carry out their responsibilities. All staff includes new hires, locum, and trainees. This education is repeated annually as relevant to their practice.

At least annually, staff are trained on fire and emergency drills and evacuation plans. Staff are certified in completing the emergency drills. Staff are trained in dealing with available hazardous materials and waste disposal.

The education includes all staff and vendors, contract workers, and others, as relevant and identified by the ambulatory care organization for each component of the organization’s facility management program.
Training, testing, and testing results are documented for each staff member in personnel files.

statement: The structure and authority of the ambulatory care organization’s governing entity are described in bylaws, policies and procedures, or similar documents.
elements: The structure of the ambulatory care organization’s governing entity is described in a written document, with those responsible for governance of the organization identified.
The authority of the ambulatory care organization’s governing entity and the delegation of authority are described in bylaws, policies and procedures, or similar documents.
There is an annual evaluation conducted of the governing entity, and the results are documented.
An approved and updated organizational chart identifies the relationship among the center’s governance, leadership, and other directors with names and titles.
The organizational chart is communicated to staff, and the staff can demonstrate their relationship to it.

statement: The operational responsibilities and accountabilities of the governing entity are described in a written document(s).
elements: The governing entity approves and periodically reviews the ambulatory care organization’s mission statement, vision, and values and makes it public.
The governing entity approves the ambulatory care organization’s strategic and operational plans, scope of services, and policies and procedures needed to operate the organization daily.
The governing entity approves the ambulatory care organization’s capital and operating budget(s) as well as the other resources required to manage the organization efficiently.
The governing entity allocates the resources required to meet the organization’s mission.
The governing entity appoints or approves, and annually evaluates, the ambulatory care organization’s chief executive, and the evaluation is documented.

The governing entity annually approves the ambulatory care organization’s program for quality and patient safety and regularly receives and acts on reports of the program, including reports of adverse and sentinel events.

statement: A chief executive is responsible for operating the ambulatory care organization and complying with applicable laws and regulations.
elements: The chief executive has the education and/or experience to carry out their responsibilities and manage the organization’s day-to-day operations, and their responsibilities are defined and written in a job description.
The chief executive and other leaders develop the ambulatory care organization’s mission statement, vision, and values.
The chief executive and other leaders recommend policies to the governing entity.
The chief executive and other ambulatory care organization leaders work together to develop a strategic plan that is guided by the organization’s mission, vision, and values.
The chief executive and other ambulatory care organization leaders build the strategic plan by aligning it to the national strategy and health holding strategy.

The chief executive and other leaders recommend the ambulatory care organization’s strategic plan for a period of three to five years, which is reviewed regularly. The strategic plan does the following: • Includes goals and objectives required to fulfill the organization’s mission • Follows the guidance of the vision as well as input from patients/service users, their families,

statement: Ambulatory care organization leaders are identified and collectively responsible for defining the organization’s mission and creating the programs and policies needed to fulfill the mission.
elements: Ambulatory care organization leaders are identified, and their collective accountabilities are described in written documents.

Ambulatory care organization leaders are collectively responsible for defining and communicating the organization’s mission, vision, and values; creating the organization’s programs and policies; and planning for the care and scope of services that are consistent with the organization’s mission and required to meet patients’ needs. The scope of services should include the following: • The range of coverage for preventive medicine, health promotion, and curative and rehabilitative

group: Leadership for Quality and Patient Safety
statement: Ambulatory care organization leaders plan, develop, and implement a quality and patient safety program and communicate quality and patient safety information to the governing entity.
elements: Ambulatory care organization leaders participate in developing and implementing an annual plan for the quality and patient safety program, which aligns with the organization’s overall strategic plan.
Ambulatory care organization leaders participate in developing and implementing an organizationwide quality and patient safety program.
Ambulatory care organization leaders determine how the quality and patient safety program will be directed and managed on a daily basis and ensure adequate technology and other needed resources.
Ambulatory care organization leaders identify and implement a structure and process for the overall monitoring and coordination of the quality and patient safety program.
Ambulatory care organization leaders report on the quality and patient safety program, including information on adverse and sentinel events, at least every six months to the governing entity.
Ambulatory care organization leaders establish a definition of sentinel event that includes at least the information in Appendix A to this chapter.
Ambulatory care organization leaders report any sentinel event to the relevant authorities—Ministry of Health, Cluster Leadership, Saudi Health Holding Company, and Saudi Patient Safety Center.

Ambulatory care organization leaders complete a credible and thorough comprehensive systematic analysis (for example, root cause analysis) of all sentinel events within a time period specified by organization leadership, and it does not exceed 45 days from the date of the event or when made aware of the event.
The root cause analysis identifies all system and process origins that may have contributed to the event.
Ambulatory care organization leaders consider each identified contributing factor and take corrective actions for improvement to prevent or reduce the risk of adverse events from recurring.
The ambulatory care organization leaders monitor the implemented corrective actions for potential process failures (unintended consequences), effectiveness, and sustainability over time.

group: Leadership for Quality and Patient Safety
statement: The ambulatory care organization’s leaders prioritize which organizationwide clinical and managerial processes and outcomes will be measured and which improvement and patient safety activities will be implemented. (See Appendix B to this chapter.)
elements: Ambulatory care organization leaders use available data to set collective priorities for organizationwide measurement activities.
Ambulatory care organization leaders set collective priorities for compliance with the International Patient Safety Goals.
Ambulatory care organization leaders set priorities for improvement activities and the sequence of implementing improvements.

group: Leadership for Quality and Patient Safety
statement: The individuals leading the ambulatory care organization’s departments and services improve quality and patient safety by participating in organizationwide improvement priorities and monitoring and improving the services specific to the department/service.
elements: Department/service leaders implement quality and patient safety performance measures that relate to the services provided in the department/service, including any contracted services for which they are responsible.
The quality monitoring specific to the department/service is integrated with the organization’s ­quality and patient safety program.
When the target for a performance measure has been reached and sustained for at least four measurement periods, a new measure is selected.
The performance monitoring results are discussed with staff and reported quarterly to the governing entity, together with the developed improvement action plans.
When the department/service measures apply to the performance of health care practitioners, they are included in their performance evaluations.

statement: Ambulatory care organization leaders are accountable for reviewing, selecting, and monitoring clinical and nonclinical contracts.
elements: Ambulatory care organization leaders are accountable for contracts to meet patient and management needs and applicable laws and regulations.
The ambulatory care organization has a written description of the nature and scope of the services to be provided through contractual agreements.
Health care practitioner contracts require credential review comparable to the ambulatory care organization’s review process.

Department/service leaders share accountability for reviewing, selecting (based on evidence-based criteria developed by the relevant department), and monitoring clinical and nonclinical contracts; and the executive leadership ensures that relevant recommendations are met.
