Departmental directors develop annual departmental plans in alignment with the service’s strategic plan.
The leaders ensure the use of evidence-based and best practice information to develop and improve the services.
The leaders plan and budget for the upgrade or maintenance of vehicles, equipment, and other resources.
The leaders meet regularly to review the key performance indicators of services, surveys, audits, and feedback, and use the collected data to improve the service’s operations.

statement: Home care leadership identifies and plans for the type of clinical services required to meet its patients’ needs.
elements: Home care leadership determines and plans with service leaders the care and services to be provided by the organization that are consistent with its mission and patient needs. The scope of services includes the specialty services available, the number of staff in each specialty, the level of professional coverage for the age group served, and working hours. The scope of services is available to the public.
Home care leadership communicates with key stakeholders in its community to facilitate access to care and information about its patient care services.

Home care leadership provides data and communicates information related to safety and quality of its services to stakeholders, which include nursing staff, nonclinical and management staff, patients, families, and external interested parties.
Home care leadership describes and documents its care and services.

statement: Home care leadership ensures effective communication throughout the organization.
elements: Home care leadership ensures that processes are in place for communicating relevant information throughout the organization in a timely manner.
Home care leadership ensures effective communication among clinical and nonclinical departments, services, and individual staff members.
Home care leadership communicates the organization’s vision, mission, goals, policies, and plans to staff.

statement: Home care leadership ensures uniform programs for the recruitment, retention, development, and continuing education of all staff.
elements: The home care organization develops and implements a process for staff recruitment.
The home care organization develops and implements a process for staff retention.
The home care organization develops and implements a process for staff personal development and continuing education.
The planning is collaborative and includes all departments and services in the home care organization.

statement: Home care leadership plans, develops, and implements a quality improvement and patient safety program.
elements: Home care leadership participates in developing and implementing an organizationwide quality improvement and patient safety program.

Home care leadership defines patient safety event and sentinel event and communicates these definitions throughout the organization. At a minimum, the organization’s definition includes those events subject to review as described in Joint Commission International’s Sentinel Event Policy.

Home care leadership selects and implements an organizationwide process to measure, assess data, plan change, and sustain improvements in quality and patient safety, and provides for staff education on this quality improvement process.
Home care leadership determines how the program will be directed and managed on a daily basis and ensures that the program has adequate technology and other resources to be effective.
Home care leadership implements a structure and process for the overall monitoring and coordination of the quality improvement and patient safety program.

statement: Home care leadership regularly communicates quality improvement and patient safety information to the governing entity and home care staff.
elements: Home care leadership reports on the quality improvement and patient safety program at least quarterly to the governing entity.

Home care leadership reports to the governing entity include, at least quarterly, the number and type of sentinel events and root causes, whether the patients and families were informed of the sentinel event, actions taken to improve safety in response to sentinel events, and if the improvements were sustained.
Home care leadership regularly communicates information on the quality improvement and patient safety program to staff, including progress on meeting the International Patient Safety Goals.

statement: The chief executive and home care leadership prioritize which organizationwide processes will be measured, which organizationwide improvement and patient safety activities will be implemented, and how success of these organizationwide efforts will be measured.
elements: The chief executive and home care leadership use available data to set collective priorities for organizationwide measurement and improvement activities and consider potential system improvements.
The chief executive and home care leadership ensure that, when present, clinical research programs are represented in the priorities.
The chief executive and home care leadership set priorities for compliance with the International Patient Safety Goals.
The chief executive and home care leadership assess the impact of organizationwide and service-level improvements on efficiency and resource use.

statement: Home care leadership is accountable for the review, selection, and monitoring of clinical and nonclinical contracts and inspects compliance with contracted services as needed.
elements: The chief executive(s) and home care leadership ensures relevant leaders’ recommendations and approval on contracts and are accountable for contracts to meet patient and management needs, including ensuring that the contracting entity and services provided meet applicable laws and regulations.
The home care organization has a written description of the nature and scope of those services to be provided through contractual agreements.

Service leaders share accountability for the review, selection, and monitoring of clinical and nonclinical contracts by ensuring contracted entities are selected based on evidence-based criteria developed by the relevant departments.

Home care leadership inspects, monitors, and documents compliance of contracted services with the appropriate standards as needed and takes documented corrective actions for improvement when standards are not met.
When contracts are renegotiated or terminated, the home care organization maintains the continuity of patient services.

statement: Home care leadership ensures that contracts and other arrangements are part of the organization’s quality improvement and patient safety program.
elements: All contracts stipulate the quality data to be reported to the home care organization, the reporting frequency and mechanism, and how the organization will respond when quality requirements or expectations are not met.
The home care organization’s quality improvement and patient safety program integrates quality data reported under contracts into its work.
The relevant clinical and managerial leaders participate with the quality improvement and patient safety program in the analysis of quality and safety information from outside contracts.

statement: Home care leadership ensures that licensed health care professionals and independent health care practitioners not employed by the organization have the right credentials and are competent and/or privileged for the services provided to the organization’s patients.
elements: Home care leadership determines those services that will be provided by independent practitioners outside the home care organization.

All diagnostic, consultative, and treatment services provided by independent practitioners outside the home care organization, such as telemedicine, teleradiology, and interpretations of other diagnostics, are credentialed and privileged by the organization to provide such services.
Independent practitioners who provide patient care services but are not employees or members of the clinical staff are credentialed, privileged, and evaluated as required in SQE.9 through SQE.12.
The quality of services by independent practitioners outside the home care organization is monitored as part of the organization’s quality improvement and patient safety program.

When the home care organization uses staff contracts for licensed health care professional staff, the organization ensures that a credential review comparable to the organization’s review process is conducted.

statement: Home care leadership makes decisions related to the purchase or use of resources—human and technical— with an understanding of the quality and safety implications of those decisions.
elements: Home care leadership uses data and information on the quality and safety implications of medical devices, equipment, and supplies choices by ensuring the following: • Contractors and suppliers of medical devices and supplies have a Medical Device Establishment License (MDEL). • All newly purchased medical devices have a Medical Device Marketing Authorization (MDMA) certificate. • Newly introduced consumables are approved based on a formal testing and feedback process from end users.
Home care leadership uses data and information on the quality and safety implications of staffing choices.
Home care leadership uses the recommendations of professional organizations and other authoritative sources in making resource decisions.
Home care leadership provides direction, support, and oversight of information technology resources.
Home care leadership provides direction, support, and oversight of the emergency management program(s).
Home care leadership monitors the results of its decisions and uses the data to evaluate and improve the quality of its resource purchasing and allocation decisions.

statement: Home care leadership seeks and uses data and information on the safety of the supply chain to protect patients and staff from unstable, contaminated, defective, and counterfeit supplies.
elements: Home care leadership outlines the steps in the supply chains for supplies defined as at most risk.
Home care leadership identifies any significant risk points in the steps of the supply chains.
Home care leadership makes resource decisions based on their understanding of the risk points in the supply chains.
The home care organization has a process for performing retrospective tracing of supplies found to be unstable, contaminated, defective, or counterfeit.
The home care organization notifies the manufacturer and/or distributor when unstable, contaminated, defective, or counterfeit supplies are identified.

statement: Medical, nursing, and other leaders of clinical services plan and implement a professional staff structure to support their responsibilities and authority.
elements: Medical, nursing, and other service leaders use a professional staff structure(s) to carry out their responsibilities and authority. The structure is defined in an approved and updated organizational chart that identifies the relationship between the home health care service’s governance, leadership, and other staff, with titles. The staff are aware of the organizational chart and its intent and can demonstrate their relationship to it.
The structure(s) is appropriate to the home care organization’s size and complexity.
The organizational structure(s) and processes support a culture of safety and professional communication.
The organizational structure(s) and processes support clinical planning and policy development.
The organizational structure(s) and processes support oversight of the quality of clinical services.

statement: One or more qualified individuals provide direction for each service provided by the home care organization.
elements: Each service in the home care organization is directed by an individual with the training, education, and experience comparable to the services provided.
Leaders recommend space, medical equipment, staffing, technology, and other resources needed by the service and have a process in place to respond to shortages.
Leaders recommend criteria for selecting the service’s professional staff and choose or recommend individuals who meet those criteria.
Leaders provide orientation and training for all staff on the duties and responsibilities for the service to which they are assigned.

statement: Each service leader identifies, in writing, the services to be provided and integrates or coordinates those services with the services of other departments.
elements: Service leaders have selected and use a uniform format and content for planning documents.
The service documents describe the current and planned services provided by each service or department.
The service documents guide the provision of identified services.
The service documents address the staff knowledge and skills needed to assess and meet patient needs.
There is coordination and/or integration of services within and with other services or departments.

statement: Home care leaders improve quality and patient safety by participating in organizationwide improvement priorities and in monitoring and improving patient care specific to the services provided by the organization.
elements: Home care leaders implement organizationwide quality measures that relate to the organization’s services, including any contracted services for which they are responsible.
Home care leaders implement quality measures to reduce variation and improve processes in the organization’s services, including implementing well-defined, evidence-based clinical measures.
Home care leaders select measures based on the need for improvement, and when improvement has been sustained, select a new measure.
Service quality measurement and improvement activities are integrated into and supported by the organization’s quality management and coordination structure.

statement: Staff performance evaluations use measures selected by the home care leaders that are applicable to evaluating the performance of physicians, nurses, and other professional staff participating in clinical care.
elements: When applicable, assessment of participation in quality activities and the results of measurement activities are included in the ongoing professional practice evaluation of the organization’s physicians.
When applicable, assessment of participation in quality activities and the results of measurement activities are included in the performance evaluation of nursing staff.
When applicable, assessment of participation in quality activities and the results of measurement activities are included in the performance evaluation of other health practitioners.

statement: Home care leaders select and implement clinical practice guidelines, clinical pathways, and/or clinical protocols.
elements: On an annual basis, home care leaders collectively determine at least two organizationwide priority areas on which to focus the use of clinical practice guidelines.

Home care leaders follow the process below in selecting and implementing clinical practice guidelines: • Select from among those applicable to the home care organization’s services and patients (mandatory national guidelines are included in this process, if present). • Evaluate their relevance to identified patient populations. • Adapt, when needed, to the technology, drugs, and other resources of the home care organization or to accepted national professional norms. • Assess their scientific evidence and endorsement by an authoritative source. • Formally approve or adopt by the home care organization. • Implement and measure for consistent use and effectiveness. • Support by staff trained to apply the guidelines or pathways. • Periodically update based on changes in the evidence and evaluation of processes and outcomes.
Home care leaders implement clinical practice guidelines and any associated clinical pathways or clinical protocols for each identified priority area as relevant to the service.
Home care leaders demonstrate how the use of clinical practice guidelines, clinical pathways, and/or clinical protocols has reduced variation in processes and outcomes.

statement: Home care leadership establishes a framework for ethical management that promotes a culture of ethical practices and decision-making to ensure that patient care is provided within business, financial, ethical, and legal norms and protects patients and their rights.
elements: Home care leadership establishes a framework for the organization’s ethical management that promotes a culture of ethical practices and decision-making to protect patients and their rights.
The ethical framework ensures that patient care is provided within business, financial, ethical, and legal norms.
The home care organization ensures nondiscrimination in employment practices and provision of patient care in the context of the country’s cultural and regulatory norms.
Home care leadership examines national and international ethical norms for incorporation when developing the organization’s framework for ethical conduct.

statement: The home care organization’s framework for ethical management addresses operational and business issues, including marketing, admissions, transfer, discharge, and disclosure of ownership and any business and professional conflicts that may not be in patients’ best interests.
elements: The home care organization discloses its ownership and any conflicts of interest.
The home care organization honestly and ethically portrays its services to patients as per applicable laws and regulations, including marketing of staff and services, if performed.
The home care organization accurately bills for services and ensures that financial incentives and payment arrangements do not compromise patient care.

statement: The home care organization’s framework for ethical management addresses ethical issues and decision-making in clinical care.
elements: The home care organization’s framework for ethical management establishes a mechanism by which health care practitioners and other staff may raise patient or non-patient related ethical concerns without fear of retribution, including related to code status and end-of-life policies.
The organizational structure(s) and processes support oversight of professional ethical issues.
Support for identifying and addressing ethical concerns is readily available and includes ethics resources and training for health care practitioners and other staff.
The home care organization resolves any ethical conflicts that arise in a timely, effective way.

statement: Home care leadership creates and supports a culture of safety program throughout the organization.
elements: Home care leadership establishes and supports an organizational culture that promotes accountability and transparency.
Home care leadership develops and documents a set of values and professional code of conduct for all staff and identifies and corrects unacceptable behaviors.
Home care leadership provides education and information (such as literature and advisories) relevant to the organization’s culture of safety to all individuals who work in the organization.
Home care leadership defines how issues related to the organization’s culture of safety are identified and managed.
Home care leadership provides resources to promote and support the organization’s culture of safety.
Home care leadership leads the daily safety huddles.

statement: Home care leadership implements, monitors, and takes action to improve the program for a culture of safety throughout the organization.
elements: Home care leadership provides a simple, accessible, and confidential system for reporting issues relevant to the organization’s culture of safety.
Home care leadership ensures that all reports related to the organization’s culture of safety are investigated in a timely manner.
The home care organization identifies systems issues that lead health care practitioners to engage in unsafe behaviors.
Home care leadership uses measures to evaluate and monitor the organization’s safety culture and implements improvements identified from measurement and evaluation.
Home care leadership implements a process to prevent retribution against individuals who report issues related to the culture of safety.

statement: Human subjects research, when provided in the home care organization, is guided by laws, regulations, and home care leadership.
elements: Home care leadership identifies the official(s) responsible for maintaining the development of and compliance with all human subjects research policies and procedures.
Home care leadership is responsible for protecting patients regardless of the research’s sponsor.
Home care leadership recognizes and establishes mechanisms for complying with all regulatory and professional requirements related to research.
Home care leadership ensures a source of indemnity insurance to adequately compensate patients participating in clinical research who experience an adverse event.

statement: The home care organization informs patients and families about how to gain access to clinical research, investigations, or clinical trials involving human subjects.
elements: As appropriate, patients and families are identified and informed about how to gain access to clinical research, clinical investigations, or clinical trials relevant to their treatment needs.
Patients and families asked to participate are informed about expected benefits.
Patients and families asked to participate are informed about potential discomforts and risks.
Patients and families asked to participate are informed about alternatives that might also help them.
Patients and families asked to participate are informed about the procedures that must be followed.
Patients and families are assured that their refusal to participate or withdraw from participation will not compromise their access to the home care organization’s services.

statement: The home care organization informs patients and families about how patients who choose to participate in clinical research, investigations, or clinical trials are protected.
elements: Patients and families are informed about the research and its potential benefits and risks.
Patients and families are informed about their rights related to withdrawing from participation.
Patients and families are informed about their rights to confidentiality and security of information.
Patients and families are informed about the home care organization’s process for obtaining consent.

statement: Informed consent is obtained before a patient participates in clinical research, investigations, or clinical trials.
elements: Informed consent is obtained when a patient decides to participate in clinical research, clinical investigations, or clinical trials.
The identity of the individual(s) providing the information and obtaining the consent is noted on the informed consent document and stored in the files for the research protocol.
Consent is documented and dated on the informed consent document by signature or record of verbal consent.

statement: The home care organization has a committee or another way to oversee all research involving human subjects.
elements: The home care organization has a committee or other mechanism such as a home care–specific or shared Institutional Review Board (IRB) to oversee and approve all research in the home care organization before starting.
The home care organization develops a clear statement of purpose for the oversight activities.
Oversight activities include a review process.
Oversight activities include a process to weigh relative risks and benefits to subjects.
Oversight activities include processes to provide confidentiality and security of research information.

statement: The home care organization plans and designs information management processes to meet the information needs of those who provide clinical services, the organization’s leaders, and those outside the organization who require data and information from the organization.
elements: The home care organization plans and implements processes to meet the information needs, including patient demographics and medical information, of those who provide clinical services. The processes cover paper format, electronic, or a combination.

The home care organization plans and implements processes to meet the information needs, including patient demographics and medical information, of the organization’s leadership and service leaders. The processes cover paper format, electronic, or a combination.
The process identifies how the information is disseminated from leaders to staff and vice versa.

The home care organization plans and implements processes to meet the information needs and requirements of individuals, services, and agencies outside the organization, defining what information is required by the relevant external authorities, and the frequency of reporting.
The processes implemented are appropriate to the home care organization’s size, complexity of services, availability of trained staff, technical resources, and other resources.

statement: The home care organization maintains the confidentiality, security, privacy, and integrity of data and information through processes to manage and control access.
elements: The home care organization develops and implements processes consistent with laws and regulations to ensure the confidentiality, security, and integrity of data and information.

The home care organization identifies those authorized to access data and information, including those authorized to make entries in the patient medical record, and determines their level of access/ security based on each individual’s role and responsibilities.
The home care organization has a process in place to grant authorized individuals access privileges to data and information in accordance with their level of access.
The home care organization implements processes to ensure that data and information are accessed only by authorized individuals and in accordance with their level of access.

The home care organization implements processes to ensure that only authorized categories of staff or individuals make entries in the patient medical record and in accordance with their level of access.
The home care organization monitors compliance with the processes and takes actions when confidentiality, security, or data integrity are violated or compromised.

statement: The home care organization maintains the confidentiality, security, privacy, and integrity of data and information through processes that protect against loss, theft, damage, and destruction.
elements: The home care organization conducts and documents an annual information security risk assessment throughout the organization, and data security risks are identified and prioritized from the risk assessment.
Data and information are stored in a manner that protects against loss, theft, damage, and destruction.
The home care organization implements data security best practices to protect and secure all types of data and information.
The home care organization identifies goals, implements improvements to address data security risks, and monitors improvement data to ensure that risks are reduced or eliminated.

statement: The home care organization determines the retention time of patient medical records, data, and other information.
elements: The home care organization determines the retention time of patient medical records and other data and information and complies with laws and regulations.
The retention process provides expected confidentiality and security.
Patient medical records, data, and other information are destroyed or deleted in a manner that does not compromise confidentiality and security.

statement: The home care organization uses standardized diagnosis and procedure codes and ensures the uniform use of approved symbols and abbreviations across the organization.
elements: The home care organization uses standardized diagnosis codes and procedure codes, including international classification of diseases (ICD) or current procedural terminology (CPT) consistent with the requirements of relevant authorities.
The home care organization implements the uniform use of approved symbols and identifies those not to be used.
If the home care organization allows abbreviations, it uniformly uses approved abbreviations, and each abbreviation has only one meaning.
If the home care organization allows abbreviations, it develops and/or adopts a do-not-use list of abbreviations.
Abbreviations are not used on informed consent and patient rights documents, discharge instructions, and discharge summaries.
The home care organization monitors the uniform use of codes, symbols, and abbreviations throughout the organization and takes actions to improve processes when needed.

statement: The data and information needs of those in and outside the home care organization are met on a timely basis in a format that meets user expectations and with the desired frequency.
elements: Data and information dissemination meets the needs of individuals and organizations in and outside the home care organization, including patients, health care practitioners, home care leadership, health care services and organizations, and regulatory agencies.

When individuals or organizations require data and information for patient care, the home care organization has processes to ensure that they are received in a timely manner that supports continuity of care and patient safety.
Individuals and organizations in and outside the home care organization receive data and information in a format that facilitates their intended use.
Staff providing patient care have access to the data and information needed to carry out their job responsibilities and provide patient care safely and effectively.

statement: Clinical staff, decision makers, and other staff are educated and trained on information systems, information security, and the principles of information use and management.
elements: Clinical staff, decision makers, and others are provided education and training on information systems, information security, and the principles of information use and management, as appropriate to their role and responsibilities.

Staff who use an electronic medical record system receive education, ongoing training, and assessment to ensure that they can effectively and efficiently use the system to carry out their job responsibilities.
Clinical and managerial data and information are integrated as needed to support decision-making.

statement: Documents, including policies, procedures, and programs, are managed in a consistent and uniform manner.
elements: The home care organization has a written guidance document that defines the requirements for developing and maintaining policies, procedures, and programs, including at least the following: • Development, review, and approval of all policies and procedures by an authorized person or

statement: The home care organization fully implements the policies, procedures, plans, and other documents that guide consistent and uniform clinical and nonclinical processes and practices.
elements: Required policies, procedures, and plans are available and communicated, and staff understand how to access those documents relevant to their responsibilities.
Staff are trained and understand those documents relevant to their responsibilities.
The requirements of the policies, procedures, and plans are fully implemented and evident in the actions of individual staff members.
The implementation of policies, procedures, and plans is monitored, and the information supports full implementation.

statement: The home care organization initiates and maintains a standardized, accurate medical record for every patient assessed or treated and determines the record’s content, format, and location of entries.
elements: A medical record with at least two identifiers unique to the patient is initiated for every patient assessed or treated by the home care organization.
The home care organization standardizes and determines the specific content, format, and location of entries for patient medical records.

The home care organization establishes and implements guidelines on properly using copy-and-paste, auto-fill, auto-correct, and templates and provides education and training on the guidelines to all staff who document in the electronic medical record.
The home care organization has a process to monitor compliance with the guidelines on properly using copy-and-paste, auto-fill, auto-correct, and templates and implements corrective action as needed.
The home care organization establishes and implements processes and guidelines to facilitate accurate and complete documentation in patient medical records.

statement: The medical record contains sufficient information to identify the patient, support the diagnosis, justify the treatment, and document the course and results of treatment.
elements: Patient medical records contain adequate information to identify the patient. The medical records contain the required patient demographics, including national identification number, contact information, emergency contacts, and insurance history.
Patient medical records contain adequate information to support the diagnosis and promote continuity of care.

Patient medical records contain adequate medical information to justify and document the course and results of the patient’s care, treatment, and services, including history, physical examination, plan of care, investigations, consultations, observations, consents, procedure/surgery reports, medications, allergies, and prior adverse reactions.
There is a uniform entry of data in medical records, whereby orders are written separately from assessments, care plans, and progress notes.

statement: Every patient medical record entry identifies its author and when the entry was made in the record.
elements: The author of each entry in the patient medical record can be identified.
The date of each entry in the patient medical record can be identified.
The time of each entry in the patient medical record can be identified.

All entries in the patient’s medical record are legible, and there is a process that addresses how entries in the patient medical record are corrected or overwritten, whereby entries are not deleted or erased. Instead, a single line is passed through the error text, dated, timed, and signed by the author, or electronically the system allows for amendment tracing.

When scribes assist with documentation in the patient medical record, they sign, date, and time their entries, and there is a process for the physician/health care practitioner to review and authenticate the scribes’ entries.

statement: As part of its performance improvement activities, the home care organization regularly assesses patient record content.
elements: A representative sample of medical records that includes active and discharged medical records is reviewed at least quarterly or more frequently as determined by laws and regulations.
The review is conducted by physicians, nurses, and others authorized to make entries in patient medical records or to manage patient medical records.
The review focuses on the timeliness, accuracy, completeness, and legibility of the medical records.
Medical record content required by laws or regulations is included in the review process.
The results of the review process are incorporated into the home care organization’s quality oversight mechanism.

statement: The home care organization has a process for completing and storing patient medical records.
elements: The home care organization has a dedicated, secure storage method/area for all medical records.
The home care organization develops a policy and procedure for its clinical documentation improvement program.
Returned files are regularly checked to ensure completion. The check includes but is not limited to demographics, medical information, and authentication.
Incomplete files are separated from completed ones in the storage area. They are completed in a time frame defined by the home care organization.
The home care organization keeps a record of the percentage of incomplete records over time and uses this information to improve staff compliance with record completion.

statement: Home care leadership identifies a qualified individual to oversee the home care organization’s health information technology systems and processes.
elements: Home care leadership provides direction, support, and resources for health information technology in the organization.

Home care leadership identifies a qualified individual to oversee health information technology systems in the organization with responsibility for at least the following: • Recommending space, equipment, technology, and other resources to home care leadership to

statement: When mobile devices are used for texting, e-mailing, or other communication of patient data and information, the home care organization implements processes to ensure quality of patient care and maintain security and confidentiality of patient information.
elements: When the home care organization allows patient data and information to be transmitted through text messaging, the organization ensures that the process is through a secure messaging platform and complies with the following: • User authentication via secure, encrypted sign-on process(es), which are password protected and

statement: The home care organization develops, maintains, and tests a program for response to planned and unplanned downtime of data systems.
elements: The home care organization develops, maintains, and tests at least annually a program for response to planned and unplanned downtime of data systems.
The home care organization identifies the probable impact of planned and unplanned downtime of data systems on all aspects of care and services.

The program includes continuity strategies for ongoing safe, high-quality patient care and services, including services from outside vendors, during planned and unplanned downtime of data systems. This includes manual procedures, if any.
The program identifies internal and, when applicable, external communication strategies for planned and unplanned downtime.

The home care organization identifies and implements downtime recovery tactics and ongoing data backup processes to recover and maintain data and ensure data integrity and confidentiality and security of patient information.
Staff are trained in the strategies and tactics for planned and unplanned downtime of data systems, including manual procedures, if any.

statement: The home care organization leaders ensure the integrity and security of telemedicine, teleradiology, and other diagnostic remote contracted services.
elements: Telemedicine, teleradiology, and other diagnostic remote contracted services are registered and comply with national health rules and regulations.
The leaders ensure the credentialing and privileging of all health care providers of diagnostic remote services before starting the service.
The leaders ensure the security and confidentiality of patient information exposed because of the telecommunication process.
Staff are trained in using medical equipment that involves remote monitoring of patients.

statement: One or more individuals oversee all infection prevention and control activities. This individual(s) is qualified in infection prevention and control practices through education, training, experience, certification, and/or clinical authority.
elements: One or more individuals oversee the infection prevention and control program and ensure that the program complies with local and national laws and regulations.
The individual(s) is qualified for the home care organization’s size, complexity of activities, and level of risks, as well as the program’s scope.
The individual(s) fulfills program oversight responsibilities on a full-time or part-time basis and as described in a job description.
This individual(s) coordinates with home care leadership regarding priorities, resources, and quality improvement opportunities related to the infection prevention and control program.
The home care organization reports infection prevention and control program results to public health agencies as required.
The home care organization takes appropriate action on reports from relevant public health agencies.

statement: There is a designated coordination mechanism for all infection prevention and control activities that involves physicians, nurses, and others based on the home care organization’s size and complexity.
elements: The designated mechanism coordinates the infection prevention and control program to reduce the risk of health care–associated infections and involves infection prevention and control professionals.
Infection prevention and control activities involve physicians, nurses, and/or others based on the home care organization’s size and complexity.
The infection prevention and control program includes all areas of the home care organization and is documented in a manual available to all staff.

statement: Home care leadership provides resources to support the infection prevention and control program.
elements: The infection prevention and control program is staffed according to the home care organization’s size, complexity of activities, and level of risks, as well as the program’s scope.
Home care leadership approves and assigns staff for the infection prevention and control program.
Home care leadership approves and allocates resources for the infection prevention and control program.
Information management systems support the infection prevention and control program.

statement: The home care organization designs and implements a comprehensive infection prevention and control program that identifies the procedures and processes associated with infection risk and implements strategies to reduce infection risk.
elements: The infection prevention and control program is comprehensive and crosses all levels of the home care organization to reduce the risk of health care–associated infections.

The leaders develop and implement infection control policies and procedures targeting the most important infection risk processes including the following: • Insertion and removal of catheters and lines • Wound dressing • Universal precautions for handling human blood and body fluids • Cleaning, decontamination, and disinfection in the patient care area during home visits with a

statement: The home care organization uses a risk-based, data-driven approach in establishing the focus of the health care–associated infection prevention and control program.
elements: The home care organization establishes the focus of the program by collecting and tracking the following data: • Respiratory tract, including procedures and equipment associated with intubation, mechanical

statement: The home care organization identifies areas at high risk for infections by conducting a risk assessment, develops interventions to address these risks, and monitors the effectiveness.
elements: The home care organization completes and documents a risk assessment, at least annually, to identify and prioritize areas at high risk for infections.
The home care organization identifies and implements interventions to address infection risks identified through the risk assessment.
The home care organization evaluates the effectiveness of the interventions and makes appropriate changes to the infection prevention and control program as needed.
The home care organization performs ongoing data monitoring to ensure that risks are reduced or eliminated.

statement: The home care organization develops and implements a process for preparing, handling, storing, and distributing parenteral and enteral tube nutrition therapy.
elements: The home care organization develops and implements a process to guide the preparation, handling, storage, and distribution of parenteral and enteral tube nutrition therapy.
The process guides the use of parenteral and enteral tube nutrition therapy in the home.
Patients, families, and caregivers are educated about the process.

statement: The home care organization develops, implements, and evaluates an emergency preparedness program to respond to global communicable diseases.
elements: Home care leaders, along with the individual(s) responsible for the infection prevention and control program, develop and implement an emergency preparedness program to respond to global communicable diseases that includes at least the following: • Communicating with organizations participating in worldwide surveillance activities (See also

statement: Gloves, masks, eye protection, other protective equipment, soap, and disinfectants are available and used correctly when required.
elements: The home care organization identifies situations in which personal protective equipment is required and ensures its accessibility and availability at any site of care where needed.
Staff are trained and correctly use personal protective equipment in each identified situation including gloves, gowns, face masks, and protective eyewear.
Gowns, masks, eyewear or face shields, and other protective equipment are worn during patient visits as required according to the infection control policy and procedures.
The home care organization implements surface disinfecting procedures for areas and situations identified as at risk for infection transmission.

The home health care service has an established and implemented policy on hand hygiene. Liquid soap, disinfectants, and towels or other means of drying are located in areas where handwashing and hand-disinfecting procedures are required.

Patients, families, and caregivers are educated on when they are required to disinfect their hands and how to correctly use personal protective equipment, such as gloves, when in contact with blood/body fluids.

statement: The infection prevention and control program is integrated with the home care organization’s overall program for quality improvement and patient safety, using measures epidemiologically important to the organization.
elements: The home care organization integrates infection prevention and control activities into the quality improvement and patient safety program.
The home care organization collects and analyzes data for its infection prevention and control activities, and the data includes epidemiologically important infections.
The home care organization uses monitoring data to evaluate and support improvements to its infection prevention and control program at least annually.
Monitoring data includes benchmarking infection rates.
The infection prevention and control program documents monitoring data and provides quarterly data analysis reports to leadership.

statement: The home care organization educates staff, physicians, patients, family, and other caregivers on infection prevention and control practices when indicated by their involvement in care.
elements: The home care organization educates all staff and other professionals on infection prevention and control when they begin work in the organization.

The home care organization provides ongoing education and training at least annually to all staff related to its infection prevention and control program and emerging trends in infection prevention and control.
The home care organization educates patients and families about infection prevention and control.
The home care organization communicates findings and trends from quality improvement activities to all staff and includes those findings and trends as part of staff education.

statement: The home health care service supports its patients and, when appropriate, families in the safe disposal of medical waste.
elements: When required, the home health care service provides its patients with sharps disposal containers and yellow bags for proper disposal of medical waste.
The home health care service educates its patients and staff on correctly disposing of wastes, including use of sharps disposal containers and yellow bags.
The home health care service collects the sharps disposal containers and yellow bags from its patients for final disposal.
Waste disposal is done effectively in the facility or through an authorized contractor.

statement: The home health care service develops policies and procedures that address employees’ screening, immunization, and post-exposure management.
elements: Employees’ screening, immunization, and post-exposure management are consistent with the laws and regulations and recommendations of professional organizations.
All employees have baseline screening for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, HIV, and tuberculosis.
The immune status of newly hired staff against hepatitis B is determined by serological testing, and appropriate vaccine(s) is administered to those who are non-immune.

The response to hepatitis B vaccination is monitored in vaccinated employees for four weeks after completing the vaccine series. Non-responders to the hepatitis B vaccine are offered at least a second series of the vaccine.

statement: A qualified individual(s) guides the implementation of the home care organization’s program for quality improvement and patient safety and manages the activities to ensure that the program is effective.
elements: An individual(s) experienced in quality improvement methods and processes is selected to guide the implementation of the home care organization’s quality improvement and patient safety program.

The individual(s) with oversight for the quality improvement and patient safety program selects and supports qualified staff for the program and supports those staff with quality improvement and patient safety responsibilities throughout the home care organization.

The quality improvement and patient safety program provides support and coordination to service leaders for like measures across the home care organization and for the organization’s priorities for improvement.
The quality improvement and patient safety program implements a training program for all staff that is consistent with staff’s roles in the quality improvement and patient safety program.
The quality improvement and patient safety program is responsible for regularly communicating quality issues to all staff.

statement: Quality improvement and patient safety program staff support the measure selection process throughout the home care organization and coordinate and integrate measurement activities throughout the organization.
elements: The quality improvement and patient safety program supports the selection of measures, including patient and staff surveys, throughout the home care organization at the organizationwide level and at the service level to measure performance and improve both clinical and managerial areas. The measures selection process is based on the home health care service’s essential processes and priorities.
The quality improvement and patient safety program coordinates and integrates measurement activities throughout the home care organization.
Each indicator has an operational definition, defined numerator and denominator, data collection method and frequency, a mathematical expression such as ratio or percentage, and a desirable target.
The quality improvement and patient safety program provides for the integration of event reporting systems, safety culture measures, and others to facilitate integrated solutions and improvements.
The quality improvement and patient safety program tracks the progress on the planned collection of measure data for the priorities selected.

statement: Home care leadership builds a culture and environment that support evidence-based care, using current scientific knowledge and information to support patient care, health professional education, clinical research, and management.
elements: Home care leadership builds a culture and environment that support implementation of evidence- based care.
Current scientific knowledge and information support patient care.
Current scientific knowledge and information support clinical education.
Current scientific knowledge and information support research when applicable.
Current professional knowledge and information support management.
Information is provided in a time frame that meets user expectations.

statement: The quality improvement and patient safety program aggregates and analyzes data to support patient care, home care management, and the quality management program and participation in external databases.
elements: The quality improvement and patient safety program has a process to aggregate data.

Aggregate data and information support patient care, home care organization management, professional practice review, and overall quality improvement and patient safety program and are readily accessible on a timely basis to those responsible for and involved in service(s) delivery. Aggregate data and information are used for making improvements and supporting leadership decision-making.
Aggregate data and information are provided to agencies outside the home care organization when required by laws or regulations.
There is a process to contribute to and learn from external databases or use internal benchmarking for comparison purposes.
Security and confidentiality are maintained when contributing to or using external databases.

statement: Individuals with appropriate experience, knowledge, and skills systematically aggregate and analyze data in the home care organization.
elements: Data are aggregated, analyzed, and transformed into useful information to identify opportunities for improvement.
Individuals with appropriate clinical or managerial experience, knowledge, and skills participate in the process.
Statistical tools and techniques are used in the analysis process when suitable.
The frequency of data analysis is appropriate to the process or outcome being studied.

Analysis results are reported to those accountable for taking action, discussed with staff, used in their evaluation, and reported quarterly to the governing body, together with action plans taken for improvement.
Data analysis supports comparisons internally over time, including comparisons with databases of like organizations (when available), best practices, and objective scientific professional sources.

statement: The home care organization uses an internal process to validate data.
elements: The quality improvement and patient safety program uses data validation in the improvement process selected by leadership.

Data is validated when any of the following conditions are met: • A new measure is implemented (in particular, those clinical measures intended to help an organization evaluate and improve an important clinical process or outcome). • Data will be made public on the organization’s website or in other ways. • An existing measure has changed, such as changes in the data collection tools, data abstraction process, or abstractor. • The data from an existing measure has changed in an unexplainable way. • The data source has changed, such as when part of the patient record has been turned into an electronic format and thus the data source is now both electronic and paper. • The subject of data collection has changed, such as changes in average age of patients, comorbidities, research protocol alterations, new practice guidelines implemented, or new technologies and treatment methodologies introduced.
Staff with appropriate knowledge and skills use an evidence-based methodology for data validation.
Home care leadership assumes accountability for the validity of the quality and outcome data made public.

statement: Data is analyzed when there are undesirable trends and variation.
elements: The home care organization develops and implements defined data gathering processes to ensure accurate data gathering, analysis, and reporting.
Intense analysis of data takes place when there are adverse levels, patterns, or trends.

Data is gathered and analyzed on the following, as applicable: • All confirmed transfusion reactions, consistent with the services provided • All serious adverse drug events, consistent with the services provided • All significant medication errors, consistent with the services provided • Adverse events or patterns of adverse events during moderate or deep sedation, consistent with

statement: The home care organization achieves and sustains improvement in quality and safety.
elements: Improvements in quality and patient safety are planned, tested, and implemented.
Data is available to demonstrate that improvements are effective and sustained.
The home care organization makes policy changes necessary to plan, carry out, and sustain improvement.
The home health care service implements at least one improvement project per year, using an evidence-based quality improvement method such as FOCUS PDCA.

statement: The home care organization has an ongoing risk management program to identify and proactively reduce unanticipated adverse events and other safety risks to patients and staff.
elements: The home health care service addresses clinical, managerial, and financial risks.
The risk management program includes reporting of incidents, variances, and claims as its essential reactive arm.
The organization’s risk management program includes the following: • Risk identification • Risk prioritization using an evidence-based process based on severity, frequency, and likelihood

statement: The home health care service implements an incident reporting policy.
elements: The policy outlines the types of incidents to be reported, both internally and to relevant regulatory authorities, as well as the time frame and mechanism for reporting.
Sentinel events and major incidents are reported and investigated, and the findings are used to prevent recurrence.
Incidents involving patients are documented in the medical record, and the physician informs the patient and family of any investigation results.
The home health care service compiles an incident report according to type and severity. The service regularly distributes an action plan to prevent their recurrence to staff and the governing body.

statement: Home care leaders define the desired education, skills, knowledge, and other requirements of all staff members.
elements: The home care organization’s mission, volume, and mix of patients, services, and medical equipment are used in planning staff requirements.
The desired education, skills, and knowledge are defined for staff.
Applicable laws and regulations are incorporated into the planning.

statement: Each staff member’s responsibilities are defined in a current job description.
elements: All categories of staff have clearly written job descriptions.

Job descriptions define roles, responsibilities, and required knowledge, skills, and attitude, based on staff credential evaluation. Job descriptions are discussed with and signed by the staff upon hiring and kept in the personnel file. The following individuals, when present in the home care organization, have job descriptions consistent with their activities and responsibilities: • The individual serves in primarily a managerial role, such as a service manager, or in dual clinical and managerial roles, with the managerial responsibilities identified in a job description. (See also

statement: Home care leaders develop and implement processes for recruiting, evaluating, and appointing staff as well as other related procedures identified by the home care organization.
elements: The home care organization establishes and implements a process to recruit staff.
The home care organization establishes and implements a process to evaluate the qualifications of new staff.
The home care organization establishes and implements a process to appoint individuals to the staff.
The home care organization establishes and implements a process that is uniform across the organization for similar types of staff.

statement: The home care organization uses a defined process to ensure that clinical staff knowledge and skills are consistent with patient needs.
elements: The home care organization uses a defined process to match clinical staff knowledge, skills, and competency with patient needs. This includes credentialing and re-credentialing all clinical staff; verifying licensing, education, training, and experience with credentials confirmed from the source or a third party; and documenting all in the personnel file. The process applies to all clinical staff licensed to provide patient care on a full-time, part-time, or visiting basis and ensures that registration and licensing follow the laws and regulations of Saudi Arabia.

The home care organization has a policy to ensure health care staff are competent in specific procedures and operating equipment. The policy includes a list of procedures requiring competency assessment for each staff category, with assessments conducted upon hiring and annually. It addresses the training and competency testing of staff using specialized equipment to ensure safe operation, allowing only properly trained and competent staff to use specialized equipment and medical devices.
New clinical staff members are evaluated before or at the time they begin their work responsibilities.
The service to which the individual is assigned conducts the evaluation.
The home care organization defines the frequency of ongoing clinical staff evaluation.
There is at least one documented evaluation of each clinical staff member working under a job description each year or more frequently as defined by the home care organization.

statement: The home care organization uses a defined process to ensure that nonclinical staff knowledge and skills are consistent with organizational needs and the requirements of the position.
elements: The home care organization uses a defined process to match nonclinical staff knowledge and skills with the requirements of the position.
New nonclinical staff are evaluated before or at the time they begin their work responsibilities.
The department or service to which the individual is assigned conducts the evaluation.
The home care organization defines the frequency of ongoing nonclinical staff evaluation.
There is at least one documented evaluation of nonclinical staff members each year or more frequently as defined by the home care organization.

statement: There is documented personnel information for each staff member.
elements: Personnel files for each staff member are standardized, current, maintained, and kept confidential according to home care organization policy.
Personnel files contain the staff member’s qualifications and work history.
Personnel files contain the staff member’s job description when applicable.
Personnel files contain the staff member’s record of orientation to the home care organization, their specific role, and the in-service education they attended.
Personnel files contain the results of performance reviews.
Personnel files contain required health information.

statement: A staffing strategy for the home care organization, developed by the home care leaders, identifies the number, types, and desired qualifications of staff.
elements: The home care organization’s service leaders develop a written strategy for staffing the organization in a manner that complies with local laws and regulations and ensures services meet the needs of safe patient care.
The number, types, and desired qualifications of staff are identified in the strategy using a recognized staffing method, defining the required credentials and roles of staff.
The strategy addresses the assignment and reassignment of staff and ensures appropriately qualified staff are recruited and assigned.
The effectiveness of the staffing strategy is monitored on an ongoing basis, and deficiencies are identified with improvement actions taken accordingly.
The strategy is revised and updated when necessary, including through an annual review.

statement: All clinical and nonclinical staff members are oriented to the home care organization, to the service to which they are assigned, and to their specific job responsibilities at appointment to the staff.
elements: All new clinical and nonclinical staff members attend a mandatory orientation program covering the home care organization; its mission, vision, values, and organizational structure; patient and family rights; safety and security; infection prevention and control; and quality, patient safety, and risk management programs. Staff are also oriented to their job responsibilities, specific assignments, and job description through a role-specific orientation.
Contract workers are oriented to the home care organization, their job responsibilities, and any specific assignments.
Students/trainees and volunteers are oriented to the home care organization and their assigned responsibilities.

statement: Each staff member receives ongoing in-service and other education and training to maintain or advance their skills and knowledge.
elements: The home care organization uses various sources of data and information, including the results of quality and safety measurement activities, to identify staff education needs.
The home care organization has a scheduled education and training program for all categories of staff based on these data and information.

The home care organization provides ongoing in-service education and training for all categories of staff. Leaders encourage and compensate staff to attend educational and training activities relevant to the home care organization’s scope of services and in line with labor law.
The education is relevant to each staff member’s ability to meet patient needs and/or continuing education requirements.
The home care organization provides adequate time and facilities for all staff to participate in relevant education and training opportunities.

statement: Staff members who provide patient care and other staff identified by the home care organization are trained and can demonstrate competence in resuscitative techniques.
elements: All staff members who provide patient care, including physicians, and other staff identified by the home care organization are trained in at least basic life support.
All staff members who provide direct patient care maintain a valid certificate on basic life support.
The home care organization identifies other staff to be trained in advanced life support as appropriate to the scope of service.

The desired level of training for each individual is repeated based on the requirements and/or time frames established by a recognized training program, or every two years if a recognized training program is not used.

statement: The home care organization provides a staff health and safety program that addresses staff physical and mental health and safe working conditions.
elements: The home care organization provides a staff health and safety program that is consistent with relevant laws and regulations; protects staff from occupational health and safety hazards and workplace violence; and responds to urgent and nonurgent staff needs through direct treatment and referral.

The home care organization implements a comprehensive staff health and safety program that includes the following: • Initial employment health screening • Measures to control harmful occupational exposures, such as toxic drugs, harmful noise levels,

statement: The home care organization identifies staff at risk for exposure to and possible transmission of vaccine- preventable diseases and implements a staff vaccination and immunization program.
elements: The home care organization identifies epidemiologically significant infections, as well as staff at high risk for exposure to and transmission of infections.

The home care organization develops and implements a staff vaccination and immunization program with policies and procedures addressing employee screening, immunization, and post-exposure management, consistent with laws, regulations, and recommendations of professional organizations.

All employees undergo baseline screening for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), and tuberculosis. The immune status of newly hired staff against hepatitis B is determined through serological testing, and appropriate vaccines are administered to those who are not immune. For vaccinated employees, the response to the hepatitis B vaccination is monitored four weeks after completing the vaccine series. Non-responders are offered at least a second series of the vaccine.
The home care organization evaluates the risks associated with unvaccinated staff and identifies strategies for reducing the patient’s risk of exposure to infectious diseases from unvaccinated staff.
The infection prevention and control program guides the evaluation, counseling, and follow-up of staff exposed to infectious diseases.

statement: The home care organization has an effective process for gathering the credentials of the home care organization’s medical staff permitted to provide patient care without supervision.
elements: The home care organization has an ongoing, uniform process to manage the credentials of medical staff members.
Medical staff members permitted by laws, regulations, and the home care organization to provide patient care without supervision are identified.

Education, licensure/registration, and other credentials required by laws or regulations are copied by the home care organization and maintained for each medical staff member in their personnel file or a separate credential file.
All credentials required by home care organization policy are copied by the organization and maintained for each medical staff member in their personnel file or a separate credential file.

statement: Medical staff members’ education, licensure/registration, and other credentials required by laws or regulations and the home care organization are verified and kept current.
elements: Education, licensure/registration, and other credentials required by laws or regulations or issued by recognized education or professional entities as the basis for clinical privileges are verified from the original source that issued the credential.
Additional credentials required by home care organization policy are verified from the source that issued the credential when required by organization policy.

When third-party verification is used, the home care organization verifies that the third party (for example, a government agency) implements the verification process as described in policy or regulations.

statement: There is a uniform, transparent decision process for the initial appointment of medical staff members.
elements: Medical staff are appointed according to home care organization policy and are consistent with the organization’s patient population, mission, and services to meet patient needs.

Appointments are not made until at least licensure/registration has been verified from the primary source, and the medical staff member then provides patient care services under supervision until all credentials required by laws and regulations have been verified from the original source, up to a maximum of 90 days.
The method of supervision, frequency of supervision, and accountable supervisors are documented in the individual’s credential file.

statement: The home care organization has a standardized, objective, evidence-based procedure to authorize all its own medical staff members to admit and treat patients and provide other clinical services consistent with their qualifications.
elements: The home care organization’s privilege delineation process meets the following criteria: • Is standardized, objective, and evidence based • Is documented in home care organization policies • Determines clinical privileges based on the staff’s current competence, privileging policy, and

statement: The home care organization uses an ongoing standardized process to evaluate the quality and safety of the patient services provided by each medical staff member.
elements: All medical staff are included in an ongoing professional practice evaluation process as defined by home care organization policy and standardized evaluation at the service level.

The ongoing professional practice evaluation process identifies areas of achievement and potential improvement related to the behaviors, professional growth, and clinical results of the medical staff member, and the results are reviewed with objective and evidence-based information as available. These results are compared to other medical staff members of the same service.

The data and information from the monitoring are reviewed at least every 12 months by the individual’s service head, senior medical manager, or medical staff body, and the results, conclusions, and any actions taken are documented in the medical staff member’s credential file and other relevant files.

When the findings affect the appointment or privileges of the medical staff member, there is a process to act on the findings, and such “for cause” actions are documented in the practitioner’s file and reflected in the list of clinical privileges. Notification is sent to those sites in which the practitioner provides services.

statement: At least every three years, the home care organization determines, from the ongoing professional practice evaluation of each medical staff member, if medical staff membership and clinical privileges are to continue with or without modification.
elements: Based on the ongoing professional practice evaluation of the medical staff member, the home care organization determines, at least every two years and earlier if needed, if medical staff membership and clinical privileges are to continue with or without modification.
There is evidence in the file of each medical staff member that all credentials that require periodic renewal, payment of a registration fee, or other action by the medical staff member are current.

Credentials obtained subsequent to initial appointment are evident in the medical staff member’s file and have been verified from the primary source prior to use in modifying or adding to clinical privileges.
The renewal decision is documented in the medical staff member’s credential file and includes identification of the reviewer and any special conditions identified during the review.

statement: The home care organization has a uniform process to gather, verify, and evaluate the nursing staff’s credentials (license, education, training, and experience).
elements: The home care organization has a standardized procedure to gather and document the education, certifications, and experience of each nursing staff member.
Education, training, and certifications are verified from the original source and documented.
Licensure is verified from the original source and documented.
There is a record maintained of the credentials of every nursing staff member.
The home care organization has a process to ensure that the credentials of contract nurses are valid and complete prior to assignment.

statement: The home care organization has a standardized procedure to identify job responsibilities and make clinical work assignments based on the nursing staff member’s credentials and any regulatory requirements.
elements: Licensure, education, training, and experience of a nursing staff member are used to make clinical work assignments.
The process considers relevant laws and regulations.
The process supports nurse staffing plans.

statement: The home care organization has a standardized procedure for nursing staff participation in the organization’s quality improvement activities, including evaluating individual performance when indicated.
elements: Nursing staff participate in the home care organization’s quality improvement activities.
The performance of individual nursing staff members is reviewed when indicated by the findings of quality improvement activities.
Appropriate information from the review process is documented in the nurse’s personnel file or a separate credential file.

statement: The home care organization has a standardized procedure to gather, verify, and evaluate other health care practitioners’ credentials (license, education, training, and experience).
elements: The home care organization has a standardized process to gather and document each health care practitioner’s education, certifications, and experience.
Education, training, and certifications are verified from the original source and documented.
Licensure is verified from the original source and documented.
There is a record maintained on other health care practitioners that contains copies of any required license, certification, or registration.

statement: The home care organization has a uniform process to identify job responsibilities and make clinical work assignments based on other health care practitioners’ credentials and any regulatory requirements.
elements: Licensure, education, training, and experience of other health care practitioners are used to make clinical work assignments.
The process considers relevant laws and regulations.
The process supports the staffing process for other health care practitioners.

statement: The home care organization has a uniform process for other health care practitioners’ participation in the home care organization’s quality improvement activities.
elements: Other health care practitioners participate in the home care organization’s quality improvement activities.
The performance of other health care practitioners is reviewed when indicated by the findings of quality improvement activities.
Appropriate information from the review process is documented in the health practitioner’s file.

statement: The home care organization leaders develop an effective process to evaluate staff performance at least annually.
elements: Performance evaluations are based on objective criteria assessing staff knowledge, skills, and attitude.
Evaluations are conducted at the end of the initial probationary period and at least annually thereafter.
Evaluations include personal goals for staff to achieve over the next year.
Staff participates in their evaluation by receiving feedback, providing comments, and signing the evaluation.
Information on staff credentials, privileges, competencies, orientation, training, education, and evaluations is securely maintained in an updated personnel file.

statement: Residents who may be admitted to the long-term care organization are screened to identify if their health care needs match the organization’s mission and resources. P
elements: Based on the results of screening, residents are accepted for treatment if the resident’s needs match the long-term care organization’s mission and resources.

If the resident’s needs do not match the long-term care organization’s mission and resources, the organization will transfer, refer, or assist the resident in identifying and/or obtaining appropriate sources of care.
There is a process to provide the results of diagnostic tests to those responsible for determining if the resident is to be admitted, transferred, or referred.
The long-term care organization identifies situations when specific screening tests or evaluations are required prior to admission.

The long-term care organization transfers, refers, or assists the resident or family in identifying and/ or obtaining appropriate sources of care if their needs do not match the long-term care organization mission, scope of care, or available resources.
Assessments and treatments completed prior to transfer are documented in a record maintained by the transferring long-term care organization.
